5 - Mentioned by Ibn Rajab al-Ḥanbalī in his book Jāmiʿ al-ʿUlūm wa'l-Ḥikam (p. 27), from the supplication of Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who used to say: "O Allah, I seek Your forgiveness for what I repented to You of and then returned to, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I made binding upon myself for You and did not fulfill for You, and I seek Your forgiveness for what I claimed I intended for Your sake while my heart was mixed with what You know…"

6 - Reported by Muslim in his Ṣaḥīḥ (2985) and Ibn Māja in his Sunan (4202); the wording is Muslim's, from Abū Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 32:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿That, and whoever honours the rites of Allah, indeed it is from the piety of the hearts.﴾ (32)

﴿That...﴾ (32) [al-Hajj]: As we said in the previous passage, it is a reference to the preceding discourse, which has become clear and well known, and after it we resume a new discourse to which attention must be paid.

﴿And whoever honours the rites of Allah...﴾ (32) [al-Hajj]: The rites (sha'a'ir) are the plural of sha'ira, and they are the markers that Allah has set for His servants so that they may attain His reward by honouring them. So ihram is a sha'ira, takbir is a sha'ira, tawaf is a sha'ira, sa'y is a sha'ira, and stoning the pillars (ramy al-jimar) is a sha'ira, and so on. These are matters that Allah has glorified and commanded us to honour.(1)

And glorifying a thing is more eloquent and more comprehensive than doing it, performing it, or working at it. To glorify the rites means: to perform them with love, passion and sincerity, and to bring them in the most perfect manner, and perhaps to exceed what was required of him.

Our example in this is the Friend of Allah, Ibrahim, when Allah commanded him to raise the foundations of the House. It would have sufficed him to build to the height his hand could reach, and thereby he would have fulfilled what he was commanded. But he loved this duty and was passionate about it, so he devised a means for the task and placed a stone upon a stone so that he could stand on it and raise the building to the height he reached.

So love of Allah's command is a rung of the ladders of faith, to which we must aspire, even in worldly work. Suppose you were transferred to a new department, and it reached your knowledge that its director is a serious and strict man who holds accountable every small and great matter, forbidding delay or laxity during official working hours. Then you find yourself adhering to these instructions to the letter, and even exceeding them, not out of love for the work, but so that you will not be called to account before this director on some day.

Therefore, the goal is that we perform the duties with love and passion that lead us to the love of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Thus we find some of the people of knowledge saying: "A sin that bequeaths humility and brokenness is better than an act of obedience that bequeaths might and arrogance."(2)

The important thing is that we reach Allah, that we submit to Allah, that we humble ourselves before His might and majesty. A sin that brings you to this end is better than an obedience that delivers you to delusion and arrogance.

This love for the duties, and this passion, was expressed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he said: "The coolness of my eyes has been made to be in prayer."(3) Therefore the Qur'an censured those who, ﴿when they stand up to prayer, stand up lazily, showing off to the people, and do not remember Allah except a little﴾ (142) [al-Nisa'].

And his daughter Fatimah(4), may Allah be pleased with her, used to polish the dirham and make it shine. When the Messenger of Allah asked her what she was doing, she said: "Because I intended to give it in charity, and I know that it falls into the hand of Allah before it falls into the hand of the poor." This is the glorifying of Allah's rites and performing them out of desire and love.

In the early ages of Islam, people were ranked by how early they were to the congregational prayer when the call was heard, and by how late they were to leave the mosque after the prayer. You may compare the state of those people with our state today. Those were a people who glorified Allah's rites and preferred nothing over them.

The love of duties and the glorifying of Allah's rites reached the point that one of the knowers said: "I have come to fear that Allah will not reward me for my obedience." They asked him: "And why is that?" He said: "Because I have come to crave it," meaning: it has become a desire for me, so how is one rewarded for a desire?

Therefore, the people of resolve and the people of knowledge of Allah, when a command comes from Allah and is established, take it up with openness and ease, without dispute or argument. And how would they argue with the command of Allah while they glorify it? From here we say to those who dispute matters that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did, such as his having more than one wife for example, and object, and some of them even accuse the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of what is unbecoming.

We say to them: Since you have believed that he is the Messenger of Allah, how do you set for him the measures of perfection from your own selves? And you say: "He should have done such-and-such, and not done such-and-such"? Do you have from perfection what you measure the Messenger of Allah's actions by? It is fitting that perfection comes from him (ﷺ) and on his side, not from your side.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿indeed it is from the piety of the hearts﴾ (32) [al-Hajj]: It is not from the piety of the limbs, but the piety of the heart, not the piety of the form. The heart is the place where Allah looks at you, and the place where your glorifying of Allah's rites is measured.

We have previously mentioned that Allah, exalted is He, does not wish to subdue our bodies; rather He wishes to subdue our hearts. Had He, glorified is He, wished that bodies be subdued, they would have submitted to Him compelled, as in His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers. If We willed, We would send down upon them from the sky a sign, so that their necks would remain humbly subject to it﴾ (3-4) [al-Shu'ara'].

You can compel someone weaker than you to do anything he dislikes; if you wish, he will prostrate to you. But you cannot place love or respect for you in his heart, why? Because you can compel the form, but the heart is not under your authority in any way.

1 - There is another view regarding the interpretation of this verse: the rites of Allah here refer to the camels (budn) and the offerings (hady) that are sent to the Ka'bah. Glorifying the rites of Allah here means: regarding the camels as great, making them fat, and considering them fine. [See the reports cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur fi al-Tafsir bi al-Ma'thur (6/46) from Ibn 'Abbas and Mujahid].

2 - From the maxims of Ibn 'Ata' Allah al-Iskandari, mentioned by Abd al-'Al Kahil in his book "Abu al-'Aynayn al-Dasuqi," p. 76, Dar al-Sha'b, Cairo.

3 - Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/128, 199, 285), al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (7/61), and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (2/160), who said: "Sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. The full hadith is: "Made beloved to me from your world are women and perfume."

4 - She is Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah, and her mother was Khadijah bint Khuwaylid. She was born in 18 BH, and Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali ibn Abi Talib married her when she was eighteen years old, and she bore him al-Hasan, al-Husayn, Umm Kulthum and Zaynab. She lived six months after her father. She died in 11 AH at the age of 29. Al-A'lam of al-Zirikli (5/132).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 33:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿For you therein are benefits until an appointed term; then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House.﴾ (22:33)

Meaning: As long as these matters are among the symbols of Allah and of the piety of hearts, then practise them and magnify them, for you have in them benefits, whether you know them or not. Perhaps you know some of them and not the rest, for they are hidden from you. Even if you do not know the reward for these symbols, the value of the reward for acting upon them is in accordance with the sincerity (ikhlas) breathed into this act.

As for the meaning of ﴿until an appointed term﴾ (22:33): since Allah, exalted is He, concluded the verse with His saying ﴿then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House﴾ (22:33), the intended meaning here is the rite of slaughter (dhabh). It is not hidden what benefits it holds, for we benefit from its wool, its hair and its milk, and its flesh, and we take it as an adornment and as a mount.

All of this is ﴿until an appointed term﴾ (22:33), meaning: a known time, which is the moment you say and intend: "This is a gift for the Haram." From the moment this intention is made, you have no right to benefit from any of it, neither you nor anyone else.(1) Therefore they mark it with a sign, so that if it strays from its owner they know that it is dedicated to the House of Allah, and no one takes it.(2)

Since these are benefits until an appointed term, they must be worldly benefits; as for the benefits of the Hereafter, you will find them later, in the Hereafter.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House﴾ (22:33), meaning: after this appointed term, its journey ends at the Haram, where it is slaughtered.

The scholars have spoken concerning this verse, ﴿then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House﴾ (22:33), saying: the place of slaughter is in Mina, not in Makkah, while the verse says: its place of sacrifice is the Ancient House.

We say: the original ruling, as came in the verse, is that slaughter is in Makkah and in the Haram. However, since they found slaughter within the Haram disagreeable because of the filth and blood and the like that this process leaves behind, it was judged appropriate to make the slaughter away from the Haram so that it remains clean. This does not negate the original ruling, which is that slaughter be in the Haram, as came in another verse: ﴿as an offering to reach the Ka'bah﴾ (5:95).

And in the noble hadith: "All of Makkah is a place of sacrifice (manhar)."(4)

1 - Ibn 'Abbas said: [the benefit lasts] as long as one has not designated it as a camel (badanah) or an offering (hady); if it is designated as a badanah or hady, all that benefit ends. Likewise said 'Ata', al-Dahhak, Qatadah and others. Others said: rather, he may benefit from it even if it is an offering, when he needs to, as is established in the two Sahihs from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw a man driving a camel (badanah) and said: "Ride it." He said: "It is a badanah." He said: "Ride it, woe to you." [Cited by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 3/220].
2 - This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, do not violate the symbols of Allah, nor the sacred month, nor the offering, nor the garlands...﴾ (5:2). Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir (2/4): "That is: do not abandon sending offerings to the Sacred House, for in it is the magnifying of the symbols of Allah; and do not abandon garlanding them so that they are distinguished from other livestock, and so that it is known that they are an offering to the Ka'bah, and whoever intends them harm avoids them, and so that whoever sees them is moved to bring the like of them."
3 - There are two opinions regarding the interpretation of this verse, concerning the referent of the pronoun in (mahalluha) [its place of sacrifice]:
- The badanah and the offering, meaning: they are slaughtered at Mina on the day of sacrifice (an-nahr). [From 'Ata']. And when it enters the Haram, it has reached its place (mahall) [from 'Ikrimah]. This is the view adopted by our shaykh, Fadilat al-Shaykh al-Sha'rawi, may Allah have mercy on him.
- The rites and rituals of the Hajj: that is, the rites of Hajj in their entirety, from standing at 'Arafah and stoning the pillars (ramy al-jimar) to sa'y, ending with the tawaf al-ifadah at the Ancient House. Said by al-Qurtubi in his Tafsir (6/4588).
4 - From Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sacrificed, then shaved his head and sat down for the people. Whatever he was asked about, he would say: "No blame, no blame," until a man came and said: "I shaved before I sacrificed." He said: "No blame." Then another came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I shaved before I threw." He said: "No blame." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "All of 'Arafah is a place of standing, all of Muzdalifah is a place of standing, all of Mina is a place of sacrifice, and all the mountain passes of Makkah are a path and a place of sacrifice." Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/326) and al-Darimi in his Sunan (2/57).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 22, verse 34:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And for every community We have appointed rites (mansak) that they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided for them of the beast of cattle. So your God is one God, so submit to Him. And give good tidings to the humble (al-mukhbitin).﴾ (22:34):

Al-Mansak (rite, mansak): it is worship ('ibadah), as in the saying of Allah, the Exalted, on the tongue of Ibrahim, peace be upon him: ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer, my rites (nusuki), my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ (6:162) [al-An'am].

The meaning of ﴿And for every community We have appointed rites...﴾ (22:34) [al-Hajj]: the rites, the ceremonies and the acts of worship are not necessarily uniform among all nations. Rather, every community has what suits it and suits its temporal and environmental circumstances.

Therefore, the messengers did not come to change the foundations and principles upon which religion rests, because these foundations and principles are fixed in all the heavenly messages; they do not change or alter with the change of messengers.

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿He has ordained for you of religion that which He enjoined upon Noah and that which We revealed to you, and that which We enjoined upon Abraham, Moses and Jesus: that you establish the religion and do not become divided therein...﴾ (42:13) [al-Shura].

This applies to the fixed doctrinal foundations; as for the subsidiary matters, we see what benefits the society and what acts of obedience and worship suit it.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, explains the wisdom behind these rites: ﴿that they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided for them of the beast of cattle...﴾ (22:34) [al-Hajj]: that is, that they mention Allah in everything, and thank Him for every blessing they receive from the beast of cattle.

Therefore, we mention Allah at the time of slaughter; we say: "In the name of Allah, Allah is greatest." Why? Because slaughter is the taking of a soul that Allah created, and it was not for you to take it by your own will. So the meaning of "In the name of Allah and Allah is greatest" here is that I do not take its soul on my own account, but because Allah commanded me and permitted it to me. So "Allah is greatest" in this situation is above your will and above your emotions.

We see some people who disdain this matter of slaughter. They say: "How do you slaughter this animal or this chicken?" They claim mercy and compassion towards these animals, but he is not more merciful to them than their Creator. We only slaughter them because Allah made them lawful, and we only eat them in the name of Allah, as evidenced by the fact that what Allah has forbidden us we never approach at all.

Do I honour the cat over the rabbit, so that I slaughter the rabbit and leave the cat? Do I respect the dog over the sheep? Never. The matter is one of legislation and a command established from Allah, so it is incumbent upon me to magnify Him and obey Him.

As for His saying, ﴿over what He has provided for them of the beast of cattle...﴾ (22:34) [al-Hajj]: provision means that He, exalted is He, brought it into existence for you, made it yours, and subjected it to you, so you tamed it, made it serve you, and benefited from it. Were it not for His subjugation, it would not have submitted to you by your strength and power.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿So your God is one God...﴾ (22:34) [al-Hajj]: meaning, even if the laws differ from one nation to another, beware lest you think that this is from one god and that from another god. Rather, it is one God who legislates for each nation what suits it and what sets it right, because heavenly legislations come as remedies for social ills.

The essential foundation is faith in one God, the Doer, All-Powerful, the Free Chooser, who is conveyed from by a messenger with a miracle that shows the truth of his conveying from Allah. This is the root of all heavenly religions. Likewise, the principles and fundamentals of religion are one and agreed upon: theft, adultery, false testimony, etc. are all forbidden in every religion.

But there are matters that suit one nation and do not suit another, and the Legislator of all is one God. All people, from Adam until the Hour is established, are His dependants, and they are equal to Him; therefore He chooses for each what sets it right.

Do you not see how the head of a household organizes the lives of his children (and to Allah belongs the highest likeness)? He says: "This one does such and such, and that one does such and such." And when the food comes he says: "This one eats such and such, because he is sick, for example, and the food of the others does not suit him," and he orders the mother to prepare for this sick one the food that suits him. That is because he is a shepherd over all of them, responsible for all of them, and he must consider the interest of each one of them individually(1).

So then: the difference of legislations in these partial matters between nations does not mean a plurality of gods, far from it, and Allah forbid. Rather, He is one God who gives His servants each according to their need, so that society may be balanced and its condition made upright.

We recall that the doctor at the health unit had two jars, each containing a specific mixture, and he gave all the patients, despite their differing illnesses, only these two types. Therefore it was of no benefit. But now the skilled doctor must perform on his patient the necessary examinations and tests, so as to determine his illness precisely, then prescribe the treatment suited to this condition in precise doses that cure the disease and do not harm the patient on the other hand. Likewise is the matter of the differences of heavenly legislations among nations.

Since your God is one God, and since you are equal before Him, and none of you is a son of God, nor is there any kinship between him and Allah. Therefore: ﴿so submit to Him...﴾ (22:34) [al-Hajj]: meaning, submit all your affairs to Allah. If He commands, magnify His command and take it with ease and openness; if He leaves room for your choice, then do what you will. And do not forget that Allah, exalted is He, has given you an opportunity for ascent in faith and for ascent in excellence (ihsan), and has opened for you the field of excellence if you wish.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And give good tidings to the humble (al-mukhbitin).﴾ (22:34) [al-Hajj]: al-mukhbit (the humble): in the general sense, it means the person who is submissive, lowly, and humble before all the commands of Allah. The precise meaning of al-mukhbit is the one who, when wronged, does not defend his own self, in accordance with the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever is patient and forgives, indeed that is of the matters requiring determination.﴾ (42:43) [al-Shura], with the emphatic lam.

As for the advice of Luqman to his son: ﴿And be patient over what has afflicted you; indeed, that is of the matters requiring determination.﴾ (31:17) [Luqman], without emphasis. Why?

They said: because Luqman advises his son to be patient over what has afflicted him, and afflictions are of two kinds: an affliction that befalls a person, and for which he has an adversary who caused the affliction upon him; this is accompanied by anger and a fury for vengeance. And an affliction that befalls a person with no adversary, such as illness, for example. If there is an adversary, then patience is harder, so it required emphasis, unlike the affliction in which there is no adversary before you, for it is from Allah, so patience over it is easier than the former.

Nevertheless, the Truth, glory be to Him, made outlets for the human soul through which it releases itself, so that anger does not ferment within it and turn into rancour and malice, which may lead to more than what has befallen you. Therefore He permitted you to respond, but made you love other paths that are more beneficial to you. He, blessed and exalted is He, says: ﴿And those who restrain anger and pardon people, and Allah loves the good-doers.﴾ (3:134) [Al 'Imran]:

These are three stages, and you choose among them according to your understanding of Allah and your nearness to Him:

The first: ﴿And those who restrain anger...﴾ (3:134) [Al 'Imran]: that is, you restrain your anger within yourself, without translating this anger into a vengeful act, so you do not take revenge. Anger, then, is a matter of feeling in the heart, present in the emotions of the soul, and this is one stage.

The second: ﴿And those who pardon people...﴾ (3:134) [Al 'Imran]: that is, he does not avenge, nor even allow anger a place in himself, but purifies his soul of feelings of rage and anger, willingly.

The third: ﴿And Allah loves the good-doers.﴾ (3:134) [Al 'Imran]: and this is the highest of ranks, which is that you do not suffice with pardon, but also do good to the one who wronged you. Some say this is contrary to the nature of humans. Yes, it is contrary to the nature of ordinary humans, but those who know the reward, and know that by doing so they will be under the care of their Lord, find this act easy, and even love to do good to the one who wronged them.

Therefore, al-Hasan al-Basri, may Allah be pleased with him, when he was informed that a man had spoken ill of him in one of the gatherings, and it was the time of the first fresh dates, sent his servant to him with a tray of fresh dates, and said: "It has reached me that you have given me your good deeds yesterday"(2).

It is known that good deeds are far more precious and valuable than a tray of fresh dates. From here they say: how strange is the one who harms the one who harmed him, for he has given him his good deeds, which are the essence of his work, so how can he harm him?

It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him, wants to create balance in society and to eliminate the causes of hatred and the reasons for rancour in the human soul. When you do good to the one who harms you, you uproot the roots of hatred and malice from his soul, as Allah, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Repel with that which is better, and thereupon the one between you and him is enmity as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ (41:34) [Fussilat]: you have removed your opponent from the mould of enmity into the mould of loyalty and love.

So the humble one is humble before Allah, but the one who is not humble you find arrogant (tyrannical, yatafar'an) towards those around him, seeing himself as greater than everyone. If he had remembered the majesty of his Lord, he would have humbled himself to Him, and been humbled and broken before His creation. Arrogance is evidence of heedlessness of the greatness of Allah, as if he had never witnessed his Creator.

So then: you may say that humility is of two kinds: humility before Allah, through submission, reverence and magnifying His commands, and humility towards the creatures of Allah, such that he does not defend his own oppression and does not oppress, but rather tolerates and pardons, because he knows well that if he is wronged by a creature, the Creator takes his side.

Look at your children: if one of them wrongs another, to whom do you lean, and with whom do you sympathize? Without doubt you will incline to the wronged one, and be tender towards him, and want to compensate him for the injustice that befell him, to the extent that the wrongdoer regrets his wrongdoing, because he has singled out his wronged brother over him, and perhaps wishes that he were the wronged rather than the wrongdoer.

Likewise the state of the humble one: he sees that all creatures are the dependants of Allah, and that the most beloved of them to Him are the most compassionate towards His dependants. Therefore he pardons the one who wronged him, and leaves his affair to Allah, Lord of all. Just as, when the wronged one returns the wrong, he returns it by his own strength and capacity, but if he leaves the response to Allah, the response comes according to the measure of His, glory be to Him, strength.

Another point that the wronged should heed before he thinks of revenge: who knows, perhaps you too have wronged others without realizing it. Perhaps people have grievances against you that you do not feel and that are not in your reckoning. So the matter is, then, for you and against you.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says in the sacred hadith: "O son of Adam, you called down (curses) upon the one who wronged you."

This is permitted to you by His saying: ﴿Allah does not like the public utterance of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged.﴾ (4:148) [al-Nisa']: that is, We have given you the opportunity to call down (curses) upon the one who wronged you.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: "And he who wronged you called down (curses) upon you. If you wish, We answer you and We answer against you; and if you wish, We delay you both until the Hereafter, and My pardon will suffice you both."(3)

So the humble one keeps all this in mind, and inclines to pardon and forgiveness, so that his Lord, mighty and majestic, takes his side. Therefore they say: if the wrongdoer knew what Allah has prepared for the wronged of honour, he would begrudge him the wrong.

So when you see the wronged one pardon you and forgive you, do not think that you have subdued him to yourself. Rather, he has submitted to Allah, who will raise him above you, and exalt his head over you one day.

Therefore, among the patterns of sound behaviour: when two people quarrel, one of the wise says: "For you both there is a father to whom we return, or an elder to whom we refer in this dispute."

1 - This is in confirmation of the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock. The ruler over people is a shepherd and is responsible for his subjects; the man is a shepherd over his household and is responsible for them; the woman is a shepherd over her husband's house and children and is responsible for them; the servant is a shepherd over his master's property and is responsible for it. Indeed, each of you is a shepherd, and each of you is responsible for his flock." Related by Muslim in his Sahih (1829), and al-Bukhari in his Sahih (893, 2409), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.
2 - Mentioned by Abu Hamid al-Ghazali (3/154) that a man said to al-Hasan: "So-and-so has backbited you," so he sent to him fresh dates on a tray, and said: "It has reached me that you have given me your good deeds, so I wanted to reward you for them, so excuse me, for I cannot reward you in full."
3 - Mentioned by Abu Hamid al-Ghazali (3/183) from the saying of Yazid ibn Maysarah: "If you keep calling down (curses) upon the one who wronged you, then Allah, exalted is He, says: 'Another calls down upon you, saying you wronged him. If you wish, We answer him and answer against you; and if you wish, We delay you both until the Day of Resurrection, and My pardon will suffice you both.'"

Then the Exalted says:

﴿Those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and the patient in what befalls them, and those who establish the prayer, and from what We have provided them they spend.﴾ (22:35)

He, glory be to Him, clarifies for us some of the attributes of the *mukhbitin* (the humble, lowly before their Lord). They are ﴿those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble...﴾ (22:35). *Wajilat* (وجلت) means they feared, were agitated, and trembled at the mention of Allah, out of glorification of Him and awe before Him.

In another verse, the Exalted says: ﴿Surely by the remembrance of Allah hearts find rest﴾ (13:28).

So once He says ﴿their hearts tremble﴾ (22:35), and once ﴿hearts find rest﴾ (13:28). Why? Because if the remembrance of Allah comes after transgression, the soul must fear, tremble and be agitated out of awe of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. But if the remembrance of Allah comes after a calamity or hardship, the soul finds rest in it and is comforted by the store of faith it has, to which it returns in hardship and on which it leans in straitness and trial. If you are afflicted with a calamity and the means of averting it are out of reach, you say: "I have a Lord," and you turn to Him, as Moses (peace be upon him) did when he said: ﴿Surely my Lord is with me; He will guide me﴾ (26:62).

﴿And the patient in what befalls them...﴾ (22:35). *Asaba* (أصاب) means that something has come upon you which you, in your own estimation, consider evil, and so you count it a calamity. We measure a calamity according to the superficiality of the harmful act. But if you take into your reckoning the reward for it, the calamity becomes easy for you and you no longer regard it as such. Therefore, in the noble hadith, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The afflicted one is the one who is deprived of reward."

This is the one truly afflicted, whose calamity cannot be mended. As for one who is struck by something and bears it patiently until he gains the reward, there is no calamity in this.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿and those who establish the prayer...﴾ (22:35). The prayer (*salah*, the ritual prayer) is the constant allegiance of the Muslim servant and an obligation that never falls from him under any circumstances. The two testimonies (*shahadatan*) need only be uttered once in a lifetime. Zakat (obligatory almsgiving), if you possess the *nisab* (the minimum threshold of wealth liable for zakat), is due once a year. Fasting is likewise: one month in the year. Hajj, if you are able, is once in a lifetime, and if you are not able, there is no hajj upon you.

So, the prayer is the continuous allegiance to the Truth, glory be to Him, throughout the entire day. Your Lord is the One who calls you to it, and then you may determine the time and place of this meeting in His presence, Exalted is He, for He is ready to meet you at any time.

Imagine that the President of the Republic, or a king for example, invites you and insists on seeing you five times a day to be in his presence. Yet the Exalted, when He calls His servants to meet Him, does not call them once but five times a day and night, for He, glory be to Him, does not burden Himself with repeated meetings in this process; He meets everyone at one time.

When Imam Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked: "How does Allah account for all these people at one time?" he said: "Just as He provides for them all at one time."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and from what We have provided them they spend﴾ (22:35). They do not spend from their own pockets, but from the bounty and provision of Allah. It is remarkable that Allah, Exalted is He, gives you, grants you and showers you with favour out of His grace, glory be to Him, and then, when He wants you to help a needy person, He says to you: ﴿Who is it that will lend Allah a goodly loan?﴾ (57:11).

It is as if Allah, Exalted is He, is saying to us: "I do not take back My gift or My giving." So I say: "Give what you took to so-and-so." Rather, if you give the poor from your wealth, it too is stored up for you and will not be lost. The provision that Allah has bestowed upon you is your possession, and We will never defraud you of any part of it. Your Lord respects your ownership and respects the reward of your labour, effort and striving.

We say, and to Allah belongs the highest similitude: it is like a man who needs a large sum for one of his sons, so he takes from the others what they have, including what they have saved from their expenses, on the promise that he will compensate them in return later on.

Therefore He says after it: ﴿so that He may multiply it for him...﴾ (57:11). Your Lord deals with you by increase. For this reason some say: Allah has forbidden us riba (usury), yet He deals with us through it. Yes, your Lord deals with you by way of increase and says to you: "Leave this dealing to Me, for when I increase you I do not diminish others, nor do I reduce anything that I possess, nor do I burden the weak or the needy, nor do I exploit their need."

In Islam, charity is a form of insurance for its giver against poverty if he should come to need. The thing a person most fears is need in old age, the inability to earn, and incapacity to work. He fears that his wealth will run out and that he will depend on people in his old age.

At that point his Lord says to him: "Be at peace. Just as you gave in your time of ease, others will give to you in your time of want and need."

So, He takes from you in order to give to you, and to secure for you the future of your life that you fear.

In Islam, charity is a fund for the mutual solidarity of society, like the reserve fund in insurance companies. So when the means of provision become narrow for you and you complain of old age and incapacity, we say to you: "Do not grieve, for you are in a believing, mutually supportive society. Just as we asked you to give while you had means, we ask others to give to you while you are destitute."

Then the Truthful One, glorified is He, says:

﴿And the camels We have made for you as among the symbols of Allah; in them is good for you. So mention the name of Allah over them as they stand in ranks. Then when their sides fall (lifeless), eat from them and feed the contented and the beggar. Thus have We subjected them to you, that you may be grateful.﴾ (22:36)

After the Exalted One spoke about spending from what Allah has provided for you, He spoke about spending on the camels (al-budn). Al-budn is the plural of badanah, which is a camel or a she-camel, or what is equivalent to them of cattle. It is called badanah as an indication that it must be fleshy, fat and abundant. This quality must be observed when you choose the offering (al-hady) that you will present to Allah. Beware of being among those who assign to Allah what they dislike. Rather, be among those to whom Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, spend of the good things you have earned...﴾ (2:267).

As for His saying, ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them as they stand in ranks⦁﴾ (22:36): that is, remember Allah with gratitude for having granted them and subjected them to you, and mention the name of Allah over them at the time of slaughtering them.

The meaning of ﴿ṣawāff⦁﴾ (22:36): that is, standing upright on their feet, with no weakness or emaciation in them, arranged in rows as if they were displayed before you. These are the good qualities of camels that suit this rite and are fitting to be presented as an offering to the House of Allah.

The meaning of ﴿fa-idhā wajabat junūbuhā⦁﴾ (22:36): "wajaba al-shay' wujūban" means that it fell forcefully upon the ground. It is well known that the camel is not slaughtered while lying on the ground like the rest of the livestock; rather, it is slaughtered (naḥr) while standing. So when it is slaughtered, it falls to the ground and collapses forcefully from its bulk.

﴿Then eat from them⦁﴾ (22:36). We have said that eating is only from the pure offering (al-hady al-maḥḍ) and the voluntary sacrifice that is not connected to any matter of the Hajj. Therefore, it is not a hady of tamattu' or qiran, nor is it a compensation (jabr) for a violation, nor is it a vow (nadhr), etc.

The reason for the command to eat from the offering is that they used to be reluctant to eat from what was slaughtered for the poor, and in the command to eat from it there is an indication of the necessity of choosing from what the soul does not loathe.

The meaning of ﴿al-qāniʿ wal-muʿtarr⦁﴾ (22:36): al-qāniʿ is the poor person who keeps himself from asking people, and al-muʿtarr is the poor person who presents himself to be asked.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Thus have We subjected them to you, that you may be grateful⦁﴾ (22:36). That is, We have subjected them to you, even outside this occasion. Allah has subjected them to you since man came into existence. Therefore, you must thank Allah for having brought them into being and given you ownership of them, and thank Him for having subjected them and made them submissive to you, and thank Him for having guided you to perform this rite, to carry out this ritual, and to do this good which will benefit you in this world and in the Hereafter.

1 - Several readings have been transmitted for this word:
- ṣawāff: that is, standing on three well-tied legs, with its left forelimb bound. Transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, and it is the reading of the majority.
- ṣawāfin: plural of ṣāfinah, which is the one that has raised one of its forelegs while tied, so that it does not become agitated. Transmitted from Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, and Ibn ʿUmar.
- ṣawāfī: that is, pure for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, they do not associate anyone with Him in the naming over its slaughter. Transmitted from al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj, Mujāhid, Zayd ibn Aslam, and Abū Mūsā al-Ash'arī.
- ṣawāff: having the same meaning as the previous one. Transmitted from al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/4593].
2 - Ibn al-Athīr said: al-qāniʿ originally means the one who asks. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said, as transmitted from him by Ibn Abī Shaybah and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd: al-qāniʿ is the one who is content with what is in your hands, coming to you without asking; and al-muʿtarr is the one who presents himself to you so that you feed him. The wording of Ibn Abī Shaybah: "and al-muʿtarr is the one who comes to you, showing you himself without asking you." [Al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti 6/55].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 37:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿It is not their flesh nor their blood that reaches Allah, but it is your piety that reaches Him. Thus He has subjected them to you so that you may glorify Allah for having guided you. And give good tidings to the good-doers.﴾ (22:37)

That is because before Islam, when they slaughtered for idols, they would smear the idol with the blood of the sacrificed animal (1), as if they were saying to it: "We have slaughtered for you, and here is the blood of the sacrifice." In this act of theirs there is evidence of their stupidity and the foolishness of their conduct, for they thought that if they did not smear it with blood, it would not be known that they had slaughtered on its account.

Here the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, draws attention to this matter: ﴿It is not their flesh nor their blood..﴾ (22:37). That is: He takes nothing from them. He is capable of giving the poor man whom you were commanded to give to, and making him exactly like you, without need.

What Allah intended by the variation among people in poverty and wealth is that there should be a balance in society. Society is not a mechanical machine that moves at one rate; it is the life of human beings, which must be built on need and on complementarity. Thus there must be differences among people, and then the heavenly laws intervene, taking from the strong and giving to the weak, and taking from the rich and giving to the poor. At that point, feelings of spite, envy, hatred and selfishness are eliminated.

When the strong gives the weak from his strength, he does not envy him for it, and he wishes for its continuance, because its good returns to him. And when the rich gives the poor from what Allah has bestowed upon him, he wins over his heart and uproots from it resentment and envy, and he prays for the continuance of blessing for him.

This difference must exist so that there may be realised in us the saying of the Messenger (ﷺ): "The believer to the believer is like a solid structure, one part of it strengthening another" (2).

Therefore, you see that the person of blessing who spreads it among others, if a misfortune befalls him in his wealth, others grieve for him and suffer with his pain, because his blessing overflows upon them and his good reaches them. And until recently, among the people of the countryside, one of them would raise a cow or a water buffalo to milk it, and he would not forget the neighbours and those in need, and they would pray to Allah to bless his wealth for him; and if a harm befell him in his wealth, they grieved on his account.

So, when you overflow with the blessing of Allah upon those who have been deprived of it, you ward off from yourself much resentment and envy. If you do not do this, then at the very least conceal this good from the eyes of the needy, so as not to stir up their resentment. Perhaps if a sensible man sees you, his faith restrains him so that his eyes do not stretch toward what is in your hand. But when small children see you carrying what they have been deprived of, or see your child eating while they are deprived, here is the problem. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But it is your piety that reaches Him..﴾ (22:37).

Fearing Allah (ittiqa') is following His method. Allah is obeyed by following the method, so He is not disobeyed, He is remembered so He is not forgotten, and He is thanked so He is not disbelieved. The path of obedience is found in following the method, with "do" and "do not do." And He is remembered so He is not forgotten, because the servant may obey Allah and carry out the method of Allah, but the blessings that Allah created may occupy the servant away from Allah. The method calls you to remember in every blessing the One who bestowed it, and beware lest the blessing make you forget the Bestower.

Then the Blessed and Exalted says: ﴿Thus He has subjected them to you so that you may glorify Allah for having guided you. And give good tidings to the good-doers.﴾ (22:37).

Here you notice the matter of the ambiguous verses (mutashabihat) in the Noble Qur'an. In the previous verse He, glorified is He, concluded with His saying: ﴿Thus We have subjected them to you so that you may be grateful.﴾ (22:36).

These ambiguous parallels are pondered by the scholars who study the Qur'an and turn over its verses. Therefore they gather such parallel verses that speak on one subject and arrange them in the mind. For this reason they are not trusted with memorisation alone. Hence they said: whoever wishes to memorise the Qur'an should set aside the question of knowledge while memorising, so that if he forgets a word he stops in his place and does not move until he recalls it; whereas the scholar may put its synonym in its place, and the meaning remains sound for him.

The meaning of His saying: ﴿so that you may glorify Allah for having guided you..﴾ (22:37) is: that you remember Him and thank Him for having enabled you to these acts of obedience. ﴿And give good tidings to the good-doers (22:37).﴾ "Give good tidings" (bashshir) means: inform of something pleasing before its time comes, so that the one given the tidings may prepare for it and rejoice in it. Likewise warning (indhar): that you inform of something bad before it befalls, so that the one warned may prepare for it, find the opportunity to make up for his error, guard himself against what he is warned of, and turn to what will save him.

And ﴿the good-doers (al-muhsinin) (22:37)﴾ is the plural of muhsin. Ihsan (excellence) is the highest rank of faith: it is that you bind yourself to some of the obedience of Allah which He has imposed upon you, beyond what He has imposed. Your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, has imposed on you five prayers in the day and night, and it is within your power to add to these prayers as much as you wish, but of the kind of what Allah has imposed on you; you should not invent an act of worship of your own. Likewise the matter stands with fasting, with zakat, with hajj, and with the rest of the acts of obedience which Allah has obligated upon you. If you do this, you have entered the station of ihsan.

In ihsan there are two matters: that by which one is excellent, which is the worship or obedience to which you bind yourself beyond what Allah has imposed, and the one who strives for it, which is that you perform the deed as if Allah is watching you, as came in the hadith of Gabriel: "Ihsan is that you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, He sees you" (3).

So your watchfulness of Allah and your observance of His regard upon you pushes you to this ihsan. Do you not see the worker whom you supervise and oversee, and how he finishes the work on its appointed time, and how he perfects it? Unlike if you left him and turned away from him.

If you do not reach this station in which you are as if you see Allah, then at the very least remember His regard toward you, and His watchfulness over your movements and stillnesses.

Therefore, in Surat al-Dhariyat: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs, taking what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that good-doers.﴾ (51:15-16).

Then it explains the reason for this ihsan: ﴿They used to sleep but little of the night, and in the hours before dawn they would seek forgiveness, and in their wealth was a right for the beggar and the deprived.﴾ (51:17-19).

And who obligates you to these duties? It is permitted for you to pray the 'isha' and then sleep until dawn; likewise He did not obligate you to seek forgiveness at the time of dawn, nor to voluntary charity. So these are acts of obedience beyond what Allah has imposed, which brought their doers to the station of ihsan, the highest rank of faith, so let whoever wishes strive for it.

1 - Ibn 'Abbas said: The people of the Jahiliyya would smear the House with the blood of the sacrificial camels, and the Muslims wished to do the same, so the verse was revealed. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/4596] al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/56) also as a saying of Ibn 'Abbas, and attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh.
2 - A hadith agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh). Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (2446), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2585), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him).
3 - A hadith agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh). Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (50), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (8), Kitab al-Iman, from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 22, verse 38:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Indeed, Allah defends those who believe. Indeed, Allah does not love every treacherous ingrate.﴾ (38)

The opening of the verse, ﴿Indeed, Allah defends those who believe...﴾ (38) [al-Hajj], makes us feel that there is a battle, and a battle in which Allah defends must be between a truth that He has sent down and a falsehood that confronts it. It has already been mentioned before this that He, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿These two adversaries dispute concerning their Lord...﴾ (19) [al-Hajj].

As long as there is enmity, battles must arise from it. These battles may take the form of words and argument, and they may take the form of violence, force, ferocity, and direct clashing with the tools of war.

The battle of the Prophet (ﷺ) with his opponents from the disbelievers of Makkah did not stop at the limit of a verbal battle. They called him, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him, a sorcerer, a soothsayer, a madman, a poet, a fabricator, and so on. Then the matter developed into harming and torturing his companions. They would come to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with their heads split and wounded, and he (ﷺ) would say to them: "I have not been commanded to fight. Be patient, be patient, patience, patience..."

Until the aggression of the disbelievers increased and their excesses overflowed, Allah permitted His Messenger to fight, and He said: ﴿Permission is given to those who are fought against, because they have been wronged. And indeed, Allah is capable of giving them victory.﴾ (39) [al-Hajj].

As for His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah defends those who believe...﴾ (38) [al-Hajj]: the form yudafi' (defends) is an intensive form of yadfa' (repels). Yadfa' indicates one thing, or one time, after which the matter ends. But yudafi' indicates the response of an action with its like: Allah repels them and they in turn respond with repelling, so there occurs a pushing back and forth and interaction from both sides, and this does not happen except in a battle.

A battle means a victor and a vanquished. Therefore, the Truth, blessed and exalted, reassures the believers that He will enter the battle in their ranks and will defend them.

His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah defends those who believe...﴾ (38) [al-Hajj], is a natural matter, because the Truth, glorified is He, would not send a messenger and leave him to the people of falsehood to overpower him; otherwise what would be the use of the message? Therefore Allah reassures His Messenger and gives him good tidings, saying:

﴿And certainly has Our word preceded to Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers – they will be the predominant.﴾ (171-173) [al-Saffat].

And He said: ﴿And Allah will surely support those who support Him...﴾ (40) [al-Hajj].

And He said: ﴿If you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet.﴾ (7) [Muhammad].

All these are verses that reassure the believers and give them good tidings, and they came in stages for a wisdom that Allah, the Truth, glorified is He, willed. He prevented them from fighting at the beginning for a wisdom; then He made fighting among themselves; and before He permitted them to fight their enemies, it was for a wisdom: that He might test the believers and purify them, so that those of weakness and cowardice would leave their ranks, and those of weak faith who worship Allah on an edge would depart, and there would remain only the strong of faith and firm of creed, who carries the banner of this religion and spreads it across the lands of the earth, because it is a universal call for every time and every place until the Hour is established. Since this call has this standing, it must have strong men to carry it; otherwise, if the enemies were able to eliminate it, the religion of Allah would never stand.

Thus: it was necessary that Allah, the Truth, glorified is He, purify the people of faith as the goldsmith purifies gold and removes its impurity when he puts it in the fire. Likewise, trials and tribulations were for purifying the people of faith and distinguishing them, but through fighting in one row.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love every treacherous ingrate.﴾ (38) [al-Hajj]. It is as if the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has become a party in the battle. Khawwan (treacherous) is an intensive form of kha'in (traitor), one who is abundant in betrayal; likewise kafur (ingrate) is an intensive form of kafir (disbeliever).

The meaning of betrayal requires that there be a trust that was betrayed. Yes, there is the first trust, which is the trust of moral responsibility, about which Allah said: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it, and man bore it...﴾ (72) [al-Ahzab]. He betrayed this trust after he consented to be fit for it.

And there is a trust before this, which is the covenant that Allah took from His servants while they were in the stage of the atoms (al-dharr)(1): ﴿And [mention] when your Lord took from the children of Adam – from their loins – their descendants and made them testify concerning themselves, [saying], "Am I not your Lord?" They said, "Yes, we have testified." [This] – lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were of this unaware," (172) or say, "Indeed, our fathers associated [others with Allah] before, and we were [only] descendants after them..."(173) [al-A'raf].

If they say: Yes, this is a trust, but it is distant, and who among us remembers it now?

We say: Did you not acknowledge that Allah created you, brought you into being from nothing, and sustained you from nothing? As He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created them?" they would surely say, "Allah..."﴾ (87) [al-Zukhruf]. And they acknowledged that Allah, mighty and majestic, created the heavens and the earth and what is in them of good things. So the fulfilment of this acknowledgment should have been that they believe, but despite all this they disbelieved. Is this not a betrayal of the trust, which they all witnessed, experienced, and took part in?

And the kafur (ingrate) is one who denies and rejects the blessings of Allah.

As long as there are the treacherous and the ingrate, the heavens must support their Messenger and grant him victory in this battle first, by permitting him to fight; then by commanding him to take up the equipment and the means that lead to victory. If matters become difficult for you, then I am with you, supporting you with soldiers from Me.

This happened at the beginning of the call: Allah supported His Prophet with soldiers from Him(3). Indeed, He supported him even through a stubborn disbeliever: was not the guide(4) of the Messenger of Allah on the migration a disbeliever? Did He not support him with the dove and the spider while he was in the cave? Did He not support him with the earth that swallowed the hooves of the horse of Suraqah(5) who went out in pursuit of him?

These are soldiers we did not see, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was not supported with them except after he had exhausted his means. Had Allah willed, He would have made those stubborn opponents submissive to His Messenger, and not one of them would have raised his head in defiance of Muhammad. Rather, the Truth, blessed and exalted, wants to give him obedience willingly, and for the people to submit to him. Did He not say, glorified is He and exalted: ﴿If We willed, We could send down upon them a sign from the heaven, and their necks would remain bowed to it.﴾ (4) [al-Shu'ara'].

We have said: Allah, exalted is He, wants to subdue the hearts of His servants, not their bodies. Had Allah subdued them with a natural cosmic sign, such as a wind, a thunderbolt, or a landslide, or any other sign that seized their like among the earlier peoples, they would have said: these are natural calamities that came upon us. But Allah placed this confrontation between the two parties, then facilitated for His party and soldiers the means of victory.

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and disgrace them and give you victory over them and satisfy the breasts of a believing people.﴾ (14) [al-Tawbah].

1 - Al-dharr in the language: the small ants, its singular being dharrah. Dhara Allah al-khalq fi'l-ard: He scattered the creation on the earth. And al-dhurriyyah is derived from it, being related to al-dharr, which is the small ants. [Lisan al-Arab, root: dh-r-r].
2 - Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir (2/261): "Narrations have come concerning the taking of the offspring from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, and distinguishing them into the companions of the right and the companions of the left, and in some of them the calling to witness against them that Allah is their Lord... Some of the predecessors and successors have said that the intended meaning of this witnessing is only their being created upon monotheism."
3 - Allah, exalted, said: ﴿When you asked your Lord for help, and He answered you, "Indeed, I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another."(9) And Allah did not make it except as good tidings and so that your hearts would be assured thereby. And victory is not except from Allah...(10)﴾ [al-Anfal]. And in other verses Allah, exalted, says: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr when you were weak. So fear Allah that you may be grateful.(123) [Recall] when you said to the believers, "Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?"(124) Yes, if you are patient and fear Allah and they come at you in this, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels marked [for battle].(125)﴾ [Al 'Imran].
4 - He is 'Abd Allah ibn Urayqit, a man of the Banu al-Dil ibn Bakr. His mother was a woman of the Banu Sahm ibn 'Amr. He was a polytheist who guided them both on the road, and they had given him their two mounts, which he kept for them until their appointed time. [Sirah Ibn Hisham 2/485].
5 - He is Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum al-Mudlaji al-Kinani, a Companion who had poetry. He used to dwell in Qudayd. In the Jahiliyyah he was a qa'if (one who tracks footprints). Abu Sufyan sent him to track the footsteps of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he went out to the cave with Abu Bakr. He embraced Islam after the Battle of Ta'if in the year 8 AH. He died in 24 AH. [al-A'lam by al-Zirikli 3/80].

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Permission is given to those who are fought against, because they have been wronged. And indeed, Allah is able to give them victory.﴾ (22:39)

The defence of the Truth by Allah, glory be to Him, takes several forms. The first of this defence is that He permitted them to fight. Second, He commanded them to prepare strength for battle: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war...﴾ (8:60).

What is meant is that they should take up every means of victory over their enemy and exhaust all the means they have. If they have exhausted their means, would I then intervene with troops from Me that you do not see? The meaning of Allah defending those who believe is not that the heavens descend to protect them while they sit in their homes. No. Rather, they take up the causes of strength, strive, and first hasten to the causes of victory themselves.

The meaning of ﴿Permission is given﴾ (22:39) is that they had been waiting for the order to fight and were looking forward to victory over the enemies, but permission had not been given to them in this. So when Allah willed that they should fight, He gave them permission for it, and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Permission is given to those who are fought against, because they have been wronged. And indeed, Allah is able to give them victory.﴾ (22:39)

The reason for fighting is that they were wronged. Therefore their Lord, blessed and exalted is He, commanded them to fight, but not to transgress, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors.﴾ (2:190) ﴿And kill them wherever you overtake them and expel them from where they expelled you...﴾ (2:191)

So, first He commanded them to be patient, and in the first stage to fight to repel aggression and to defend themselves without transgressing. In the second stage He would say to them: ﴿O you who have believed, fight those adjacent to you of the disbelievers and let them find in you harshness. And know that Allah is with the righteous.﴾ (9:123)

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed, Allah is able to give them victory.﴾ (22:39): this is through causes that He enables you to use, or without causes, so that a hidden strength comes to them which they do not see; and indeed they have actually seen examples of that.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 40:

Then the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Those who have been expelled from their homes without right, only because they say, "Our Lord is Allah." And were it not that Allah checks one set of people by means of another, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches (1), oratories and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned. And Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Mighty.﴾ (40):

So, had they been expelled in truth, as if they had done something that called for their expulsion from their homes, such as violating modesty, threatening security, committing crimes, or rebelling against the laws of their tribes, then their expulsion would have been in truth.

But the reality is that they did nothing, and they have no sin, ﴿except that they say, "Our Lord is Allah"..﴾ (40) [al-Hajj]. This statement is what those people regarded as a sin and a crime that deserves that they be expelled from their homes because of it.

As He, glory be to Him, said about the People of the Trench: ﴿And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy﴾ (8) [al-Buruj].

And in another verse: ﴿Do you resent us except that we believed in Allah..﴾ (59) [al-Ma'idah].

And in the story of Lot, peace be upon him: ﴿They said, "Expel the family of Lot from your town. Indeed, they are men who keep themselves pure."﴾ (56) [an-Naml].

So, they expelled them not because they were people of impurity and disobedience, but because they are people who keep themselves pure. Purity and chastity were their crime for which they were expelled, just as you say: "There is no fault in so-and-so except that he is generous," or you say: "There is no honor in so-and-so except that he is a thief." This, then, is a quality that is not praised, and that is a quality that is not blamed.

These people reversed the scales and opposed sound nature with these corrupt judgments, which indicate the corruption of their dispositions. And what corruption is greater than that, after they reversed the standards, disliking what should be loved and loving what should be disliked? And nothing indicates the corruption of their natures more than their worship of a stone and their abandonment of the worship of the Creator of the heavens and the earth.

Then the Exalted says: ﴿And were it not that Allah checks one set of people by means of another, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, oratories and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned..﴾ (40) [al-Hajj].

In another verse, the Truthful One, glory be to Him, shows the result of the absence of this checking: ﴿And were it not that Allah checks one set of people by means of another, the earth would have been corrupted..﴾ (251) [al-Baqarah].

Corruption, if it occurs among people in the movement of life, can be made good and remedied. But if corruption extends to the foundations of faithful certainty on earth, so that people reject what ties them to the heavens and demolish the places of worship, then this is the catastrophe and the corruption after which there is no reform. Thus the two verses depict a kind of extremity in corruption and a depth of crimes.

The earth is corrupted when this checking is absent. How? Suppose that a tyrannical despot in some land enslaves the people and drains their wealth, even their blood, with no one repelling him. Undoubtedly this will spread negligence and chaos in society, no one will strive beyond his capacity, and whoever works, his benefit goes to others. This is the beginning of corruption on earth.

If we say: "This is corruption among people in the movement of their lives, which can be set right later," then what about when corruption extends to places of obedience and worship, and cuts the bond between people and the heavens?

If the first corruption is capable of reform, the corruption of religion cannot be reformed, because you have ruined the scales that regulated the movement of life, so society becomes without a balance and without controls to refer back to.

We note in His statement: ﴿And were it not that Allah checks one set of people by means of another..﴾ (40) [al-Hajj]: it came as a general matter for all people. He did not specify one group over another. He did not say, for example, "Were it not that Allah checks the disbelievers by means of the believers," but He said "people" in general, because it is a general matter in which all are equal in every society.

Likewise, the word "some" (ba'd) came general, to indicate that each of the two parties may at one time be the one checked and at another time the one checking. They lie in wait for one another: whoever corrupts is confronted by the other, who stops him at his limit. So the meaning is not that one group checks another all the time.

An example of this is His statement: ﴿And We raised some of them above others in degrees..﴾ (32) [az-Zukhruf], without specifying which is raised and which is raised over, because each of them is raised in one matter and raised over in another matter. This is because all the servants are the dependents of Allah, and He does not favor any of them over another.

Now look at the power of Russia in the East and the power of America in the West. They are an example of His statement: ﴿And were it not that Allah checks one set of people by means of another..﴾ (40) [al-Hajj]. Each of them lies in wait for the other, watching its movements and military advance, as if Allah, the Exalted, has made them, for the protection of the safety of others, such that each stands in a position of caution and fear of the other.

This fear, watchfulness and preparation is what prevents war from breaking out between them. What then if war were to take place between them, resulting in a victor and a vanquished? Certainly the victor would spread corruption in the land and dominate the others, and his oppression would spread for lack of anyone to restrain him.

Among the mercies of Allah toward the believers is that He plots against the wrongdoers by means of wrongdoers in all their forms and varieties, and disciplines the wrongdoer by one who is more wrongdoing than he, so that the people of goodness remain far from this battle, not entering any side of it, because the righteous cannot withstand these operations, for they are people of tender hearts, unsuited to this harshness and severity in revenge.

Read the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And thus do We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others for what they used to earn.﴾ (129) [al-An'am]. Thus Allah protects the people of goodness, preserves their blood, and relieves His friends of such futile conflicts.

Therefore, when the Prophet (ﷺ) entered Makkah as a victor, after his people had expelled him from it, and after they had done to him and his companions their abominations, how did he enter it, being the victorious commander who had gained mastery over the necks of his enemies?

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered Makkah with his head bowed low, so that his head nearly touched the curved front of the saddle upon which he sat, out of humility on his part (ﷺ). Nevertheless, Abu Sufyan, when he saw the Messenger in this position, said to al-Abbas: "The kingdom of your nephew has become mighty."

And after the Messenger had gained power over the disbelievers of Makkah, and he was able to destroy them all, he said: "O assembly of Quraysh, what do you think I will do with you?" They said: "A generous brother and a generous nephew." He said: "Go, for you are the freed ones (al-Tulaqa')" (4).

What mercy is this! And what gentleness is this that Allah placed in the hearts of the believers! Would such a religion be opposed and turned away from?

So: the Truthful, blessed and exalted, sets the wicked upon one another, and this is a sign we see in wrongdoers in every time and place, while the righteous sit watching such conflicts in which Allah destroys the wrongdoers by means of wrongdoers.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿...would have been demolished, monasteries and churches..﴾ (40) [al-Hajj]: "Sawami'" is the plural of "saw'ama" (ṣawmaʿa), which is a special place of worship for Christians. Their general place of worship that everyone enters is the church (kana'is). As for the saw'ama, it is a special place where its occupant withdraws alone and devotes himself to worship. The saw'ama is not in settled areas; it is in mountains and valleys, far from habitation, so that the monk cuts himself off from the movement of people's lives. These are what they call monasteries, and they are found in remote places.

Islam has forbidden monasticism in this sense, because it is a monasticism that Allah did not prescribe, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿But monasticism they invented; We did not prescribe it for them, except seeking the pleasure of Allah, but they did not observe it with its proper observance..﴾ (27) [al-Hadid].

The meaning of "and churches (biya')" (40) [al-Hajj]: "biya'" are the churches.

So the Exalted does not criticize them for devoting themselves to worship, but He criticizes them for cutting themselves off from the movement of life and the means of livelihood. Therefore He said: ﴿But they did not observe it with its proper observance..﴾ (27) [al-Hadid].

Islam has also permitted monasticism and withdrawal for worship, but on condition that it be in openness, meaning among people, not withdrawing from the movement of life. Rather, you worship Allah in every movement of your life, and you keep Allah always in your mind and before your eyes in all that you do and all that you leave undone. Thus there is a difference between one who worships Allah in his seclusion and one who worships Allah in his public life.

Therefore, our master 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said about a man who devoted himself to the mosque for worship, and it was known that his brother supported him and spent on him: "His brother is more devout than he." How so?

They said: "Because you can make every movement of your life an act of worship, when you purify your intention in it for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And you may compare a believer and a disbeliever: both work and strive to provide for themselves and their households, and to live a dignified life, and this is the aim of everyone in work. But if the believer limited his work to this aim, he would be exactly equal to the disbeliever.

Rather, the believer has beyond this other aims that lie in his intention and conscience. The believer acts according to his capacity, not according to his need. Then he takes what he needs and spends from the remainder, and gives charity to those who cannot take part in the movement of life."

Therefore the Truthful One, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Successful indeed are the believers, who are humble in their prayer, and who turn away from ill speech, and who are active in giving zakah﴾ (1-4) [al-Mu'minun]. Does it mean only "those who pay"? No. Rather the believer moves, works and strives, and in his intention is the one who cannot strive or work. So he sets himself to work and strive, and in his intention is to do something for Allah with what overflows from his needs from the product of his work. This is what distinguishes the believer in the movement of life from the disbeliever.

I recall once that we came from the countryside in winter in the 1930s to visit our master Shaykh al-Hafiz al-Tijani, and he was ill, may Allah have mercy on him and be pleased with him. He lived in an alley. We preferred to take a taxi to bring us, rather than walk through the winter mud. At the entrance of the alley the taxi driver refused to enter, saying that the fare for the drive would not cover washing the car and cleaning it of this mud. After insistence he agreed and brought us to where we wanted to go. We gave him double his fare. But before I left, I said to him: "Why do you work with this taxi, and why do you exhaust yourself?" He said: "For my own interests and the interests of my children." I said: "What would harm you if you added to that and made it your intention to ease people's burdens through this work of yours?" The man was moved, and the word affected him, and he said: "By Allah, I will never turn away a rider again."

As for the meaning of "and who are active in giving zakah (3)" (al-Mu'minun): He did not say "those who pay," because "fa'iluna" (active, doers) (4) means that their intention in the act is to act according to their capacity and to strive to set aside something beyond their expenses, from which they give charity.

Therefore, Islam forbade the monasticism that deprives society of a person's participation. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no monasticism in Islam." (7) Because it regarded every movement intended for the good of the whole society as a faithful, worshipful movement. From this, work is worship.

The scholars set conditions for one who wishes to devote himself to worship. The first of them: that he not take his maintenance from anyone, meaning that he work first to secure his needs for the duration of his seclusion. And Iqbal spoke truly when he said:

"It is not asceticism when one of piety withdraws from the turmoil of life through religion;
Sufism is recognized in the market by wealth, ambition and temptation."

Then the Exalted says: ﴿...and oratories (salawat) (40) [al-Hajj]: this is for the Jews, who call their place of worship "salwata" (ṣalūtā). But why did the Qur'an not order them chronologically, saying "monasteries, oratories and churches"? They said: because the Qur'an narrates from the near to the far.

﴿And mosques (40) [al-Hajj]: this is for the Muslims, ﴿in which the name of Allah is much mentioned (40) [al-Hajj].

Since the Truthful One mentioned the mosques after the act ﴿would have been demolished (40) [al-Hajj], this is evidence that the Muslims must have a place set aside for worship, even if the whole earth has been made for them a mosque and a means of purification. This means that you may pray in any spot on earth, and if water is unavailable you purify yourself with its dust. Thus the earth becomes a place of worship and a place of the movement of life, of work and of striving. You may carry out your work in your factory, for example, and pray in it. But the Truthful One wants us to set apart some of His earth to be a house for Him, from which the whole movement of life is cut off, and which is dedicated only to the affairs of the servants.

1 - "Bi'ah": the church of the Christians, plural "biya'," as Ibn 'Abbas said, related by 'Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir. He also said: "Sawami'" are those in which the monks dwell, and "biya'" are the synagogues of the Jews. "Salawat" are the churches of the Christians, and "masajid" are the mosques of the Muslims. [al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti 6/59].
2 - "Al-qurbus": the curved front of the saddle. The "hanw" (curve) of anything is its crookedness. So the hanw of the saddle and the rahl is every crooked stick among its wood. [Lisan al-'Arab, entries: qurbas, hanaa]. Ibn Hisham in the Sirah (4/405) mentioned "that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would lower his head in humility to Allah when he saw what Allah had honored him with of the conquest, until his 'uthnun (the edge of his beard) almost touched the middle of the saddle."
3 - Abu Sufyan said, when the armies of the Muslims passed before him on the day of the conquest of Makkah: "No one has the power or strength against these people. By Allah, O Abu al-Fadl, the kingdom of your nephew has become mighty this morning." Al-'Abbas said: "O Abu Sufyan, it is prophethood." He said: "Then yes."
4 - Ibn Ishaq said: Some people of knowledge related to me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood at the door of the Ka'bah in his address and said: "There is no god but Allah alone, without partner. He fulfilled His promise, supported His servant, and defeated the confederates alone..." until he said: "What do you think I will do with you?" They said: "Good. A generous brother and a generous nephew." He said: "Go, for you are the freed ones." [Sirah of Ibn Hisham 4/412].
5 - "Tarahhub": worship. They practiced tarahhub by withdrawing from the concerns of the world, abandoning its pleasures, renouncing it, isolating themselves from its people, and taking upon themselves its hardships, to the extent that some of them would castrate themselves, put a chain around their necks, and other kinds of torment. The "rahib" is the one who worships in the saw'ama. [Lisan al-'Arab, entry: rahiba].
6 - That is: they did not carry out what they had committed to with its proper observance. This is a censure of them in two respects: first, innovating in the religion of Allah what Allah did not command; second, not fulfilling what they had committed to, which they claimed was a means of drawing near to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Said by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (4/315).
7 - Al-'Ajluni said in Kashf al-Khafa' (3154): "Ibn Hajar said: I have not seen it with this wording, but in the hadith of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas in al-Bayhaqi: 'Allah has replaced for us monasticism with the upright, easy religion.' And Ahmad in his Musnad (6/226) narrated from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Monasticism was not prescribed for us.'"

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 22, verse 41:

When victory has been achieved for you, know that you have a role to play, namely:

﴿Those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer, give zakat, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. And with Allah rests the outcome of all matters.﴾

The meaning of ﴿We establish them in the land﴾: We give them authority, strength and dominance, so that no one dares to challenge them or dislodge them. They must know that Allah did not empower and support them for their own sake, but so that they might carry out the task of reform (islah) and purify the human vicegerency (khilafah) on earth of everything that weakens its righteousness or corrupts it.

Therefore, Prophet Sulayman (peace be upon him) used to ride the flying carpet which carried him wherever he wished. Something of self-admiration (zahw) entered him, so the carpet swayed with him and nearly threw him off. Then he heard the carpet say to him: "We were commanded to obey you only as long as you obey Allah."

The one empowered on earth, whom Allah has given might, strength and authority, can impose on his society whatever he wills. Even if he is empowered on earth in falsehood, he can impose his falsehood and subject people to it, though only for a time.

So what is entrusted to the believer if he is empowered on earth?

The Exalted says: ﴿Those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer...﴾: so that they may always remain mindful of and loyal to their Lord, who granted them this empowerment, because they return to Him, glorified is He, five times a day and night.

﴿And give zakat, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾: these are the foundations of righteousness in society and the balance by which everyone is made happy.

﴿And with Allah rests the outcome of all matters﴾: meaning, the final return is to Us, and the ultimate destination is with Us.
