Whoever adheres to these directives and fulfils his assigned role in his society, then how excellent that is; and whoever casts them behind his back, his end is well known.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 22, verse 42:

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, consoles His Messenger (ﷺ) so that he does not worry about what his people do of disbelief, obstinacy, and opposition to the call.

{And if they deny you, then the people of Noah, and 'Ad, and Thamud had denied [their messengers] before them} (42):

﴿They deny you...﴾ (42) [al-Hajj]: meaning, in your call, so that they confront you, and stand in the way of your call in order to nullify it. Know, then, that in this you are not an innovation among the messengers, for many messengers denied before you. And you must not consider the matter of denial separately from its outcome. Yes, the people denied, but how was the outcome? Did We leave them, or did We seize them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Able?

So do not grieve, for there will befall them what befell those who denied and opposed before them.

We have said that the Messenger bears hardship of the message and toil of the call in proportion to his message. Every messenger of Allah before Muhammad was sent only to his own people, for a limited period and a limited time, and despite that they exerted themselves greatly in the cause of their call. So what of a messenger who was sent to all mankind, in every time and every place? Without doubt he will bear exertion and toil many times over what his brother messengers before him bore.

It is as if Allah, blessed and exalted, is preparing His Messenger (ﷺ) and accustoming him to bear hardships from the start of the path, so that his resolve is not broken when he confronts them at the outset of the call. He says to him: Leadership is not an easy matter; behind it lie troubles, terrors and hardships, so prepare yourself. Just as a father alerts his son: "Be attentive, for the examinations will be difficult this year, since the ministry wants to reduce the number of applicants to the university, so strive hard to obtain a high total." When the son hears this warning, he gathers his steadiness and gathers his focus, and so he does not waver when he faces the examinations.

Then Allah, blessed and exalted, mentions examples of those who denied the messengers: {the people of Noah, and 'Ad, and Thamud} (42) [al-Hajj].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 43:

Then the Exalted says:

﴿And the people of Abraham and the people of Lot, and the companions of Madyan. And Moses was denied. So I granted respite to the disbelievers, then I seized them; and how was My disapproval?﴾

We notice here that the Truthful One (al-Haqq) mentioned the deniers as groups, except in the story of Moses, where He mentioned the one who denied. He did not say "the people of Moses" but said "and Moses was denied." Why? They said: because his mission was harder, since in his call he confronted one who claimed divinity itself.

As for His saying, ﴿So I granted respite to the disbelievers, then I seized them...﴾ [al-Hajj]: "amlaytu" (I granted respite) means: I gave them time until they thought it was neglect. It is a respite in which Allah extends for them and lengthens their term, not as an honour to them, but so that He may seize them afterwards with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent. In another verse He clarifies this brief telegram for us, saying:

﴿And let not those who disbelieve suppose that Our granting them respite is good for their souls. We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin...﴾ [Al 'Imran].

In this same meaning He also says: ﴿So let not their wealth nor their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them thereby in the worldly life, and that their souls should depart while they are disbelievers﴾ [al-Tawbah].

So: do not be deceived by what is in their hands, for it is a trial; so that when Allah seizes them, their regret will be greater. Whoever is deprived of these blessings, his heart does not become attached to them, and he does not grieve over their loss.

Something of this happened in the days of Sa'd Zaghloul. One of his opponents used to insult him and attack him, but everyone was surprised when he appointed him to a prominent post in Cairo. People wondered and asked him about it, and he said: Yes, I placed him in this post so that he would know高 rank and standing, so that he would regret it when it is taken from him, and it would be more painful to him. That is: he raises him high so that he falls on his neck, for what is the benefit of dropping him from the mat, for example?

Then the Exalted says: ﴿How was My disapproval?﴾ [al-Hajj]: the Truthful One presents the report in the form of a question, so that you may state what happened and bear witness to it. The meaning is: Did We punish them with what they deserved?

And "nakir" is disapproval directed at a person by changing his state from blessing to vengeance, like one who honours you, comforts you, greets you cheerfully and showers you with favours, then cuts all of this off from you, so you say: Why has so-and-so turned against me? That is: he cut off his blessing from me.

It is as if the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted wants to draw from us an acknowledgement of His power to punish His enemies and the deniers of His messengers. This meaning also came in His saying:

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would wink at one another. And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are misguided." But they had not been sent as watchers over them. So today, those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, looking on. Have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin]: meaning, were the disbelievers repaid for what they did? And were We able to punish them with the torment they deserved?

﴿How was My disapproval?﴾ [al-Hajj]: that is, My disapproval of their stance of not fulfilling the rights of blessing, so Allah replaced it for them with vengeance.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 44:

Then the Exalted says:

﴿And the people of Abraham and the people of Lot, and the companions of Madyan. And Moses was denied. So I granted respite to the disbelievers, then I seized them, and how was My disapproval?﴾

We note here that Allah, glory be to Him, mentioned the deniers [of their messengers] in the form of peoples, except in the story of Moses, where He mentioned the one who denied: He did not say "the people of Moses" but said "and Moses was denied." Why? They said: because his mission was harder, since in his call he confronted one who claimed divinity itself.

As for His saying, ﴿So I granted respite to the disbelievers, then I seized them...﴾ [al-Hajj]: "amlaytu" (I granted respite) means I gave time, until they thought it was neglect. It is a respite in which Allah extends for them and lengthens their term, not as an honour to them, but so that He may seize them after this with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent. In another verse He clarifies this brief telegram, saying, glory be to Him:

﴿And let not those who disbelieve suppose that Our giving them respite is good for themselves. We only give them respite that they may increase in sin...﴾ [Al 'Imran: 178].

In this same sense He also says:

﴿So let not their wealth or their children impress you. Allah only intends to punish them thereby in the life of this world, and that their souls depart while they are disbelievers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 55].

So: do not be deceived by what is in their hands, for it is a trial, so that when Allah seizes them their regret will be greater. Whoever is deprived of these blessings does not have his heart attached to them, nor is he pained by their loss.

Something of this happened in the days of Sa'd Zaghlul. One of his opponents used to insult him and act arrogantly towards him, but everyone was surprised when he appointed him to a prominent post in Cairo. The people wondered and asked him about it, and he said: Yes, I placed him in this post so that he would know high standing and rank, and then he would grieve over it when it is taken from him, and it would be more painful to him. That is: he raises him high so that he falls upon his neck, for what is the benefit in dropping him from the mat, for example?

Then the Exalted says: ﴿So how was My disapproval?﴾ [al-Hajj]: Allah, glory be to Him, presents the report in the form of a question so that you may say what happened and bear witness to it. The meaning is: Did We punish them with what they deserved?

"Nakir" (disapproval) is disapproval of a person by changing his state from blessing to punishment, like one who honours you, comforts you, greets you cheerfully and showers you with favours, then cuts all of this off from you, so you say: "Why has so-and-so turned against me?" That is: he has withdrawn his blessing from me.

It is as if the Truth, blessed and exalted be He, wants to extract from us the acknowledgement of His power to punish His enemies and the deniers of His messengers. This meaning also comes in His saying:

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they winked at one another. And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are the astray." But they had not been sent as guardians over them. So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, looking on. Have the disbelievers been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 29-36]: That is: Were the disbelievers recompensed for what they did? And were We able to punish them with what they deserved of torment?

﴿So how was My disapproval?﴾ [al-Hajj]: That is: My disapproval of their stance of not fulfilling the rights of blessing, so Allah replaced it for them with punishment.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿So how many a city have We destroyed while it was wrongdoing, and it is now fallen upon its roofs, and [many] a well abandoned and a lofty palace.﴾ (45)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So how many a city…﴾ (45) [al-Hajj]: "Ka'ayyin" (how many) is a particle indicating multiplicity, like the interrogative-exclamatory "kam" when you say: "Kam ahsantu ilayka" (how many times I have done good to you), meaning countless times, so it expresses exaggeration in number and quantity. Among its occurrences is His saying: ﴿And how many a prophet fought, with him many devoted servants…﴾ (146) [Al 'Imran].

And "al-qaryah" (the city)(1) is the name of a place, and when God destroys a city, He does not destroy the place; rather, He destroys its inhabitant within it. Thus, what is meant by "al-qaryah" is its people, as in His saying: ﴿And ask the city in which we were…﴾ (82) [Yusuf]: that is, ask the people of the city.

It may also mean: ask the city and it will inform you, because if you asked the people of the city, they might lie, whereas the city records events and reports them as they happened.

Destruction may also extend to the city itself, altering its features, as in His saying: ﴿So those are their houses, ruined because of what they did wrong.﴾ (52) [al-Naml].

The meaning of ﴿…We destroyed while it was wrongdoing…﴾ (45) [al-Hajj] is: because of its wrongdoing. God does not change what is with a people until they change what is in themselves. In another verse He says: ﴿And Allah presents an example: a city that was secure and tranquil, its provision coming to it in abundance from every place, but it denied the favors of Allah, so Allah made it taste the envelopment of hunger and fear for what they had been doing.﴾ (112) [al-Nahl].

So the destruction of cities must have a cause. When destruction befell it, it became ﴿fallen upon its roofs…﴾ (45) [al-Hajj]. Something "khawiyah" (fallen) is that which has collapsed and fallen upon other things. His saying ﴿upon its roofs…﴾ (45) [al-Hajj] indicates the magnitude of the destruction that befell it, where the roof fell first and then the walls collapsed upon it. Or it means that God overturned it upside down, making its top its bottom.

His saying, glorified is He: ﴿and [many] a well abandoned…﴾ (45) [al-Hajj]: "al-bi'r" (the well) is the deep cavity in the earth, reaching the level of the underground water, from which people draw water for drinking, for irrigation, and so on. Among its occurrences is His saying: ﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan…﴾ (23) [al-Qasas]: that is, the well from which they drink.

When a well is in use and benefited from, signs of life are visible around it: people gather around it, plants grow on the traces of the water drawn from it, and birds hover around it to drink. But an abandoned, unused well is found desolate, with no signs of life. Winds may blow over it and bury it (2), so it is disabled and forsaken. The meaning of "mu'attalah" (abandoned) is disabled from performing its function, and the function of a well is giving drink.

﴿And lofty palace﴾ (45) [al-Hajj]: "al-qasr" (palace) is the name for a splendid dwelling. A shelter may be a tent, a pavilion, a hut, a house, or a building. When a person rises in his dwelling and builds for himself something special to him, he must still go out to meet the necessities of life such as food and the like. But a palace is a place of residence that provides within it everything you need, so that you do not need to go out of it; that is, within it are all the requirements of life. From this root the houris were called "maqsurat" in His saying: ﴿Houris restrained in pavilions﴾ (72) [al-Rahman], meaning they do not go beyond them or leave them.

And "mashid" (lofty) (45) [al-Hajj] derives from "al-shid," which is the lime used as mortar in building stone, that is, the material for adhering stones and bringing them to one level. In earlier times construction was with mud brick, with mortar made of clay, whereas in palaces and fine, elevated dwellings construction is with stone. "Mashid" also means high and raised; from it comes the saying "ashada bihi," meaning he raised him and elevated his status. Height is a characteristic of palaces. It is well known that room dimensions in apartment buildings, for example, differ from those in palaces: the former are narrow and low, while the latter are spacious and high.

In His saying: ﴿and lofty palace﴾ (45) [al-Hajj] there is evidence that those who were destroyed were people of wealth and luxury, dwellers of palaces and of the elite of their people.

1 - Al-qaryah: a large town, smaller than a city, or every place to which buildings are joined. [al-Qamus al-Qawim 2/115].
2 - Safat al-rih al-turab: it scattered it; it was said: it carried it. Al-safya': the wind that carries much dust over the surface of the earth and sweeps it onto people. [Lisan al-Arab, root: s-f-a].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 46:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿Have they not travelled through the earth, so that they might have hearts with which to understand, or ears with which to hear? For indeed it is not the eyes that grow blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that grow blind.﴾ (46)

Al-sayr (travel): crossing distances from one place to another; they call it siyaha (touring). Allah, glorified is He, calls His servants to travel throughout the earth, because travel has two benefits:

Either it is travel for investment, to seek provision, if you are in a place where life is constricted for you, like those who travel to other lands for work and to seek provision.

Or it is travel to take a lesson and to reflect upon the creatures of Allah in His vast dominion, so that one may draw evidence from the creation of Allah and His signs for His power, exalted is He.

Travel through different lands gives you the opportunity to notice the differences from one environment to another: this is hot and that is cold, this is a barren desert and that is green with not a grain of sand. Therefore our Lord, blessed and exalted is He, addresses us: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth, then observe...﴾ (11) [al-An'am].

The conjunction in the verse with (thumma, "then") indicates that travel has another purpose, namely investment and seeking provision. So the verse alludes to combining these two purposes: when you go to work, beware of neglecting the signs of Allah in the place you travelled to, and take from it a cosmic lesson that benefits you in your religion.

In another verse He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth, then look...﴾ (69) [al-Naml].

The conjunction here is with (fa, "so"), which indicates sequence; meaning: travel through the earth so that you may look upon the signs of Allah. This is specifically for travel of contemplation and reflection, not travel for investment and seeking provision.

Therefore they say in proverbs: "Whoever lives, sees much; and whoever walks, sees more." Thus, the more places there are, the more signs and wonders there are that indicate the power of Allah. You may see a sight that does not affect you, and see another that shakes you and moves your emotions and your reflections on the universe.

As for His saying: ﴿Have they not travelled...﴾ (46) [al-Hajj]: it means and affirms that they had actually travelled, as you say: "Have I not honoured you?" You would only say this if you had indeed honoured him. It did happen that they actually travelled in the lands during the winter and summer journeys, and they used to pass by the dwellings of the people who were destroyed, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning﴾ (137) [al-Saffat].

Meaning: you are people of travel and journeying, and people who look at the fate of those before you, so how can you accept turning away from the signs of Allah?

﴿Have they not travelled through the earth, so that they might have hearts with which to understand, or ears with which to hear? For indeed it is not the eyes that grow blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that grow blind.﴾ (46) [al-Hajj]: Since they have travelled and journeyed through the lands, how do they not understand the signs of Allah? And how do their hearts not stir?

We pause at His saying: ﴿so that they might have hearts with which to understand...﴾ (46) [al-Hajj]: Can a person understand with his heart? It is known that the intellect ('aql) is in the brain, and the heart is in the chest.

Yes, a human has means of perception, which are the senses that receive sensible objects; out of courtesy to knowledge they are called the apparent five senses. For science has established for the human, in the functions of the organs, other senses that are not apparent. When you hold two different things, you can distinguish which of them is heavier than the other. By which of the five well-known senses did you reach this conclusion?

If you say by the eye, then put it on the ground and look at it. If you say by touch, you may touch it without lifting it from its place. Therefore, you do not perceive weight by these senses, but by something else and by another instrument of perception, namely the sense of muscle which distinguishes for you the light from the heavy.

When you go to buy a piece of cloth and rub the cloth gently between your fingers, you can distinguish the thick from the thin, although the difference between them hardly deserves mention. By which sense did you perceive it? It is the sense of pressure (al-bayn). Likewise there is the sense of distance and other senses that modern science discovers in the human.

When a person perceives these things through the means of perception, the intellect intervenes to sift these perceptions and choose from among the alternatives what suits him. If he is going to choose a garment, he says: "This is softer and finer than that." If he is going to choose a scent, he says: "This is more delicate than that." If it is summer he chooses the light, and if it is winter he chooses the thick.

After the intellect chooses and weighs the alternatives, it passes judgment on a matter that settles in the mind, and you become convinced of it. It no longer requires perception after that, nor choice between alternatives. Then you accept what has settled in your soul and what your heart has come to rest upon.

Thus: perception by the senses, discernment by the intellect, and standing at a principle by the heart. Once the principle has settled in your heart, it becomes a constitution for your life, and all your limbs serve this principle at which you have arrived and which has settled in your heart and conscience.

But why the heart in particular? They said: because the heart is what performs the pumping of the fluid of life, which is blood, to all parts of the body and its limbs. These limbs are the instrument of executing what has settled in the conscience. Therefore they said: faith has its locus in the heart. How? They said: because you have sifted the matters and purified the issues until the creed and faith settled in your heart. Faith, or creed, is what has been firmly established in the heart and settled in it. From the heart, the creed extends to all the organs and senses, which act in accordance with this faith. Since you have arrived at a principle and creed, beware of deviating from it to something else, or else your heart has not understood and has not comprehended.

The phrase ﴿they might have hearts with which to understand﴾ (46) [al-Hajj] indicates that the intellect has other duties besides choosing and distinguishing among alternatives. Among its duties is that it restrains its possessor from error, and holds him back from wandering into labyrinths. Some think that "intellect" ('aql) means freedom of thought, and that a person may let his mind roam among ideas as he wishes. No: the intellect is from the ʿiqal (tether) of the camel, which restrains it and keeps it from straying from you.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿or ears with which to hear﴾ (46) [al-Hajj]: How, when these people have ears that hear? Yes, they have ears that hear, but it is hearing without benefit, as if the sense did not exist. For what is the use of something you heard but did not benefit from and did not put to use in the movement of your life? It is hearing like its absence; indeed its absence is better than it, because your hearing establishes the proof against you.

﴿For indeed it is not the eyes that grow blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that grow blind.﴾ (46) [al-Hajj]: The blindness of the eyes is a light matter compared with the blindness of the hearts(1), because when a person loses sight he can still hear, use his intellect, and be guided, and what he cannot see with his eyes can be told to him by another, who describes it to him precisely as if he saw it. But what is to be done when the hearts are blinded while the sights are seeing?

If blindness of the eyes has a substitute and compensation, what is the substitute when the heart is blinded? The blind man tries to feel his way, and if he fails he says to you: "Take my hand." But what does the blind-hearted man do?

Therefore, we say of one who neglects the clear matter and the settled principle: "He is blind of heart." That is, a seal has been set upon his heart, so he understands nothing.

As for His saying: ﴿the hearts within the breasts﴾ (46) [al-Hajj]: It is known that hearts are in the breasts, so why was the expression phrased this way? They said: to affirm for you that the intended meaning is the real heart, lest you think it is the thinking, rational heart, as in His saying: ﴿They say with their mouths﴾ (167) [Al 'Imran].

It is known that saying comes from the mouths, but He intended to emphasise speech and utterance, because speech may be by signs and indication, so speech by words is the most eloquent and most emphatic kind of speech. Therefore the poet said:

"The wounds of the spear have a way of healing, but the wound the tongue inflicts never heals."

And they say: "Guard your tongue, which is between your jaws." Is the tongue anything but between the jaws? But He intended to emphasise speech and utterance specifically, not the other means of understanding and expression.

1 - Qatada said: "The penetrating sight is made for benefit and utility, and the beneficial sight is in the heart." Mujahid said: "Every eye has four eyes," meaning every person has four eyes: two eyes in his head for his worldly life, and two eyes in his heart for his afterlife. If the two eyes of his head go blind while the two eyes of his heart see, his blindness does not harm him at all; and if the two eyes of his head see while the two eyes of his heart are blind, his sight does not benefit him at all. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi 6/4608].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 47:

Then the Almighty says(1):

﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, but Allah will not fail His promise. Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.﴾ (47)

Did they not say, regarding the hastening of the punishment: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down on us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment﴾ (32) [al-Anfal].

And they said: ﴿Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful﴾ (70) [al-A'raf].

A person does not hasten punishment unless he does not believe in it. The one who truly believes in punishment fears it, and wishes to delay it or to escape it. The meaning of ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment..﴾ (47) [al-Hajj] is that they think that if Allah threatens them with punishment, it will fall upon them immediately. Therefore the Almighty corrects this understanding for them, saying: ﴿But Allah will not fail His promise. Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾ (47) [al-Hajj]. So do not hasten, for your threatened punishment will certainly befall you, because it is a promise from Allah, and Allah does not fail His promise. But know that a day with Allah is not like your day. Your day is twenty-four hours, but with Allah it is like a thousand years by your reckoning of days.

A day is a span of time that accommodates some events, and cannot contain more than what can be done in it. But a day with Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, contains many events that fill a thousand years of your days. That is because you engage in works and deal with them, whereas the Creator, glory be to Him, does not perform actions through treatment; rather, His command, when He wills something, is to say to it: "Be," and it is. Your action requires time, whereas your Lord's action is by the word "Be." Allah, the Almighty, has willed that these people live in the torment of contemplating this threat throughout their lives, so they are punished by it before it occurs.

So do not suppose that the punishment with which He threatens you will happen today or tomorrow. No, because the reckoning of time is different.

Have you not read the words of Allah, the Exalted, to His prophet Moses, peace be upon him, when he invoked against his people: ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts, so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment﴾ (88) [Yunus].

His Lord said to him: ﴿Your supplication has been answered..﴾ (89) [Yunus].

The commentators say: this answer came to Moses forty years after his supplication against them.(3)

In another place the Exalted says: ﴿He arranges the affair from the heaven to the earth; then it ascends to Him in a day the measure of which is a thousand years of what you count﴾ (5) [al-Sajdah].

This period increases in His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a day the measure of which is fifty thousand years﴾ (4) [al-Ma'arij]. Why? Because time for you in such a state is suspended: from the awe of what you see, you stretch out the short, and time passes heavily upon you, so you wish to be dismissed, even to the Fire.

Just as the one in bliss finds the long short, and time passes for him as the blink of an eye, and of this is what you notice: the time is short with loved ones and long with enemies and those your heart does not desire. There are many examples of this matter in our Arabic poetry, among them the saying of one of them:

The events of joy are weighed by weight, and afflictions are measured by the qafizan(4)

And the saying of another: My night did not lengthen, but I did not sleep; the phantom of pain drove off sleep from me.(5)

And Ibn Zaydun says:
If your absence lengthens my night, how often have I spent the night complaining of the shortness of the night with you.

1 - Occasion of revelation of the verse: al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir (6/4609): "It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, regarding his saying: ﴿Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful﴾ (70) [al-A'raf]. It was also said it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, regarding his saying ﴿Rain down on us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment﴾ (32) [al-Anfal]."
2 - al-Dahhak said: their dinars, dirhams, copper and iron became engraved stones. [al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti 4/384], and he attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh.
3 - Said by Mujahid as transmitted from him by al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi. Ibn Abbas said, as transmitted from him by Ibn al-Mundhir: they claim that Pharaoh remained forty years after this supplication. Both are cited by al-Suyuti in (al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/385).
4 - Al-qafizan: plural of qafiz, which is a unit of measure, and is a measure of land equal to one hundred and forty-four cubits. [Lisan al-Arab, root: q-f-z].
5 - This verse is by Bashshar ibn Burd. Cited by Abu Ali al-Qali in al-Amali (1/132). Al-kara: sleep, drowsiness.

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿And how many a town have I given respite while it was wrongdoing; then I seized it, and to Me is the final return.﴾

﴿And how many (كأين) (48)﴾ [al-Hajj]: We have said that it indicates multitude, meaning: many towns.

﴿Given respite (أمليت) (48)﴾ [al-Hajj]: given time (أمهلت). But prolonging the respite does not mean neglect, for Allah, exalted is He, gives the disbeliever respite and allows him a term. When the appointed term and the punishment come, He seizes him.

﴿Then I seized it (48)﴾ [al-Hajj]: The act of seizing is proportionate to the strength and power of the one who seizes, and to the severity of retribution according to the one who exacts it. When the one who seizes is Allah, mighty and majestic, how then will His seizing be?

In another verse He clarifies this, saying: ﴿The seizing of One Mighty, Capable (42)﴾ [al-Qamar]: none can overpower Him, and none can withhold anything from Him, and the word "seizing" carries the meaning of severity, vehemence and subjugation.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And to Me is the final return (48)﴾ [al-Hajj]: meaning the place of return and recourse, so they will not be able to escape.

So, al-imla' (إملاء, giving respite) is the postponement of punishment until a specified term, as He, glorified is He, says: ﴿So give the disbelievers respite; give them time for a little (17)﴾ [al-Tariq].

This term may be for a period, after which the punishment befalls them, as happened to the earlier nations whom Allah destroyed by being swallowed up by the earth or by drowning, etc. As for the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), the respite takes the form of superficial events in this world, such as the disgrace, humiliation and defeat that befell the disbelievers and the breaking of their power, while the true punishment awaits them in the Hereafter.

Therefore, the Truthful, blessed and exalted is He, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): Do not be impatient for their punishment and for retribution against them in this world, for what you do not see of punishment for them in this world, you will see in the Hereafter: ﴿Whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We take you (in death), then to Us they will be returned (77)﴾ [Ghafir].

Then the Truthful, glorified is He, says:

﴿Say: O mankind, I am only for you a clear warner.﴾ (22:49)

Warning is a form of mercy, for you inform a person of evil before its time, so that the one warned may take heed of it, try to save himself from it, and keep away from its causes. So when I remind you of God, and that He seizes His enemies with the seizure of the Mighty, the All-Powerful, then it is incumbent upon you to keep yourself far from this end, and to be saved from the causes of destruction.

And the meaning of ﴿clear﴾ [al-Hajj] is: encompassing, leaving out neither a small matter nor a great one.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 50:

﴿So those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is forgiveness and generous provision.﴾ (22:50)

Since they believed and did righteous deeds, they have benefited from the warning, and it has borne fruit in them. They believed in Allah as a God who acts by choice, possessing absolute perfect attributes, and then they acted in accordance with His commands. Therefore, for them there is forgiveness, should their souls have been touched by some acts of disobedience, and for them there is generous provision. The "karim" (generous) is the one who gives freely and abundantly, as if the provision itself reached them with generosity and increase. Just as the generous person is one whose hand is always extended with giving, in accordance with the saying of the poet:

"And I am a man whose dirhams never rest
In the palm, except as passing travellers."

Thus the provision itself is generous, because it is flowing and never cut off, just as if you take a cup of water from a running stream, and another replaces it immediately, and so on.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 51:

﴿And those who strive against Our verses, seeking to frustrate them, they are the companions of the Blazing Fire.﴾ :

Al-sa'y (striving): an action that proceeds toward an aim. If it is the covering of a distance, we say: "We travelled from such-and-such place to such-and-such place." If it is in an intellectual, scholarly matter, it means that the event proceeds from a beginning to an aim.

Striving is not praised absolutely, nor blamed absolutely. If it is in goodness, it is praiseworthy and commendable, like the striving of which God said: ﴿As for those, their striving is appreciated﴾ [al-Isra' 19]. If it is in evil, it is ugly and blameworthy, like the striving of which God Almighty said: ﴿And among the people is one whose speech about the worldly life impresses you, and he calls upon Allah to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents. And when he turns away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And Allah does not like corruption﴾ [al-Baqarah 204-205].

As for al-sa'aya (tale-bearing), it customarily takes the side of evil. It means: informing and going between people with malicious gossip. You say: "So-and-so is a tale-bearer among the people," meaning he carries evil from one person to another with the intent of harm. Such people, if they know good, they hide it; if they know evil, they spread it; and if they do not know, they lie.

Therefore, we say concerning the evil that results from this tale-bearing among people: this is the calamity of the one who takes it up, meaning the one who hears evil, transmits it and carries it about, when he should have restrained and concealed it, so that this vice does not spread among creation.

A tale-bearer once informed on Hammam ibn 'Abd Allah al-Sulami to Ziyad ibn Abihi, and Ziyad was a tyrant. He said to the informer: "Shall I bring you together with him?" The informer could find no way but to say: "Yes." How could he deny what he had said? Perhaps he said to himself: "Perhaps God will decree a matter that will extricate me from this predicament (al-wartah) before this confrontation." Then Ziyad sent for Ibn Hammam and he was brought. Ziyad had placed the informer in his assembly behind a curtain, and Hammam was admitted. He said to him: "O Hammam, it has reached me that you satirised me." He said: "Never, may God set you right, I did not do that, nor are you deserving of it." Ziyad uncovered the curtain and said: "This man told me that you satirised me." Ibn Hammam looked, and behold, it was a friend of his who sat with him. He said to him:

"You are a man: if I entrusted you in privacy, you betrayed; and if you say a saying without knowledge,
then you have turned the matter that was between us into a station between treachery and sin."(1)

That is: you are blameworthy in every state, for either you betrayed the trust of the gathering and the conversation, not keeping a secret I confided to you, or you fabricated this saying as a lie and without knowledge.

When Ziyad bestowed on Hammam a robe of honour (al-khal'ah)(2), yet he did not punish the informer. In this there is an indication of their contentment with the one who carries tales to them, and that their ears have become accustomed to it and familiar with it.

The meaning of ﴿in Our verses﴾ [al-Hajj 51]: the verses are either cosmic, like the sun and the moon, or miracles, or verses of legal rulings. "Striving in them" means they speak about them a false saying, other than the truth, just as the informer strives with falsehood among people. Such people, if they look at the verses of the cosmos, say: "It is the product of nature." If they witness a miracle at the hand of a prophet, they say: "Sorcery and the fables of the ancients." If they hear the verses of legal rulings recited, they say: "Poetry." By all this they wish to corrupt the faith of the people of belief and to turn them away from the way of God.

The meaning of ﴿frustrating [them]﴾ [al-Hajj 51]: "mu'ajizin" is the plural of the active participle "mu'ajiz", like "muqatil". It derives from "'ajaza" with a different sense: "'ajaza 'an kadha" means he was unable to do such-and-such, i.e., he did not have power over it. "'Ajaza fulanan" (he contested him) means he vied with him to see which of them would fall short before the other, so "'ajazahu" is like "barahu" (he competed with him) in order to establish that he is the superior, and like "sabaqahu" (he outran him) and "nafasahu" (he rivalled him).

Thus, al-mu'ajazah is a reciprocal action and participation. The root of the word "nafasahu" (he rivalled him) is the breath (nafas) that we take in with the inhalation and expel with the exhalation, and by which the blood is oxygenated and the movement of a human being continues. If breathing is prevented, he dies, for a human being can endure without food and can endure without water, but he cannot endure without air, not even for a single breath.

This contest or rivalry (mu'ajazah) occurred between our master 'Umar and our master al-'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both. 'Umar said to al-'Abbas: "Do you compete with me in water?" That is: we dive beneath the water and look to see which of us makes the other fall short, and which endures the stopping of breath. Such a contest may be overcome by a person who holds his breath while in the air; but if he goes beneath the water, where there is no air, how will he contrive in this matter? Beneath the water there is only the air each of them has stored in his lungs, and such a contest makes clear which of them has the broader chest and which is more enduring beneath the water. This is the mu'ajazah.

So the meaning of ﴿they strive against Our verses, seeking to frustrate [them]﴾ [al-Hajj 51] is: they suppose that they are able to frustrate Us. When We bring them an eloquent, inimitable speech, they fabricate empty words to frustrate Us with, but how could that be for them? And how could they dare to disparage the word of God with their speech?

Then He explains the recompense for this act and this arrogance: ﴿they are the companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Hajj 51]. This is God's judgment concerning them, a clear matter by the shortest route. For who could frustrate God?

1 - al-Ghazali cited these verses in "Ihya' 'ulum al-din" (3/157), but he mentioned a different story in connection with them, saying: "A man informed on Ziyad al-A'jam to Sulayman ibn 'Abd al-Malik, so he brought them together for confrontation, and Ziyad turned to the man and said..." and he mentioned the verses.
2 - Al-khil'ah (robe) of garments: what you take off and throw onto another, or do not throw. Every garment you take off is a khal'ah. [Lisan al-'Arab, root: kh-l-'].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 52:

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he desired [or recited], Satan threw [something] into his desire. So Allah abolishes what Satan throws in; then Allah makes His verses firm. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ (22:52)

This verse has provoked a long dispute among the scholars, and much superfluous material (ḥashw) and Isra'iliyyat (narrations from Jewish and Christian sources) has entered into it, especially concerning the meaning of ﴿tamannā﴾ (desired/recited). The word carries two meanings in the language, and since the term admits of two meanings, neither is preferred over the other except by the extent of its usage and its currency among the majority of Arabic speakers. In the language, tamannā can come in the sense of "recited," as occurs in the words of Ḥassān ibn Thābit in lamenting ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān, may Allah be pleased with them both:

"Tamannā the Book of Allah on the first night and its last, until the decree of destinies befell him."

That is, ʿUthmān was killed while reading the Qur'an. This meaning is, however, strange to apply to the Qur'an because it is not common.

Tamannā also comes in the sense of "to love that a thing should be," and this is the well-known meaning in the Arabic language. As for the meaning "recited," it is not widespread. This view is refuted, and immediately and initially undermined, by the Almighty's words: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet..﴾ (22:52).

It is well known that a messenger receives a Book that he can recite, whereas a prophet does not receive a Book but acts according to the law of the messengers before him. Therefore, since messenger and prophet are both included in Satan's throwing, the desire here must necessarily mean "to love that a thing should be," not "to recite." For what would the prophet recite when he has no Book with him?

Those who understood tamannā in His words ﴿...when he desired, Satan threw into his desire﴾ (22:52) to mean "recited," whether they were deep scholars or superficial ones, said: the meaning is that when the Messenger of Allah recited the Qur'an, Satan intruded into the recitation, so that something not part of it entered into it.

They cited as evidence for this His words: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt, the third, the other?﴾ (53:19-20), then they added: "and the exalted cranes (gharāniq), and their intercession is to be hoped for," and it was as if Satan had inserted this speech into the Qur'an, then Allah abrogated it afterward, and Allah made His verses firm.

But this view casts doubt on the matter of the Qur'an. How can we say it after Allah said in the Qur'an: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit brought it down, upon your heart, that you may be of the warners﴾ (26:193-194)?

And He said: ﴿Had he attributed to Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand, then We would have cut from him the aorta, and none of you could have held Us off from him﴾ (69:44-47).

So the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, has preserved His Qur'an and His speech from such absurdity. How can we insert into the Qur'an these blasphemies? And how can their phrase "the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for" be reconciled with the words of Allah: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt, the third, the other? Is the male for you and the female for Him? That, then, is an unjust division.﴾ (53:19-22)? How can this and that be harmonized?

This understanding of the verse's interpretation is not sound, and it is not possible for Satan to introduce into the Qur'an what is not part of it. But Satan's interference may occur in another way: when the Messenger of Allah recites the Qur'an, in which there is guidance for people, admonitions, rulings and miracles, do you expect the enemy of Allah to leave the atmosphere clear for people so that they may hear this speech without him disturbing them, confusing their thoughts, and coming between them and hearing it?

So when the Messenger desires, that is, recites, Satan throws into his desire, and sets his followers from among mankind to say about the Qur'an: "Sorcery, poetry, falsehood, and tales of the ancients." Satan's role, then, is not to enter into the speech of Allah what is not part of it, for this is something he cannot do, and Allah never enables him over His Book. Rather, he can throw in the path of the Qur'an, its understanding and its influence, obstacles and hindrances that turn people away from understanding it and being affected by it, and that corrupt the Qur'an in the eyes of whoever wishes to believe in it.

But, did this attempt to distort the Qur'an and turn people away from it achieve its result and actually divert people from the Book of Allah?

Allah has frustrated his effort, and his attempts did not stand as an obstacle in the way of faith in the Qur'an and being affected by it, because the Qur'an found hearts and ears that listened and reflected, so they believed and collapsed before its majesty and greatness, and submitted to its style and eloquence, and so they believed in it one after another.

Then He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿So Allah abolishes what Satan throws in; then Allah makes His verses firm. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾ (22:52). That is: He annulled and nullified what Satan threw in of falsehoods and obstacles by which he wished to turn people away from the Qur'an, and Allah made His verses firm, and made clear that they are from Him, glorified is He, and that it is the Book of Allah, miraculous, such that if mankind and jinn gathered together to produce its like, they would not be able to do so.

This is according to the view of those who held that ﴿tamannā﴾ means "recited."

As for the meaning that it is the beloved thing we wish for, we say: the Messenger whom Allah, may He be exalted, sent with the method of truth to creation, if he is capable of applying the method in himself, then his desire is that it be believed and that he be obeyed in what he brought; his desire is that his method prevail, dominate, and govern the movement of life among people.

The prophet or messenger is the most entitled of people to his people, and he is the most eager of them for their benefit and guidance, and the Qur'an is good which he loves for people to take up, in acting upon the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "None of you believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself."

But will Satan leave the Messenger of Allah's desire to be fulfilled among his people, or will he place obstacles in his path and stir souls against him, so that his people rebel against him, as Satan reminds them of the sovereignty and status they had, which they would lose through Islam?

And thus Satan throws into the desire of the Messenger: ﴿except when he desired, Satan threw into his desire﴾ (22:52). Satan would never leave the Qur'an to reach the hearts of people or even their ears. Is he not the author of the idea: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise over it...﴾ (41:26)?

Indeed, if Satan did not place obstacles in the way of hearing the Qur'an and cast doubt upon it, everyone who heard it would believe in it, for the Qur'an has an irresistible sweetness and an effect that reaches hearts directly.

Yet what Satan threw did not weaken the Qur'an's strength, nor the strength of the call, and it kept growing day by day, and the number of believers in the Qur'an who affirm it kept increasing. The important thing is that we be alert: how we receive the Qur'an and how we take it up. We must receive it in the manner of one free of desire, for what spoils judgments is that you receive and enter with a prior passion.

We have said before that a single space cannot hold two things at the same time; you must remove one to enter the other. So you must empty your mind and thought completely, then receive the speech of Allah, and investigate it as you wish, for you will arrive at belief in it on condition that you purify your heart for it, so that you leave in your mind nothing that disturbs the purity of the fitrah which Allah created in you. Then the Qur'an will take its path to your heart, and when your heart has drunk the love of the Qur'an, nothing will dislodge it afterward.

And for us in the conversion of our master ʿUmar there is an example and a lesson. When he heard the Qur'an from his sister for the first time, while his heart was closed upon his disbelief, he was not affected by it, and he struck her until her face bled. Then his heart softened, and his feeling moved toward his sister, as if the feeling of love displaced the feeling of enmity and revealed the purity of his nature. When he heard the Qur'an after that, he believed in it immediately.

Likewise, if you wish to discuss the matter of faith or disbelief, and to choose between them, since they never combine and you must choose, then when you discuss this matter while you are insistent upon disbelief you will not reach faith, because Allah seals the heart that insists, so disbelief does not leave it and faith does not enter it. Rather, expel disbelief first and free yourself from its captivity, then discuss the matters as you like.

As Allah says: ﴿Say: I admonish you with one thing: that you stand up for Allah in pairs and singly, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion...﴾ (34:46).

As for discussing an issue while holding a preconceived idea in your mind, you are like those of whom Allah said: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until when they leave your presence they say to those who were given knowledge, "What did he just say?"﴾ (47:16). That is: "What is the new thing he brought? And what is the miracle in this speech?" Then the response comes: ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah has sealed and who follow their desires. And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety.﴾ (47:16-17).

And in another verse the Truth, glorified is He, says of the Qur'an: ﴿Say: It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing; and for those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness upon them...﴾ (41:44).

So the Qur'an is one, but the recipients differ. We have mentioned that when you want to cool a hot cup of tea you blow on it, and likewise if you want to warm your hands in winter cold you also blow on them. How, then, when the agent is one? Yes, the agent is one, but the outcome of the action differs.

And His words: ﴿...any messenger or prophet﴾ (22:52). The particle "min" here indicates generality and the inclusion of all the earlier prophets and messengers. Every prophet or messenger desires, that is, wishes, loves, and longs for his religion to spread, his method to be applied, and all his people to believe in him. But far be it that Satan would leave him what he loves; rather, he must stand in the path of his call to turn people away from it and divert them from his call and method. Yet in the end Allah grants victory to His messengers and prophets, and abolishes the obstacles Satan threw into the path of the call, then Allah makes His verses firm, confirming and manifesting them, so they become established, and no one denies them.

And whenever you hear the word ﴿alqā﴾ (22:52), know that after it come obstacles and evils, as He says: ﴿And We have cast among them enmity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection﴾ (5:64).

Among what the proponents of the first view said regarding the interpretation of ﴿tamannā﴾ (22:52), taking it to mean "recited," they say: Allah, exalted is He, sends down to His Messenger (ﷺ) things that establish his humanness, then Allah erases the traces of this humanness to show that he was fashioned by Allah under His eye, so that if his humanness intended something, Allah would protect him from it.

For this reason the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "It is brought back to me and I say, 'I am not like any of you,' and it is taken from me and I say, 'I am only a human like you.'"

So the Messenger is human, except that revelation is sent to him which protects him from the lapses of humans.

And among his humanness (ﷺ) is that he was affected by sorcery, and this is an event that cannot be denied, and authentic hadiths have been transmitted about it. The unbelievers plotted against the Messenger of Allah with every kind of scheming: mockery, abuse, persecution, and humiliation; then they conspired against him by night to kill him, and laid plans against him, but they did not succeed. Allah says: ﴿And when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to restrain you or kill you or expel you, they plot, and Allah plots, and Allah is the best of plotters﴾ (8:30).

Allah outmaneuvered them for His Messenger and brought him out from among them safely. Thus Allah exposed their nighttime plotting and frustrated their efforts, and their open and secret schemes failed, so they resorted to sorcerers to do to the Messenger of Allah what they themselves could not do. They worked sorcery against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a comb and combings of his hair and the spathe of a male palm tree, and Allah exposed them, and informed His Messenger of it, so he sent Imam ʿAlī, who brought it out from the well of Dhurwān.

It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, wishes to show us the humanness of the Messenger, and that what happens to humans happens to him, but his Lord does not leave his humanness alone; rather He protects him by His self-subsistence (qayyūmiyya).

This is what the proponents of the first view intended: that the Messenger is subject to what happens to ordinary humans, but heaven intervenes to protect him. We, however, choose the other view, which says that tamannā means "wished" and "loved."

1 - Occasion of revelation of the verse: al-Wāḥidī mentions in Asbāb al-Nuzūl (p. 178), on the authority of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-ʿUzzā, and Manāt, the third, the other?﴾ (53:19-20), and Satan cast upon his tongue: "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for." The polytheists rejoiced at this and said: "He has mentioned our gods." Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Recite to me the speech of Allah." When it was recited to him, he said: "As for this, I did not bring it to you; this is from Satan." Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he desired, Satan threw into his desire...﴾ (22:52).
Ibn Kathīr said in his Tafsīr (3/229): "Many exegetes have mentioned here the story of the cranes, but all its chains are interrupted (mursal), and I have not seen it transmitted with a sound connected chain, and Allah knows best."

2 - Ibn Manẓūr cited in Lisān al-ʿArab, root m-n-y, with the wording: "Tamannā the Book of Allah on its first night and its last; it met the doves of destinies."

3 - Abū Manṣūr said: Recitation is called umniyya, because the reciter of the Qur'an, when he passes a verse of mercy, desires it, and when he passes a verse of punishment, desires to be protected from it. [Lisān al-ʿArab, root m-n-y].

4 - Gharāniq: the idols; originally the males of water birds. They used to claim that the idols brought them closer to Allah, azza wa-jall, and interceded for them with Him, so they were likened to birds that soar and rise into the sky. [Lisān al-ʿArab, root gh-r-n-q].

5 - Al-Waatīn: a vein in the heart, if it is cut the person dies; it is the main vital artery that supplies the body with pure blood leaving the heart. [al-Qāmūs al-Qawīm 2/319].

6 - A hadith agreed upon (muttafaq ʿalayhi). Recorded by al-Bukhārī in his Ṣaḥīḥ (13) and Muslim in his Ṣaḥīḥ (45), Book of Faith, on the authority of Anas ibn Mālik, with the wording: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, a servant does not believe until he loves for his neighbour—or he said: for his brother—what he loves for himself."

7 - The story of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb's conversion is mentioned by Ibn Hishām in al-Sīra al-Nabawiyya (1/344), and in it he said: "I have been informed that you two have followed Muhammad in his religion," and he assaulted his brother-in-law Saʿīd ibn Zayd. His sister Fāṭima bint al-Khaṭṭāb stood up to restrain him from her husband, so he struck her and wounded her. When he did that, his sister and brother-in-law said to him: "Yes, we have become Muslims and believed in Allah and His Messenger, so do what you wish." When ʿUmar saw the blood on his sister, he regretted what he had done and calmed down.

8 - That is: to imprison you and keep you in your place in Mecca under their control. It was also said: to bind you in chains. [al-Qāmūs al-Qawīm 1/105].

9 - Recorded by al-Bukhārī in his Ṣaḥīḥ (3268), and likewise Muslim in his Ṣaḥīḥ (2189), from the hadith of ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her.

Then the verse concludes with His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ [al-Hajj]: He knows the scheming of Satan and his plotting, and He is All-Wise in dealing with this scheming.

﴿So that He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease and whose hearts are hardened. Indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension﴾:

One may ask: if Allah abrogates what Satan casts, why was the casting at the beginning?

Allah made the casting a trial in order to test people and to distinguish those who rise to bear the burdens of the message. It is a responsibility that none undertakes except one who passes through trials, is saved from the allurements of Satan, and overcomes his obstacles and hindrances. Therefore Allah says of them: ﴿You are the best nation brought forth for mankind﴾ [Al 'Imran].

You did not attain this station except because you are fit to carry this trust. Trials pass over you, and you withstand them and they do not shake you. Therefore He says: ﴿So that He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾ [al-Hajj], meaning hypocrisy. If such a person encounters a trial, he turns on his heels. He says what they say: "Sorcery, lies, and the fables of the ancients."

Likewise the trial of ﴿and whose hearts are hardened﴾ [al-Hajj]: these are the ones who have lost the softness of heart, so they do not look at the beauty bestowed upon them in the universe, in creation, in origination, and in provision. They do not acknowledge Allah's favour upon them, and they do not rejoice in it and turn to Him.

We observe a small child who is comforted by his mother and father and leans on them, because he has tasted their tenderness and was raised under their care. If, for example, a nursemaid raises him even in the presence of his mother, he inclines to her and grows fond of her embrace, and does not turn to his mother. Why? Because he looked at the beauty, at where it came from, and at who bestowed the favour on him, and his heart was softened toward him, regardless of who the bestower of the kindness is.

These people came into the universe of Allah with no power and no strength, and He received them with every kind of good. Yet their hearts were hard and petrified, not acknowledging any kindness.

Then He, glorified be He, says: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension﴾ [al-Hajj]: they are wrongdoers first to themselves, when they looked to a small, immediate benefit and abandoned a great, lasting benefit. Al-shiqaq (dissension) is disagreement, and from it comes our saying: "This one is on one side, and that one is on another side," meaning they are not reconciled. Would that it were a minor dissension that could be gathered and reconciled, would that it were like the dissension of the world among people over some worldly matter. Rather, they are in far-reaching dissension. That is, its effect is lasting and its effect is grave.

So, the first reason for what Satan casts to be a trial is established. As for the second reason, it is in His saying:

﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord and believe in it, so that their hearts humble themselves to Him. Indeed, Allah is guiding those who believe to a straight path﴾ [al-Hajj, 54].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 54:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord (54)﴾ [al-Hajj]. He means: that they may become firmly and clearly certain that this is the truth, however much those who create confusion confuse them, and whatever they say about it: that it is sorcery, or lies, or "the fables of the ancients," because God will nullify all of this, and the people of knowledge and reflection will stand witness to the truthfulness of the Qur'an through the facts, premises and inferences they possess, by which they know that it is the truth.

Since it is the truth, which these false winds have not shaken, they must believe in it: ﴿so that they believe in it (53)﴾ [al-Hajj]. Then this belief is followed by action and practice: ﴿and their hearts humble themselves to it (54)﴾ [al-Hajj]. He means: they become humble, submissive, gentle and meek.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And indeed God is the Guide of those who believe to a straight path (54)﴾ [al-Hajj].

The matter of Satan's scheming and his casting (of doubts) did not end with the death of the Messenger. Rather, he sits in wait for his community after him. Satan lies in wait for the whole community of Muhammad, and for everyone who carries his call.

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And thus We have made for every prophet an enemy: devils of mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with ornamented speech as deception. And if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it. So leave them and what they invent (112)﴾ [al-An'am].

He means: leave them aside, for God is watching them closely. So why, then, did they do it? What is the wisdom?

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And that God may purge those who believe... (141)﴾ [Al 'Imran].

And He said: ﴿And that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline toward it (113)﴾ [al-An'am].

So the task of Satan is to exploit the weak in faith, and those who worship God on the edge (of faith), from among the people of excuse-making justifications, who want to justify to themselves their immersion in desire and their walking in the way of Satan. These people enjoy attacking the religion, and they wish that the religion, the Resurrection and the Lord were illusions with no reality, because they fear that they might be real, and that they would be entangled by their evil deeds and their painful end. Therefore they deny the Resurrection and say: ﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected?" (16)﴾ [al-Saffat].

Why? Because he wants to justify his conduct. He wants to extricate himself from a predicament from which there is no exit. These people follow every caller, and chase every doubt about the religion of God, seizing it and repeating it, and their aim is to demolish the religion from its foundation.

From these people who are wasteful toward themselves we hear an example: someone who objects to the prohibition of carrion and to eating the slaughtered animal. This is evidence of the leaven of polytheism and disbelief in their souls. They have feeble arguments that will not deceive anyone except their like among the disbelievers and hypocrites. And this is a clear matter: death is not the same as killing, and not the same as slaughter.

Death: the soul leaves first without the structure of the body being broken, and after the soul leaves, the structure of the body collapses. Killing, however, occurs by breaking the structure first, and the departure of the soul follows from the breaking of the structure, as when a person or an animal is struck on the head, for example, and dies after its brain has been disrupted and shattered, so that it is no longer fit for the soul to remain in it.

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And Muhammad is no more than a messenger; the messengers have passed away before him. So if he dies or is killed... (144)﴾ [Al 'Imran]. Thus: death is other than killing.

We have illustrated this with the electric light that we see, which runs through the wires and whose effect appears in these bulbs. We still do not know the essence of this electricity or the reality of this light; we only see it and enjoy it. When this bulb is broken, the light goes out, because it is no longer fit to receive this light, even though the light is present in the wires. Thus, the light of electricity appears only in a sound structure of this evacuated glass form.

Likewise, the soul does not dwell in the body, and does not remain in it, except when the body has certain specifications. If these specifications are disrupted, the soul leaves the body.

As for slaughter, it too is the taking of a soul, but by the command of God, its Creator, and by His permission, glory be to Him, as when a person is killed in retaliation (qisas), or in a lawful battle, or we slaughter the animal that God has made lawful for us and commanded us to slaughter. Had God not commanded its slaughter, we would not have slaughtered it, and had God not made it lawful, we would not have eaten it, as proven by the fact that we do not eat the other animals that are not lawful to us.

As for those who dispute the legal (shar'i) process of slaughter, and who take the lives of animals by strangling, for example, they have overlooked the wisdom of slaughter: slaughter is the shedding of blood, and in blood there are substances harmful to the human being that must be cleansed by draining the blood of the slaughtered animal, because it contains a quantity of corrupt blood that has not passed through the kidney to be purified.

Muslims are eager to carry the method of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and eager for this method to govern the movement of life. But Satan will not let them achieve this wish, just as he did not leave His Messenger (ﷺ) alone before. His scheming and his casting did not end with the death of the Messenger; rather, it remains, until the Hour comes.

Therefore Allah, the Exalted, says in the verse after it:

﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it until the Hour comes upon them suddenly or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day.﴾ (55)

His saying: ﴿in doubt (55)﴾ [al-Hajj]: meaning, in doubt about this. For this reason we have said that the followers of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) are charged by Allah with being an extension of his message: ﴿That you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you...﴾ (143) [al-Baqarah]. That is, witnesses that you have conveyed, just as the Messenger was a witness over you. So each of us is, as it were, sent by Allah, and just as the Messenger of Allah bore witness that he had conveyed (the message), so too does he bear witness that he has conveyed it after the Messenger of Allah. Therefore this verse came for both matters: that the Messenger may be a witness over you, and that you may be witnesses over the people.

When Allah, glory be to Him, entrusted us with this message, He said: since you are an extension of the message of the Messenger, you must encounter what the Messenger encountered of mockery, harm, and casting into your wishes. If you stand firm, then Allah, the Exalted, abrogates what Satan casts, and in the end gives victory to His friends. Islam will remain until the Hour comes, and there will always be people who oppose religion and cast doubt upon it. The atheists who cast doubt among people about the existence of Allah will continue to come out at times with what contradicts the religion of Allah, such as their saying: this universe came into being by nature. You see and hear this talk in their writings and articles.

Scientific knowledge has not been spared from these superstitions of theirs. When they see an animal in harmony with its environment, they say: nature has provided it with a color suited to it and a formation suited to its environment.

As for plants, when they stop at one of His signs, for example: ﴿Watered with one water, yet We make some of them exceed others in fruit...﴾ (4) [al-Ra'd], they say: plants feed by a process of selection, meaning the plant itself selects and chooses its nourishment. In one soil and with one water, sweet, bitter, sour and pungent plants grow. Instead of acknowledging Allah's bounty and power, they say: nature and the process of selection.

We spoke with some of these people in France, and we tried to respond to them and refute their arguments. The simplest of these is that the process of selection requires a conscious will that distinguishes between the things selected. Does the plant have a will that enables it to choose the sweet or the sour? Does it distinguish between the bitter and the pungent?

They try to persuade people of the role of nature in order to turn minds away from the power of Allah. They say: plants feed by the property of capillary tubes, meaning very narrow tubes resembling a hair, from which they are named (capillary, from the Arabic sense of hair). We know that a hair is a hollow tube. When you place this narrow tube in water, the water rises in it to a higher level, because the air pressure inside this tube, due to its narrowness, is less than the pressure outside it, so water rises in it. But if this tube were wide, the pressure inside it would equal the pressure outside, and water would not rise in it.

So we said to them: if we brought a basin containing different liquids, some dissolved in others, and then placed capillary tubes in it, would we find in each tube a particular liquid to the exclusion of the other liquids, or would we find in it the liquid mixed with all its elements?

If you carry out this experiment, you will find that the liquid does rise in the tubes by this property, but they do not distinguish between one element and another. The liquid is one in all the tubes, and how far this is from the growth and nourishment of plants!

Allah has spoken truly when He said: ﴿He who created and proportioned (2) and who decreed and guided (3)﴾ [al-A'la].

So: how far these explanations are from reality, and how ignorant are those who hold them and promote them, especially in an age in which knowledge has advanced, research has progressed, and its means have diversified, an age in which minds have been illuminated and the secrets of the universe have been discovered, which point to the power of its Creator, may He be exalted. Yet still there are those who persist in falsehood.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it until the Hour comes upon them suddenly...﴾ (55) [al-Hajj].

So they exist within the nation of Muhammad until the Hour comes, and we will confront them just as the Messenger confronted them. Satan will continue to cast into the souls of these people, whisper to them, inspire his friends among humans and jinn, and place obstacles and hindrances to turn people away from the religion of Allah. This is one example of Satan's casting regarding the foremost matter, which is faith in Allah.

Satan also casts regarding the matter of the Messenger. Among them are those who attack the personality of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: how could he, an unlettered Bedouin, lead a nation? They accuse him and speak falsely about him, and about the matter of the plurality of his wives (ﷺ), and so on, which forms an obstacle on the path of believing in him.

We are amazed at these people's attacks on the Messenger of Allah, given that they disbelieve in him. This attack carries within it a belief that he is the Messenger of Allah; otherwise they would not object to him or criticize him. If he were an ordinary person, he would not have been subjected to these criticisms.

Therefore, do not debate such people on the matter of the Messenger first; rather debate them on the matter of the foremost principle, the existence of God, and then the Messenger who conveys from this God. If you engage them first in the question of the Messenger, you will never reach a resolution with them, because they set the standards of perfection from themselves and then measure the conduct of the Messenger of Allah by them. This is an inverted approach: perfection is to be taken from the Messenger and from his actions; we do not set for him standards of perfection ourselves.

Then they cast doubt on the rulings. For example, they object to divorce in Islam, asking: how can we separate a couple? This is a strange matter from them. How can we compel two unwilling spouses to live together when they do not desire it, as though they were bound together in a chain of iron? How can you bind a friend to a friend who does not want him, when he sees him only once a day, for example? Can you bind a husband and wife in one place when they are mutually averse in a state of hatred?

Allah frustrates their endeavor, and the falsehood of these ideas becomes manifest, and the events of life and its problems compel them to legislate divorce, for there is no alternative to it for resolving such problems.

These people have debated much over the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾ (33) [al-Tawbah].

And over His saying: ﴿They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah will perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it﴾ (8) [al-Saff], and ﴿although the polytheists dislike it﴾ (9) [al-Saff].

They say: despite this, the religion has not been completed, and the great majority in the world still do not believe in Islam, wanting to cast doubt upon the Book of Allah. This statement of theirs arises from a failure to understand the verse. As for the meaning of ﴿to make it prevail (33)﴾ [al-Tawbah], it does not mean that Islam will triumph over everything else with a triumph that obliterates those who oppose it.

Rather, "to make it prevail" means: victory is written for it by the truth of its proofs and its matters, despite the dislike of the disbelievers and polytheists. So they exist, but it prevails over them, and the religion of Islam rises high, and they are compelled to adopt its laws and legislation as a solution to their problems. That they take it as a solution to their problems while they disbelieve in it is the most eloquent refutation of them, for if they believed in Islam it would not prevail over them and dominate them.

What you used to doubt and say it never came from a god or a messenger: behold, the days have bitten you with their events and experiences and have driven you to this ruling which you oppose. And here you are legislating with the legislation of Islam while you disbelieve in it, and this is evidence of its supremacy over you.

As for the meaning of ﴿suddenly, the Hour comes upon them (55)﴾ [al-Hajj]: it means unexpectedly. The scholars have discussed the meaning of "the Hour": is it the Day of Resurrection, or the day a person dies? The Hour includes both meanings together, on the basis that whoever dies, his resurrection has occurred, since his deeds have ended, and a person's death comes suddenly, just as the Resurrection comes suddenly. Thus the two are equal.

But if the Hour is sudden and overtakes them with its horrors, what of the minor signs and the major signs? Are they not preliminaries that herald the arrival of the Hour, and then it would not be sudden? They said: the signs of a thing are not its existence; a sign means the nearness of its appointed time, so be attentive and prepared, but its time of occurrence no one knows, and it must come suddenly despite these preliminaries.

Then Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day (55)﴾ [al-Hajj]. Some (1) have taken ﴿the punishment of a barren day (55)﴾ to mean the Resurrection, and accordingly "the Hour" means death. Others (2) say: ﴿the punishment of a barren day (55)﴾ means the Day of Badr, in which Allah separated truth from falsehood.

This is an interpretation for which they are to be thanked, but when we reflect on the verse ﴿and those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it (55)﴾: meaning the doubt continues. But Badr has ended, and the doubt will remain until the Hour comes (3).

There is no objection to the Hour meaning the Resurrection, and the barren day is also the Day of Resurrection, so the referent is one, because there is a difference between the time of an event and the event itself. The Hour is the time in which the event, which is the punishment, occurs. So the Hour comes first, then the punishment comes, although the mere establishment of the Hour in itself is a punishment.

As for the meaning of ﴿punishment of a barren day (55)﴾ [al-Hajj]: "barren" ('aqim) is that which does not bear children, whether a man or a woman, so nothing comes after it. Allah says of Sarah, the wife of Ibrahim (peace be upon him): ﴿an old barren woman (29)﴾ [al-Dhariyat]. Likewise the Day of Resurrection is a barren day, after which there is never another day, the end of the road, in the words of one of them: "The world loved them, but it grew barren."

Or ﴿barren (55)﴾ may mean that it brings no good but only evil, as in His saying: ﴿And in 'Ad, when We sent upon them the barren wind (41), which left nothing it came upon but made it like powder (42)﴾ [al-Dhariyat].

That is because when the wind blows, good is expected from it, either as a rain-bearing cloud or as stirring the pollen of the male to the female: ﴿And We sent the fertilizing winds (22)﴾ [al-Hijr]. But this wind has no good in it and no benefit from it, and it does not stop at mere lack of benefit, but goes further to bring harm: ﴿which left nothing it came upon but made it like powder (42)﴾ [al-Dhariyat]: it destroys everything over which it passes.

As He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said: this is a cloud that will bring us rain. Rather, it is what you were hastening: a wind in which is a painful punishment (24), destroying everything by the command of its Lord, so that by morning nothing could be seen but their dwellings (25)﴾ [al-Ahqaf].
