So the meaning of ﴿barren (55)﴾ is: there is no good in it and no benefit, but in it is evil and punishment; or "barren" means that no day comes after it, because you have left the world of changes, and the transformation of conditions from state to state: the world turns from poverty to wealth, from health to sickness, from youth to old age, from safety to fear, and changes from summer to winter, from heat to cold, from night to day, and so on.

As for the Hereafter, you have passed from the world of changes, which lives by causes, to another world which lives with the Causer, glory be to Him, and to another day after which there is no day, as though it were barren, having no sequel or like after it. This is like attending a feast that has completed all the forms of perfection and blessings, and you say: this is an event that will not be repeated, meaning it is barren and nothing like it will come after it.

If in this world you live by the causes that Allah created for you, then in the Hereafter you will sit at rest, enjoying the Causer, mighty and majestic, and it will suffice that a thing occurs to your mind for you to see it before you. And because the Resurrection has no changes and no transformation, all will remain each in his state at one age, neither growing old nor aging, neither falling ill nor dying.

Do you not see His saying, the Exalted, concerning the women of Paradise: ﴿Indeed, We have created them with a special creation (35) and made them...﴾

---
1 - Said by al-Dahhak and Mujahid, who said: on the Day of Resurrection there is no night. [Quoted by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir 6/4619, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 6/70].
2 - Said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah. [Quoted by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir 6/4619].
3 - Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (3/231): "This view is the correct one; though the Day of Badr was among what they were warned of, this is what is meant, and for this reason He said: ﴿The dominion on that day belongs to Allah; He will judge between them (56)﴾ [al-Hajj]."

The Most High then says:

﴿The dominion on that Day belongs to Allah. He will judge between them. So those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in Gardens of Bliss.﴾ (22:56)

One might ask: Is not the dominion Allah's on that Day, and on every day? Yes, dominion belongs to Allah in this world and in the Hereafter. But in this world Allah created creatures and gave them dominion, making them rulers from within His own dominion, may He be exalted. Yet it is a dominion that does not last, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Say: O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is the good. Indeed, You are Competent over all things.﴾ (3:26)

So, in this world there are rulers whom Allah has empowered over some matters, and so there is a dominion held by others. But in the Hereafter, dominion belongs to Allah the One alone: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is for Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ (40:16)

And on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the dominion on that Day belongs to Allah; He will judge between them…﴾ (22:56). Thus all dominion has been returned to its owner, and all means have been returned to their Causer.

The meaning of ﴿He will judge between them…﴾ (22:56) is that there is a dispute between two parties, one of whom is in the right and the other in the wrong. Resolving disputes in this world requires witnesses, evidence, and oaths. In courts they say: "The burden of proof is on the claimant, and the oath is on the one who denies." This is the case with the disputes of this world. But the disputes of the Hereafter are judged by the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, who knows the secret and what is more hidden. He needs no evidence, no witnesses, and no authority to enforce what He has decided.

In the court of the Hereafter you will not need a lawyer, nor will you be able to deceive the Judge or hire a false witness. In the court of the Hereafter you cannot use your worldly authority to overturn or annul the verdict, because on that Day the dominion belongs to Allah alone, and the judgment belongs to Allah alone. He, glorified is He, is the Judge, the Witness, and the Enforcer, and no one can appeal His ruling.

And since there is a ruling, it must result in one who is judged in his favor and one who is judged against, and His saying, the Most High, clarifies these: ﴿So those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in Gardens of Bliss.﴾ (22:56)

These are the victorious, whose verdict came in their favor.

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 57:**

﴿And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾ :

These are the tyrants and the masters of power in the world of disbelief and obstinacy, those upon whom Allah has decreed a punishment that humbles them after their might and dominion in this world. You notice that the punishment is described once as painful (ʾalīm), once as great (ʿaẓīm), and once as humiliating (muhīn).

The painful punishment (al-ʿadhāb al-ʾalīm) is that which causes pain to its bearer, but it may last for a period and then end. The great punishment is the lasting one. The humiliating punishment is that which abases a person and tramples the dignity in which he has long taken pride. You find that people differ in how they accept the kinds of punishment. Some are not affected by a painful beating and it does not move them, but a word that wounds their honour and dignity pains them. Therefore the punishment came in these varied forms, to encompass all the types of psychological dispositions and to confront every soul with what pains it.

Then the Exalted spoke of a matter that we must know. The early Muslims in Makkah were expelled from their homes, their children and their wealth, because they said: "Our Lord is Allah." Without doubt, homeland, family and the environment in which a person grew up have an effect on the dispositions of his soul, which can never be erased in any way. If he is absent from it, he longs for it and wishes to return, as the poet says:

*My homeland, though it wrongs me, remains dear to me;*
*my people, though they withhold from me, are noble.*

Therefore, when a seeker of knowledge leaves his country for Cairo, they say: he must return, even if events and hardships afflict him. He returns to seek help and assistance from his family, or even returns to it in the end so that they may bury him in the soil of his homeland.

They also said: when our master Sulayman (peace be upon him and our Prophet) inspected the birds, ﴿he said, "Why do I not see the hoopoe? Or is he among the absent? I will surely punish him with a severe punishment or slaughter him, or he must bring me a clear authority."﴾ [An-Naml]. That was because he was a prophet; the matter is not one of tyranny and torment without first hearing from him. They also said: the bird asked Sulayman, "How will you punish the hoopoe?" He said: "I will place him among other than his own kind, and in a place other than the one he is accustomed to," meaning: in other than his native place.

1 - Ibn ʿAbbas said: it means plucking out its feathers. ʿAbdullah ibn Shaddad said: plucking its feathers and exposing it to the sun. Similarly, more than one of the early generations (al-salaf) said: he plucked its feathers and left it lying where the ants and the black ants would eat it. [Tafsir Ibn Kathir 3/360].

Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿And those who emigrated in the cause of Allah and were then killed or died - Allah will surely provide for them a good provision. And indeed, Allah is the best of providers.﴾ (22:58)

In another place He says: ﴿Those who have been expelled from their homes without right, only because they say, "Our Lord is Allah."﴾ (22:40) These people bore much and toiled in the cause of their belief, so Allah must compensate them for these sacrifices. Therefore He says here: ﴿And those who emigrated in the cause of Allah and were then killed or died - Allah will surely provide for them a good provision.﴾ (22:58)

We have explained that death is other than killing. Death is that the soul leaves without the breaking of the structure, whereas killing is the breaking of the structure which results in the departure of the soul.

﴿Allah will surely provide for them a good provision...﴾ (22:58): as compensation for what they lost in their homeland of family and wealth, just as a just ruler compensates the wronged person by giving him more than what was taken from him. Therefore He, glorified is He, says elsewhere: ﴿And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, and then death overtakes him, his reward has already fallen upon Allah...﴾ (4:100)

For whoever is killed has attained the martyrdom and gained one of the two good things, whereas whoever dies has been deprived of this honour. Therefore his reward has fallen upon Allah. So what about the reward of the one who fulfils it, your Lord, Mighty and Majestic? It is like a weary man walking with nothing in his possession, not even finding anyone to lend him something. Suddenly his foot fell into a pit, and he was distressed and said, "Even this?" But soon his foot had stirred up something in the dust that had a sparkle, and behold, it was much gold, which had fallen upon him by itself.

It is related that Fadalah(1) was present with them while they were burying a martyr, and another who had died without being a martyr. They saw him leave the grave of the martyr and go to the grave of the non-martyr. When they asked him, "How do you leave the grave of the martyr for that of a non-martyr?" he said, "By Allah, I do not mind in which of the two pits I am placed, so long as my reward has fallen upon Allah." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger, and then death overtakes him, his reward has already fallen upon Allah...﴾ (4:100)

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And indeed, Allah is the best of providers.﴾ (22:58) When the Truth, glorified is He, describes His Essence with an attribute and then it comes in the plural form, this means that Allah, Exalted is He, has included creation in this attribute, as we previously discussed in His saying: ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.﴾ (23:14)

He has affirmed for creation the attribute of creating and has associated them with Himself, glorified is He, in this attribute, because He, glorified is He, does not deprive His servants of anything and does not deny them the fruit of their effort. Everyone who brings something into existence has created it, even in falsehood He said: ﴿And you fabricate a falsehood...﴾ (29:17)

Because creation is bringing into being from non-existence. When you make, for example, a water cup from glass, you have brought into existence what did not exist, although you used materials created by Allah, the Exalted, and applied your mind to them until you arrived at producing a new thing that did not exist. In this sense you are a good creator, but the creation of your Lord is better. You create from something existing, while your Lord creates from non-existence. What you have brought into existence remains in its state and stays fixed in the form you gave it; it does not reproduce by procreation, does not grow, and has no life in it. As for the creation of your Lord, glorified is He, as you know...

Likewise He, glorified is He, says here: ﴿And indeed, Allah is the best of providers.﴾ (22:58) Thus He affirms for His creation also the attribute of provision, insofar as they are a cause of it, because provision is everything from which one benefits; even the unlawful is considered provision. Therefore Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who believe, eat from the good things with which We have provided you...﴾ (2:172)

We say: the servant is a cause of provision, because Allah, Exalted is He, is the Creator of provision first, then He gives it to you to benefit from and to work with, and you give from it to others. Thus provision from you is a delivery on behalf of the First Provider, glorified is He. So in this sense you are a provider, even though they disliked that a person be called a provider, despite His saying: ﴿And indeed, Allah is the best of providers.﴾ (22:58). Why? They said: so that it is not understood that provision comes from people.

Therefore we often hear simple workers, or a minor employee, or a building doorman for example, when his employer dismisses him, say to him: "O sir, provisions are in the hand of Allah." How so, when he used to take his salary from His hand and from His wealth? They said: because he looked at the first deliverer of provision and did not look at the second deliverer.

1 - He is: Fadalah ibn Ubayd al-Ansari al-Awsi, Abu Muhammad, a Companion who pledged under the tree, participated in Uhud and after it, took part in the conquest of Syria and Egypt, settled in Syria, was appointed to lead raids and the sea forces in Egypt, then Mu'awiyah appointed him judge of Damascus, and he died there in the year 53 AH [al-A'lam of al-Zirikli 5/146].

2 - Mentioned by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir (6/4620) and attributed it to Ibn al-Mubarak that he related it from Fadalah ibn Ubayd.

Regarding the good provision (rizq hasan) that Allah has prepared for those who emigrated in His cause, He clarifies it in His saying:

﴿He will certainly admit them to an entrance that they will be pleased with. And indeed, Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.﴾

Because provision may be good yet not satisfy its recipient, whereas Allah's provision for these people has reached the point of their being pleased. Contentment (al-rida') is the soul's being satisfied with something in which it finds enjoyment, such that it does not look upward to anything higher than it, nor desire more than that.

Therefore, after the people of Paradise have been granted its bliss, such as no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and nothing has occurred to the heart of a human being, then the Truth, glory be to Him, will manifest Himself to them and say to His believing servants: "O My servants, are you pleased?" They will say: "And how would we not be pleased, when You have given us what You have not given anyone from among the worlds?" He will say: "Shall I not give you something better than this?" They will say: "And is there anything better than what we are in?" He will say: "Yes, I shall let My pleasure descend upon you, so that I shall never be displeased with you after this, ever." (1)

From this is His saying, exalted be He, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ):

﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be satisfied.﴾ [al-Duha]

And His saying:

﴿O tranquil soul, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him].﴾ [al-Fajr]

He exaggerates in contentment, to the extent that the contentment extends beyond you until your very life becomes content, as if it loves you and is pleased with you.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And indeed, Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.﴾ [al-Hajj]

"Knowing" (alim): of what each person deserves of bliss at the reckoning; then He increases whom He wills from His bounty. The reckoning of your Lord in the Hereafter is not like your reckoning in this world; rather His reckoning, exalted be He, is by grace, not by strict justice.

"Forbearing" (halim): He shows forbearance toward the servant if he errs, and overlooks the slips of the righteous. If your righteous deed is mixed with some evil, and if you oppose the method of Allah through heedlessness or a slip, do not let this cloud the clarity of your relationship with your Lord or disturb the tranquility of your life, for your Lord is Forbearing and will overlook such things, according to their saying: "Your beloved will swallow the pebbles for you."

For this reason, when a certain believer (2) informed the disbelievers about the conquest of Mecca, and Umar wanted to kill him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade him and said: "Perhaps Allah has looked upon the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you." (3)

And it is enough that they went out of their own accord and plunged into a battle unequal in number and equipment; shall we not mention this stance for them? Did not the Truth, glory be to Him, say: ﴿Indeed, good deeds do away with bad deeds.﴾ [Hud] Whoever is tested with something to which he is weak, let him be strong in what he is able to do; and if Satan overcomes you in one door of evil, then exert yourself in the doors of good, for that will compensate for this.

1 - Agreed upon. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (7518), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2829), Book of Paradise and Description of its Bliss, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.

2 - He is Hatib ibn Abi Balta'a. His story is that he wrote to the people of Mecca about the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) preparations for the conquest of Mecca. Umar said: "Let me strike his neck." He said: "He witnessed Badr." Hatib excused himself, saying that he had no clan in Mecca to protect his family, so his excuse was accepted. Al-Marzubani said in "Mu'jam al-Shu'ara'": he was one of the knights and poets of Quraysh in the pre-Islamic period. Al-Madaini said: Hatib died in the year thirty during the caliphate of Uthman, at the age of sixty-five. [al-Isaba of Ibn Hajar 1/314]

3 - A hadith agreed upon. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4890), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2494), from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.

Then the Most High, glory be to Him, says:

{That is so. And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with, and then is wronged again, Allah will surely help him. Indeed Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving (60).}

﴿That﴾ means: this matter we have been discussing is settled. Now here is a new topic: ﴿And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with, and then is wronged again, Allah will surely help him..﴾ [al-Hajj].

Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, created the human being and placed in him various faculties so that he may carry out his vicegerency on earth through balanced movements. He created for us emotions and gave them a function. These emotions are not governed by a fixed law. He also created for us instincts, which have a function, but they are governed by the law of the instincts' elevation (ta'liyat al-ghara'iz) in creation. So beware of letting your instinct transgress beyond the function for which Allah created it.

For example, the instinct for food Allah placed in you to preserve life. So do not make it an end in itself, such that you eat merely to enjoy eating, for that is a momentary pleasure followed by long pains and hardships. Allah placed this instinct in the human soul precisely regulated, just as an alarm regulates. When you become hungry you find yourself longing for food and seeking it, and if you become thirsty your soul inclines toward water, as though within you there is a bell alerting you to what your body needs of the means of its preservation.

The instinct of curiosity is an instinct Allah placed in you so that you may look with it and explore what is in the universe of secrets indicating the power and greatness of Allah. So do not transgress this purpose, and do not direct this instinct to spying on people and uncovering their secrets.

Procreation is an instinct Allah placed for the preservation of the species, so it is not fitting that you transgress what it was made for into what Allah has forbidden.

Anger is an instinct and an involuntary emotional reaction. You do not choose with your intellect whether to become angry or not; rather, if you are exposed to its causes, you cannot but become angry. Nevertheless, Allah set limits for it, legislated for it, and commanded self-restraint and non-indulgence in it.

Love and hatred are an instinct and an emotion not subject to law, and the intellect does not govern them. You may love and you may hate, but beware of letting this emotion transgress into an intellectual act or a tendency by which you aggress or wrong.

Therefore the Most High says: ﴿And do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just..﴾ [al-Ma'idah 8].

Because this matter is not governed by law, and love or hatred is not in your hand. So when the lord (sayyidna) Umar met the killer of his brother, he said to him: "Turn your face away from me, for I do not love you." The man was intelligent and said to the lord Umar: "Does your not loving me prevent me from one of my rights?" Umar said: "No." The man said: "Only women weep over love." That is, love or hate as you wish, but do not transgress, and do not deprive me of any of my rights.

So have we kept the instincts within their limits and aims? If you consider, for example, the sexual instinct, which some describe with full mouths as a "bestial instinct"... Glory be to Allah! Are you not ashamed to wrong the beasts merely because they do not speak, while they understand this instinct better than you? Do you not see that as soon as the male impregnates the female, he never approaches her again, and she does not allow him near her when she is pregnant, whereas you exaggerate this instinct and give it free rein, carrying it beyond its purpose and wisdom? Anyone who says such a saying should be ashamed, and should not wrong the beasts, for there are people far lower than beasts.

What is said about the sexual instinct in animals is said likewise about food and drink.

So: the Creator, glory be to Him, created the instincts in you and did not suppress them, and He made for them lawful outlets so that they may carry out their function in your life. Therefore He surrounded them with a fence of obligation that organizes and governs them, so that they do not bolt with you. For example, regarding the instinct of food and drink He said: ﴿O children of Adam, take your adornment at every mosque, and eat and drink, but do not be excessive..﴾ [al-A'raf 31].

And regarding the instinct of curiosity He said: ﴿And do not spy..﴾ [al-Hujurat 12]. Thus in all your instincts you will find limits that you must not transgress.

Therefore we have said, regarding the attributes of faith and the attributes of disbelief, that Allah the Most High describes the believers as ﴿harsh against the disbelievers, merciful among themselves..﴾ [al-Fath 29], because they place every instinct in its proper place: severity with the enemies and mercy with their fellow believers. They stop at these limits and do not reverse their measures, and they adhere to the saying of the Most High: ﴿humble toward the believers, mighty against the disbelievers..﴾ [al-Ma'idah 54].

It is as if the Creator, mighty and majestic, is making us equal in a faith-based equality: the believer was not created mighty or humble; rather, the situation is what places him in his suitable position. He is mighty and lofty with the disbelievers, and humble, lowly and modest with the believers.

From this matter there branches the question of returning punishment when you are transgressed against: ﴿And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with..﴾ [al-Hajj 60]. The Most High, glory be to Him, is the Creator of the human soul, and He is most knowing of its impulses and inner stirrings. Therefore, if you are transgressed against, He permitted you to repel the aggression with its like, so that anger does not ferment in your soul, which may result in something more severe and extreme in retaliation. He permits you to respond in kind so that the matter ends at this limit and does not escalate. Whoever strikes you a blow, you may vent yourself and strike him with its like; that is yours. But remember that the likeness here must be complete, as He said in another place: ﴿And if you retaliate, then retaliate with the like of what you were afflicted with..﴾ [al-Nahl 126].

Can you control this likeness, so that you return a blow with its like? Is your strength like his, and is the intensity of your reaction like the intensity of his? And if you exceed in your response out of anger, what do you do? Would you allow him to return this excess against you? Or would you then be an oppressive aggressor?

So why would you throw yourself into such a maze, when in forgiveness there is ample room? And in His saying after it: ﴿But if you are patient, it is better for the patient (126)﴾ [al-Nahl] is an exit from this constraint.

We have already related the story of the Jewish usurer who said to a debtor: "If you are late in repayment, I stipulate that I take a pound of your flesh." When the time of payment came and the debtor did not pay, the creditor brought him before the judge and informed him of what he had stipulated. The judge said: "Yes, you have the right to take a pound of his flesh, but with a single stroke of the knife, taking exactly a pound. If it exceeds or falls short, we will take it from you."

So the principle of likeness here is a barrier that restrains the surge of anger, and it opens a door to elevations of faith. If the Most High permitted you to vent yourself, saying: ﴿And the recompense for an evil is an evil like it..﴾ [al-Shura 40], then He also says to you: do not forget pardon and forgiveness: ﴿And those who restrain anger and pardon people, and Allah loves the good-doers (134)﴾ [Al 'Imran].

Therefore the verse before us draws our attention with a faith-based subtlety: ﴿And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with..﴾ [al-Hajj 60]: one for one. ﴿Then is wronged again..﴾ [al-Hajj 60]: that is, he increases after having repelled the aggression with its like, and wrongs and transgresses against him. ﴿Allah will surely help him..﴾ [al-Hajj 60]: He will help him against the aggressor who did not accept Allah's ruling on retaliation by its like.

And you notice in His saying the signs of victory in His words ﴿Indeed Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving (60)﴾ [al-Hajj]: although the attribute suited to victory would be to say "Strong, Mighty," because victory requires strength and requires might. But He, glory be to Him, chose the attribute of pardon and forgiveness to draw the attention of one who wants to punish to these elevations of faith: forgive, show mercy, and pardon, for your Lord is Pardoning and Forgiving. So He chose the attribute that softens the heart of the believer toward his believing brother.

Then, do you not have sins before Allah? ﴿Do you not love that Allah should forgive you..﴾ [al-Nur 22]. So as long as you love that Allah forgive you, then forgive His servants. And when you forgive one who deserves punishment, the result comes as your Lord, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿Then the one between you and him who has enmity will become as if he were a devoted friend (34)﴾ [Fussilat].

The Most High wants to spread among us inner purity and faith-based unity. So He gave you the right to return punishment with its like, so that you vent your anger, and then He calls you to pardon and forgiveness.

1 - Sha'ana, and sha'ana: he hated and detested him. Al-sha'in: the hater. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/357]. And jarrama: he burdened him with committing an evil or a sin or a crime. That is: the hatred of a people should not burden you into not being just; that is, adhere to justice even with those you dislike. [Al-Qamus al-Qawim 1/121].

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and because Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.﴾ (22:61)

﴿That..﴾ (22:61): meaning, what I told you earlier has a proof. What is it? That Allah takes from the strong and gives to the weak, and takes from the tall and gives to the short. So the matter is not fixed (like a machine), rather Allah created it according to a measure. The night and the day are the containers of the events you do, and the Truth, glory be to Him, ﴿causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night..﴾ (22:61).

"Causes the night to enter" means: the night enters upon the day, taking from it bit by bit, so the night lengthens and the day shortens. Then the day enters upon the night, taking from it bit by bit, so the day lengthens and the night shortens. Therefore we see that they are not equal: at one time the night lengthens in winter, for example, and the day shortens; at another time the day lengthens in summer and the night shortens. The increase of one and the decrease of the other is a continuous matter, and changes alternate between them.

If changes occur within the container of events, then the events themselves must change accordingly. So when the container expands, what is in it expands as well. For example, in measures we have the kayla, the qadah, the wiba, and we have the ardab, and each of them holds contents according to its capacity. Likewise, as we increase or decrease in the container of events, we increase or decrease in the events themselves.

Then the verse concludes with His words, glory be to Him: ﴿and because Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.﴾ (22:61): All-Hearing of what is said, All-Seeing of what is done. Speech corresponds to action, and both are deeds. Some think that action is one thing and speech is another; no, because action is the function of the organ, so every organ performs its task and is thus working: the eye's work is to see, the ear's work is to hear, the hand's work is to touch, the nose's work is to smell, and likewise the tongue's work is speech. Speech belongs to the tongue alone, and action belongs to the other organs, and both are deeds. Thus we always place speech opposite action, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Why do you say what you do not do?﴾ (61:2).

Hearing and sight are the two main organs in the human being, and they are the pillar of all the senses, as they work continuously, unlike smell, for example, or taste, which works only several times a day.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 62:

﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they call upon besides Him is falsehood, and Allah is the Most High, the Most Great.﴾ (62):

﴿That…﴾ [al-Hajj]: That is, the preceding discourse is a known matter, and we have finished with it. ﴿Because Allah is the Truth…﴾ [al-Hajj]: The truth (al-haqq) is that which is firm and never changes. Everything other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic, changes, while He, glory be to Him, is the One who causes change and does not change. For this reason, the people of knowledge (ahl al-ma'rifa) say: Allah, Exalted, does not change for your sake, but you must change for the sake of Allah.

Since your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is the firm Truth who does not change, and all else changes, do not grieve, and O angry one, be content, and O one who weeps, laugh and be at peace. For you are a son of changes, living in a world of changes that does not remain steady on anything. Therefore, a person becomes angry when he is struck by a hardship in his life and says: "If only this had not happened." We say to him: "Did you want it to be perfect? Something must befall you, for you are a son of changes. What do you expect? If you reach the summit, you must decline, for you are a son of changes, constantly fluctuating in conditions, while your Lord alone is the Firm One who does not change."

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And what they call upon besides Him is falsehood…﴾ (62) [al-Hajj]: Everything you claim or worship besides Allah is falsehood, meaning that which perishes, as in His saying, Exalted: ﴿Indeed, falsehood is ever bound to vanish﴾ (81) [al-Isra]: that is, it passes away and never endures. ﴿And Allah is the Most High, the Most Great…﴾ (62) [al-Hajj]: "The Most High" means that all His creation is beneath Him, and "the Great" means that all His creation is small.

Among His names, Exalted is He, is ﴿al-Kabir﴾ (62) [al-Hajj]. We do not say "Akbar" except in the adhan and at the opening of the prayer. Some think that akbar is more eloquent in description than kabir, but this is not correct, because whatever is beneath akbar is kabir; rather, the opposite of kabir is saghir (small). He, glory be to Him, is al-Kabir, because whatever is beneath Him and other than Him is small.

As for when He calls you and summons you to perform the obligation of Allah, He says: "Allah is Akbar," because the movement of life and the necessities of living are, in the sight of Allah, a great matter and an important one that is not to be neglected. But if the movement of life and striving in it is a great matter, then Allah is Akbar. Your Lord brings you out from work to prayer, and then calls you back to work: ﴿And when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land and seek of the bounty of Allah…﴾ (10) [al-Jumu'a].

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green? Indeed, Allah is Subtle, Acquainted with all things.﴾ (22:63)

﴿Have you not seen..﴾ [al-Hajj]: If it refers to a matter perceptible to the eye, then you have not seen it, and We are alerting you to it; and if it refers to a matter that cannot be perceived by the eye, then it means: Have you not known? Knowledge has been put in place of sight to show you that what Allah teaches you is more certain than what your eye guides you to.

So the meaning is: Have you not known, and have you not looked? Both meanings together.

﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky..﴾ [al-Hajj]: This is a sign you see, but you see only its outward aspect. You see the water pouring down from the sky, but how this water forms in the layers of the atmosphere, and why it falls in this particular place, these are processes you have not seen. The power of Allah, the Exalted, is vast. Reflect: if you wanted to gather one cup of water from water vapour, how much effort, time, and processes of heating, evaporation and condensation would it take you? Have you seen these processes in the formation of rain?

So you have seen the outward aspect of the rain, and therefore your Lord draws your attention to what lies behind this outward aspect so that you may reflect upon it.

For this reason, the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, made the surface of water three-quarters of the earth's sphere. The expanse of the water's surface increases the evaporation that Allah spreads over the dry land. For example, if you place a cup of water in your room and leave it for a month or two, you will find that it decreases by perhaps a centimetre; but if you spread the cup's contents on the floor of the room, it will dry within minutes.

So the expanse of water increases the amount of vapour rising from it, and we on dry land need large quantities of fresh water suitable for agriculture, drinking, and so on, which is available only through abundant rainfall.

Then Allah explains the result of sending down water from the sky: ﴿and the earth becomes green..﴾ [al-Hajj]: That is, after a short time it becomes bright green. Without mention of any human intervention in this process: man has not ploughed, sown, or irrigated; the whole matter is by the power of Allah. But from where did the seeds that produced this vegetation come? And who scattered and distributed them? The seeds were present in the soil, living and dormant, untouched by anything, however long the time passed, because Allah, the Exalted, preserves them until they find water and the conditions for germination are met, and then they sprout. For this reason we call this vegetation (al-'adhi) [the vegetation that grows without cultivation], because it emerged by the power of Allah with no human involvement.

The winds took on the task of carrying these seeds from one place to another, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilising..﴾ [al-Hijr] (15:22). If you trace this seed, you will find it from tree to tree until it reaches a mother tree which the Creator, Glorified is He, created without any tree before it or any seed. For this reason it is related that Yusuf the carpenter, who was caring for and supervising Lady Maryam, peace be upon her, and who is said to have been her betrothed, when he saw her pregnant without a husband, asked her politely: "O Maryam, can there be a tree without a seed?" She said: "Yes, the tree that produced the first seed."

Then He, glorified, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle, Acquainted with all things.﴾ (22:63) [al-Hajj]: Subtlety (al-lutf) is the fineness of handling things. For example, when you want to thread a string through a needle, you find that the string does not pass through the eye the first time, so you try to thin the end of the string and twist it until it becomes fine enough to pass through the hole. The string, which was thick, has become subtle and fine.

They say: the more subtle a thing is, the more forceful it is, whereas some suppose that the big thing is the strong one. But this is not correct: the finer and more subtle a thing is, the greater its danger. Do you not see how a microbe afflicts a person, and how we do not feel it and find no pain from it? That is because it is fine and subtle, and it also has a subtle entry that you do not feel, being so small that you cannot see it with the naked eye.

How small and insignificant the mosquito is, yet its bite pains you with its fine proboscis, which you can barely see. The finer a thing is, the more precaution it requires so that you may protect yourself from its harm. For example, if you want to build a house in the open country or a remote area, you will be obliged to put iron bars on the windows to protect you from predatory animals such as wolves; then you put a wire mesh to protect you from rats; and if you want to protect yourself from flies and mosquitoes, you need a finer wire. Thus, the smaller and finer a thing is, the more precaution it requires.

The subtle one is the one who enters things gently. That is why they say: "So-and-so has a subtle approach," meaning he enters to each person by what suits them, and knows for each person a point of weakness through which to enter, as if he had a (tafashsha) [a master key] for men, with which he can open any personality.

But what is the connection between His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle, Acquainted with all things.﴾ (22:63) and His preceding saying ﴿and the earth becomes green..﴾ (22:63)? They said: because the process of germination depends on pores and fine hairs that emerge from the seed after germination and absorb nourishment from the soil. These root hairs require subtlety, and the absorption of the appropriate nourishment for each kind requires expertise, as He said: ﴿Watered with one water, yet We make some of them excel others in food..﴾ (13:4) [al-Ra'd].

So the earth becomes green through the subtlety of the Real, glorified is He, and through His expertise in the entry points of things. That is why He said after it: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Subtle, Acquainted with all things.﴾ (22:63)

And because of the fineness of the root hairs, we take care that groundwater does not rise in the soil, because it corrupts these hairs, so they rot and die, and the plant turns yellow and dies.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾ (22:64)

Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth is the possession of Allah, the Exalted. Yet the Truth, glorified is He, does not benefit from any of it in anything. He created them for the benefit of His creation, and He is free of need from them and free of need from them (all). With His attributes of perfection, He, glorified is He, created whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Therefore, after this He said: ﴿And indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾ (22:64) [al-Hajj].

The attributes of perfection in Allah, the Exalted, exist before He created the creation, and with His attributes of perfection He created. His ownership, the Exalted, of the heavens and the earth, and of what is in them, is an ownership of the container and of the contained. We do not own the heavens, and we do not own the earth; rather, we own only what is in them of good things and benefits, of what Allah has made us to possess. So He is the Free of need, glorified is He, the Owner of everything, and we possess nothing except from the inner part of His dominion.

Al-Hamid (the Praiseworthy): meaning the one who is praised. So He is Free of need and praised, because His freedom from need does not return to Him, glorified is He; rather, it returns to His creation, so they praise Him for His freedom from need, and they do not harbor resentment against Him. It is remarkable that the Truth, glorified is He, makes His creation possessors from His own possession. Whoever uses a blessing for what it was made for, and whoever gives to one who is unable from the blessing of Allah upon him, thanks Allah for him, though it is originally His blessing. That is because you are His servant, and He has summoned you into existence, and it is incumbent upon Him, glorified is He, to take charge of you and look after you.

If one who is unable among you needs something, Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan...﴾ (2:245) [al-Baqarah].

So consider it a loan, though it is His property; but He has made it yours, so He does not take it from you, rather He takes it as a goodly loan and multiplies it for you, because He is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy, that is, the one who is praised. And wealth is not praiseworthy unless the one who lacks it benefits from its owner's wealth.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the earth, and the ships that sail through the sea by His command? And He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission. Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to the people.﴾ (22:65)

This verse is a continuation of the previous verse. Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth belongs to Him, glorified is He, yet He has subjected it for the benefit of His creation. If someone asks: "Why does Allah not make it ours and give us ownership of it?" We say: because your Lord wants to reassure you that He will never give it to anyone, and it will remain His possession while you benefit from it. Would you feel safe if Allah gave ownership of it to someone else, that he might change toward you and deprive you of it? So you are reassured by the fact that ownership remains with Allah alone, because He is your Lord and your Guardian, and He will not change toward you, nor will He turn against your benefit.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and the ships that sail through the sea by His command...﴾ (22:65). Al-Fulk (the ships): it refers to ships, and it is used for both the singular and the plural. They sail through the sea by His command, the Exalted, so ships move with the wind wherever Allah directs them, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿and the changing of the winds...﴾ (2:164). This is something no one owns or has power over except Allah. And He said in another verse: ﴿If He wills, He calms the wind so that they remain motionless upon its surface...﴾ (42:33).

Reflect on the precision of the Qur'anic expression from Allah, who knows what has been, what is, and what will be. Someone may now say: "We no longer need the wind to move ships or steer them, because they now move by machines and engines." Yes, ships now move by engines, but the wind has a broader meaning than that. The wind is not merely the natural force that pushes ships over the surface of the water; rather, "wind" means force in itself, whatever it may be: wind, steam, electricity, or the atom, etc.

The proof is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and do not dispute, lest you lose courage and your strength (rih) departs...﴾ (8:46). That is: your strength departs, whatever that strength may be. Even the fisherman who rides the sea in a small boat, propelling it with oars by the strength of his hand and muscles, that too is a force and does not fall outside this meaning.

Thus the meaning of the verse remains applicable to every time and every place, until the Hour is established.

When "rih" (wind) is used in the singular, it indicates the occurrence of evil and harm, as in His saying: ﴿And in 'Ad, when We sent upon them the barren wind﴾ (51:41); and His saying: ﴿and your strength departs﴾ (8:46); and His saying: ﴿Rather, it is that which you sought to hasten: a wind in which is a painful punishment﴾ (22:24).

And when it comes in the plural form, it indicates goodness, as in His saying: ﴿And We send the fertilizing winds﴾ (15:22).

We have previously discussed the role of the wind in the cohesion of things and their standing by themselves. The towering mountain that you see firm and fixed is only stable through the effect of the wind upon it and its encompassing it from every side, such that if the air were emptied from one side of the mountain, it would collapse. This is the principle upon which the bomb is based: air is what erects and holds buildings and skyscrapers in place, because it surrounds them from every side, producing this balance; if it is emptied from one of their sides, the building collapses.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿and He holds back the sky from falling upon the earth except by His permission...﴾ (22:65). The sky is raised above us without pillars; none holds it above us except Allah, by His power and self-subsistence, from falling upon the earth except by His permission, the Exalted. As He said in another verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; and if they should cease, none could hold them after Him...﴾ (35:41).

﴿Indeed, Allah is Kind and Merciful to the people﴾ (22:65). Among His attributes, the Exalted, are ra'fa (kindness) and rahma (mercy). A superficial understanding of these two attributes sees them as one, but they are two different attributes. Ra'fa removes afflictions, while rahma increases bounties. The principle is that averting harm always takes precedence over bringing benefit. Your Lord is kind to you, so He removes the causes of pain from you before bringing you benefit through His mercy.

We had previously clarified this matter with an example: suppose one person throws a stone at you and another throws you an apple. Which will occupy you first? Without doubt, you will be occupied with the stone: how will you protect yourself from its harm before trying to obtain the apple?

Therefore He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if Allah were to seize the people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave upon it [the earth] a single creature, but He defers them to a specified term...﴾ (16:61).

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿It is He who gave you life, then will cause you to die, then will give you life again. Indeed, man is ungrateful.﴾ (22:66)

Al-Haqq, blessed and exalted is He, reminds us of some of His blessings and of some of the processes which, if we follow them, would bring us to stand upon the blessings of God upon us, and we would never forget them.

The first of them: ﴿It is He who gave you life...﴾ (22:66). Al-Ihya' (giving life) is that the one who gives life bestows upon what he gives life a strength by which it performs the task for which it was created. The first giving of life was in Adam (peace be upon him), when his Lord created him, shaped him, and breathed into him of His spirit; then He brought us into being, we who are from his offspring.

﴿Then will cause you to die...﴾ (22:66). Just as creation is one of the signs of God, so too death is a sign of God, which we see and touch. As long as you believe in the sign of creation and the sign of death, and see them, and have no doubt concerning them, then when we tell you that after this there is another life, believe it, because the Possessor of these signs is one, and the premises which you judge to be true must lead to a conclusion which you also judge to be true, and here are the premises before you, true.

Therefore, He, exalted is He, says after that: ﴿Then will give you life again...﴾ (22:66). Al-Ihya' is used in the Qur'an with several meanings, among them the material life which is manifested in movement, eating and drinking, and among them the life in the Hereafter, of which God said: ﴿And indeed, the Last Abode - that is the [true] life, if they only knew.﴾ (29:64).

This is the real life, because the life of this world is subject to change, and man fluctuates within it between strength and weakness, health and sickness, wealth and poverty, youth and old age, and after that it is subject to cessation. As for the life of the Hereafter, which God described as al-Hayawan (the life), meaning: an intensification of life, it is a life in which there is no change and no cessation.

So: you have two lives: a life for the structure of matter, by which you move, feel and live, and another life which endures and has no cessation.

Therefore, the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life...﴾ (8:24). How then, since we are alive? They said: "That which gives you life" is not the material worldly life which is subject to change; rather, it gives you the real life in the Hereafter, the enduring life which does not cease, of which God said: ﴿And indeed, the Last Abode - that is the [true] life, if they only knew.﴾ (29:64). That is: the true knowledge which guides its possessor.

If the material worldly life is by the breathing of the spirit into man, then by what is the second life? ﴿When He calls you to that which gives you life...﴾ (8:24).

They said: this life is also by a spirit, but other than the first spirit; it is by the spirit of the Qur'an, of which God said: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a Spirit of Our command...﴾ (42:52). And He called the angel who descends with it a spirit: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ (26:193).

So the second spirit, which gives you the real, eternal life, is the method of God in His noble Book; if you follow it, you attain this enduring, eternal life and enjoy in it what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no heart of man has conceived, and it is neither cut off nor prevented.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful.﴾ (22:66). Kafur (ungrateful): an intensive form of kafir (disbelieving), and the kafur is one who did not recognize the right of the blessing-giver regarding the blessing, although if he had clearly perceived it, he would never have ceased to thank the Blessing-Giver, glorified is He.

Man passes through various stages between life and death, as God says: ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice and given us life twice, and we have acknowledged our sins. So is there to an exit any way?"﴾ (40:11). So when will they say this statement?

They said: this is the Day of Resurrection. God gave them life from the death of non-existence, so He gave them life in the world, then caused them to die, then gave them life in the Hereafter. So there is a death before bringing into existence, and a death after bringing into existence; then comes the resurrection on the Day of Judgment.

As for His saying: ﴿It is He who gave you life...﴾ (22:66): it is a matter which the Creator, Mighty and Majestic, has stated, and which no one has claimed for himself, despite the abundance of disbelievers, atheists and charlatans in every time and place. We have not heard of anyone claiming the matter of creation. This is a matter at which we must pause and inquire: why has no one appeared who claims it? And if no one has claimed creation, and no one has claimed giving life, then who, then, is the owner of creation, giving life and causing death?

If people concern themselves with and record the history of any inventor who invented a machine, for example, they say: the inventor of electricity was so-and-so, who lived in such-and-such a town, and his affair was such-and-such, and he learned from such-and-such, and obtained such-and-such, etc. How then of the One who created you and gave you life from non-existence? Especially since this matter has not been boastfully claimed by anyone, so the matter is established for Him, glorified and exalted is He.

Then the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿For every community We have appointed rites (manasik) which they perform. So let them not dispute with you the matter, and invite to your Lord; indeed you are upon a straight guidance.﴾ (22:67)

Al-Haqq (the Truth), glorified and exalted is He, created Adam, peace be upon him, as His khalifah (vicegerent) on earth, and gave him training in his mission through the divine command and the divine prohibition. He informed him of the enmity of Satan towards him and his offspring, and warned him not to follow his footsteps. This test came to an end with Adam's descent from the Garden to the earth, to undertake his mission as the vicegerent of God on His earth, on condition that he remain mindful of his experience with Satan. God subjected to him everything in existence, to serve him and to work for his sake.

Then God sent down to him a method (manhaj) by which to live, so that the movement of his life and the life of his descendants might be set right. He reminded him of the earlier training method with which he had been charged in the Garden, and of what happened to him when he opposed his Lord's method, when his nakedness appeared: ﴿And they began to fasten over themselves from the leaves of the Garden...﴾ (7:22) [al-A'raf].

Likewise, if you oppose this divine method in this world, your nakedness (awrat) will appear. Therefore, whenever you see any nakedness in society, in any respect, in social life, in the economy, in upbringing, know that one of God's rulings has been disabled, and so a blemish of the society's blemishes has appeared, because the method of God is the law of preservation which protects you and organizes your life so that you can carry out your mission in life.

It is like when you enter your house and find an appliance of the house not performing its task; you know that it has a fault, so you take it to the specialist engineer responsible for its maintenance. Likewise, if something in your lives ceases to perform its task, return it to its maintainer: to God and to the Messenger. This is firm reasoning which everyone, believer and unbeliever alike, acknowledges: that a made thing is referred back to its maker, and to the one who knows the law of its maintenance. No one has claimed that they created you, so when a defect occurs in you, you must go to your Lord and Creator.

Therefore, when a matter overwhelmed the Prophet (ﷺ), he would stand up to prayer. The meaning of "hazabahu amr" (a matter overwhelmed him) is: something beyond his capacity and means; he would hasten to prayer to present himself before his Lord, mighty and majestic. So if you find in yourself a fault in any respect, you have only to perform ablution and stand before your Lord that He may set right what has been disabled in you.

If the engineer repairs the appliance with a material thing, even a small piece of wire, your Lord, mighty and majestic, is unseen, and His remedy too is unseen; it comes to you from where you do not know.

The method which God has laid down for the preservation of His creatures has principles and has branches. The principles: that you believe in the one God, the Acting, the Choosing; this is a foundation on which none of the heavenly messages has ever differed, as He, exalted, says: ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah, and that which We revealed to you...﴾ (42:13) [al-Shura].

These are principles on which no religion among the religions differs. But since people were scattered across the various corners of the earth, each community living isolated from the others because of the great distances and the absence of the means of communication and contact that we see today, which have made the whole world one village, so that what happens in the farthest East you see and hear about in the farthest West, at the same time. When people lived in this isolation, no one knew of anyone else, to the point that only two hundred years ago they were discovering new continents.

This isolation resulted in the multiplication of ailments according to the multiplication of communities. So a messenger or prophet would come to treat the ailments of one particular community, being sent specifically to his people: this one to treat the matter of measure and balance, that one to treat the tyranny of wealth, another to treat the deviation and aberration of dispositions, and another to treat tribal fanaticism.

As for the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), it came at the beginning of the meeting of communities here and there, so his message (ﷺ) was general for all mankind. You find that the principles of the messages of Moses, Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them, are one set of principles, while the branches differ according to the differences of environments.

But since it was within His knowledge, exalted is He, that this isolation would end, and that these environments would come together and meet upon a single matter, and that their ailments would become one, He therefore sent the final Messenger to them all across time and place.

In this verse, ﴿For every community We have appointed rites (manasik) which they perform...﴾ (22:67): that is, the Truth, glorified is He, has appointed for every nation among the nations to which messengers were sent rites suited to the requirements of their time, because they were isolated from one another, as He, exalted, says: ﴿For each of you We have appointed a law and a way...﴾ (5:48) [al-Ma'idah].

Thus the laws differ in the branches suited to the time, the place and the environment, but the morals and the beliefs are one. God, mighty and majestic, is one God in all the heavenly religions, and lying is forbidden in all the heavenly religions; no prophet came to permit his people to lie.

Al-mansak (the rite): the method of worship, and from it is His saying: ﴿Say: Indeed my prayer, my rites (nusuk), my living and my dying are for God, Lord of the worlds﴾ (6:162) [al-An'am].

﴿they perform it...﴾ (22:67): meaning, they carry it out.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿So let them not dispute with you the matter...﴾ (22:67): such as their saying: you are a messenger, and we too follow a messenger who has a method and a law. Yes, but this is the final law, which came dominant over all the laws before it, and suited to new affairs.

Therefore the Truth, blessed and exalted is He, reassures His Messenger (ﷺ) afterwards: ﴿And invite to your Lord; indeed you are upon a straight guidance﴾ (22:67): meaning, be reassured. You are upon the truth, so invite to your Lord, for you are upon a straight guidance which will reach them: if not as faith, then as reform and a human legislation which the events and problems of life will compel them to, so they will find no better than the law of God to rule by, even if they do not believe.

It is as though the Truth, glorified is He, were saying to His Messenger (ﷺ): do not dispute with them, and they will not dispute with you, and take what God has commanded you: ﴿So proclaim what you are commanded and turn away from the polytheists﴾ (15:94) [al-Hijr]: those who argue with you and dispute with you about the message. Matters will befall them in proportion to the wickedness they commit, and they will turn to your law and your legislation to resolve their problems with it.

Guidance is described as straight because it is guidance from God, which He has fashioned for you: the guidance of the Creator, who knows all the faculties of the human soul and has legislated for each faculty what suits it, and the events of life will compel them to what God has legislated for His vicegerency on earth.

1 al-Mansak: the place where the nusk (sacrifice) is slaughtered. And al-mansak: the law of ritual, which is slaughter. And al-manasik: acts of worship. [Lisan al-Arab, root: nasaka].

Then the Almighty, glory to Him, says:

﴿And if they dispute with you, say: "Allah knows best what you are doing."﴾ (22:68)

Al-Jidal (dispute, argumentation): it is derived from "jadala al-habl," meaning the twisting of a rope's strands together to strengthen it. Even if it is a thin thread, we twist it so that it gains thickness and strength. For that thread, when we twist it, decreases in length, because its parts interlock and it becomes stronger. Thus al-jidal is the strengthening and firming of a thing, and likewise al-jidal (disputation), which is an attempt to strengthen one's proof before an opponent.

In another verse: ﴿And argue with them in the best manner...﴾ (16:125) [An-Nahl]. The meaning is: if they dispute with you after [using] the best manner, then say ﴿"Allah knows best what you are doing."﴾ (22:68) [Al-Hajj]. That is: refer them back to Allah and submit the matter to Him. Therefore there follows after it:

﴿Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that about which you used to differ.﴾ (22:69)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 22, verse 69:

﴿Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that wherein you used to differ.﴾ (22:69)

Note that the Exalted did not say: "He will judge between us and you," as the meaning would normally require, since you are two parties who argue. It is as though the Blessed and Exalted is saying to His Messenger (ﷺ): Leave them, for they will differ among themselves, and the dispute will not remain with you, because disagreement over one thing arises from the desires of the soul, and the desire of the soul arises from eagerness for temporal authority. That is to say: ease your mind, for your Lord will judge between them concerning that wherein they used to differ.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 70:

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heaven and the earth? Indeed, that is in a Book. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.﴾ (70)

This is a matter that the Truth, glory be to Him, has decided for Himself, and no one has claimed it. None knows what is in the heaven and the earth except Allah. This verse came after the ruling on the dispute, so someone may object and say: "If the matter is from Allah as rulings that organize the movement of life, and every messenger has come with them, then what is the necessity for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to come to all people?"

We have said that religion is of two kinds. One kind does not differ with the differences of messengers, nations and eras. This concerns the general, comprehensive matters that do not change, namely the beliefs, the fundamentals and the morals. The other kind differs with the differences of eras and nations, so the ruling comes suited to each era and each nation.

Since the Truth, glory be to Him, is the One who will judge between the two parties, He said: ﴿Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heaven and the earth..﴾ (70) [al-Hajj]: I know every thing that exists in the universe, its outward and its inward. So I judge with knowledge and from complete experience.

﴿Indeed, that is in a Book..﴾ (70) [al-Hajj]: Knowledge is one thing, and the Book is another thing. Since Allah, exalted is He, knows everything, and since He, glory be to Him, neither errs nor forgets, what is the necessity of the Book?

They said: The Book here refers to the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz), which contains everything. In another verse He said: ﴿No! Indeed, it is a reminder. So whoever wills may remember it. In honored scriptures, exalted, purified, by the hands of scribes, noble and virtuous.﴾ [Abasa].

Even the Qur'an itself is in that Book: ﴿Rather, it is a glorious Qur'an, in a Preserved Tablet.﴾ [al-Buruj].

And He, exalted, said: ﴿Allah erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.﴾ [al-Ra'd] And He says: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but He knows it, nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything fresh or dry, but it is in a clear Book.﴾ [al-An'am]

So the necessity of the Book is for your own sake and to inform the angels who are present, that the things that will happen in the future were written by Allah from eternity. Their coming in the future in accordance with what He wrote is proof of His knowledge of them. The One who wrote a thing before it existed, and then the thing came in agreement with what was written, is the greatest proof of His knowledge and encompassing comprehension.

Thus, the coming of the Book is not to help us with anything, but rather to be a proof against you. It will be said to you: ﴿Read your record; your soul is sufficient against you this Day as a reckoner.﴾ [al-Isra'] Here is your history, and here is your story. It is not words from us, but your deeds, and the proof is against you.

The knowledge of Allah, exalted, in His saying: ﴿He knows what is in the heaven and the earth..﴾ (70) [al-Hajj] carries the promise and the threat at one time, and this is among the wonders of Qur'anic expression, that it gives a thing and its opposite. How? Suppose you have two sons, one of whom wronged the other in your absence. When you returned, each of them hurried to complain about the other. You said to them: "Be silent, I do not want to hear your voice. I know what happened, and I will arrange for each of you what suits him and what he deserves according to what I know." Without doubt, the wronged one will rejoice and be glad, and the wrongdoer will fear and his color will change.

Thus, Allah's knowledge of everything in the heaven and the earth, and His encompassing of what passes between His creatures, is a promise to the one in the right and a threat to the one in falsehood.

1 - Said by Ibn 'Abbas, as related from him by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh. Cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/74).

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that for which He has sent down no authority, and of which they have no knowledge. And for the wrongdoers there is no helper.﴾ (22:71)

It seems that worship — which is obedience to a command and avoidance of a prohibition — must proceed from a higher authority above all of us. None of us has the right to legislate for another, commanding him or forbidding him, for a command from one who is equal to you has no preponderance (lā murajjiḥ lahu), and he may say to you: "Why are you commanding me while I obey?" But if the command comes from one above you, you obey without objection, and you have the proof that the command comes from above. You say: "My father commanded me to do such and such," or "My Lord commanded me to do such and such, or forbade me from such and such."

Thus: every evidence for the ruling on an act or an abstention must originate from the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, for He is above me and above you. If I submit to His command and prohibition, there is no fault or harm upon me, because I have not submitted to an equal; I have submitted to Allah, to whom you and I are both servants, and there is no shame in following His judgment.

Therefore, among the rural folk they say: "Whoever is cut by the Sharia's finger, no blood flows from it" (allī al-sharʿ yiqṭaʿ ṣubāʿahu mayikhrish damm). Why? Because you did not cut it; it was Allah who cut it. So there is in the matter no domination or tyranny from anyone, and no humiliation or subjection to anyone.

As for His words, ﴿And they worship, besides Allah...﴾ (71): meaning, they worship other than Him, the Exalted. ﴿That for which He has sent down no authority...﴾ (71): authority (sulṭān) is either the authority of coercion or the authority of proof. The authority of coercion is that it compels you and forces you to do what you did not want to do; the authority of proof is that it convinces you and establishes for you by argument that you should act by your own choice. These deities they worship besides Allah have no authority, neither coercion nor proof.

Therefore, in Iblis's argument on the Day of Resurrection with those who followed him, he says to them: ﴿And I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me...﴾ (Ibrahim 14:22). Meaning: you were inclined by a hint and you responded to me; I had no authority over you — no force by which I could compel you to disobedience, and no proof by which I could convince you.

Then He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And that of which they have no knowledge...﴾ (71): meaning, the knowledge of ijtihad (ʿilm al-ijtihād, scholarly deduction), which derives rulings from the general judgment that the Truth, blessed and exalted, has sent down. This is the proof of knowledge of which Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, those who derive it from them would have known it...﴾ (An-Nisa 4:83). Meaning: the people of knowledge.

So: worship must be grounded in authority from Allah — a definitive, explicit text that admits no dispute — or in the ijtihad of the people of knowledge.

As for His words, ﴿And for the wrongdoers there is no helper﴾ (71): He did not say, "The wrongdoers will not be victorious," nor did He negate victory from them, because that is an established matter; rather, no one will come forward to aid them. So they will not be victorious, and no one will help them. No one comes forward to help another unless the one being helped is weak.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted, says:

﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you see denial in the faces of those who disbelieve. They almost assault those who recite Our verses to them. Say: "Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve, and wretched is the destination."﴾ (22:72)

This verse depicts the state of the disbelievers when they hear the Book of Allah and His verses from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) or his Companions. When they hear them, ﴿denial is recognised in the faces of those who disbelieve﴾: that is, the aversion can be seen and read in their faces as frowning, scowling, anger and agitation. They deny what they hear, and their agitation almost turns into a furious impulse that would destroy those who recite the Qur'an, because of the evil and hatred within them toward what is recited to them.

Therefore Allah says after it: ﴿They almost assault those who recite Our verses to them.﴾ "As-sataw" (assault) means to destroy and to seize violently, because the emotional state that occupies their souls first appears on their faces as an agitation that signals something they wish to inflict upon the believers; then the emotion turns into a bodily impulse, which is destruction and violent seizure.

(Qul) "Say" is in reply to them: "What angers you so that you assault us and hate what we recite to you from the Book of Allah?" Their rage and hatred on hearing the Qur'an is evidence of their inability to answer with proof, and also of their inability to believe; therefore they fluctuate between rage and hatred.

Therefore He addresses them with His saying: ﴿Say: "Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve."﴾ That is: "Why do I see you enraged at the signs of Allah and averse to them now, while the matter is still minor? Does merely hearing the verses produce all this in you? What then will you be when you encounter the Fire in the Hereafter? The rage you think is evil, for which you assault us, is a trivial matter, and there is something worse awaiting you: ﴿the Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve.﴾"

Similar to this is the stance of the Companion Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) when he made the chieftains of Quraysh stand at the door and brought forward the weak believers before them. They became angry at that and their noses swelled, so he said to them: "Do your noses swell that I have brought them forward before you now? How will you be when Allah brings them forward before you into Paradise?"

As for the word ﴿promised (wa'adaha)﴾: the word "promise" (al-wa'd) is always used for good, but here it is used in the sense of mockery of them and belittling them, as He said in another verse: ﴿So give them the tidings of a painful punishment﴾ (84:24). When one hears good tidings, he looks forward to good, so the punishment strikes him unexpectedly, and it is then more grievous to him.

Among the same usage is His saying: ﴿And if they seek relief, they will be relieved with water like molten brass that scalds the faces﴾ (18:29), because the constriction of the soul and its despair after the first signs of relief is more severe than the punishment itself.

And His saying: ﴿And wretched is the destination (wa-bi'sa al-masir)﴾ (22:72): that is, "Wretched is your end and your return."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 73:

﴿O mankind, a parable is presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it. And if the fly should snatch away from them anything, they could not retrieve it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought.﴾ (22:73):

We say: ḍarb (striking, presenting) is the placing of one thing upon another with force, and from it we say "ḍarabnā al-dīnār," meaning: after it was a piece of gold or silver, for example, it became a known currency in circulation.

And mathal (parable, similitude) is the likening of something unknown to something else that is known, and is strange and wondrous, fixing itself in the mind, just as we describe to you a person you have not seen by a person you know. We say: "He is the mathal of so-and-so." And thus are all comparisons: something you want to make known to the addressee, and he does not know it.

From it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their likeness is that of one who kindled a fire, and when it illuminated what was around him, Allah took away their light and left them in darkness, not seeing.﴾ (2:17) [al-Baqarah].

And His saying: ﴿So his likeness is that of a dog: if you chase it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants. That is the likeness of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories that perhaps they will reflect.﴾ (7:176) [al-A'raf].

And His saying: ﴿The likeness of those who take protectors other than Allah is like the spider, which takes a house; and indeed the frailest of houses is the spider's house, if only they knew.﴾ (29:41) [al-'Ankabut].

So then: the amthal (parables) are an informing about something known so that knowledge of it may reach something unknown. And the word "mathal" has become characterized by being a parable that is wondrous in its composition, eloquent and concise, such that tongues transmit it quickly in a few words.

If you found, for example, a negligent student who was lazy all year and did not study, and then when the examination came he began to strive in study, you would say to him: "(Before the shooting, fill the quivers)," meaning: before you hunt with arrows, you must prepare them first and fill your quiver with them. This is a parable struck for preparing for a matter before it arrives.

Among the proverbs of the rural folk they say: "(Give the bread to its baker, even if he eats half of it)," and it is struck for one who entrusts a craft to other than its craftsman and its specialist.

And they say of one who falls short in a matter entrusted to him: "(The carpenter's door is loose)."

And when you send someone to accomplish a need for you and he succeeds in it and brings the desired result, he says to you: "(The churning has revealed the butter)," and churning is the process of agitating milk in a waterskin to separate the butter from the milk.

Thus, a mathal is a concise, eloquent saying uttered on a particular occasion, and then people used it, for its lightness, beauty and eloquence, in similar situations. The mathal remains in its original state without change, and its wording must be kept with the singular, dual and plural, and with the masculine and feminine. For example, if you send a messenger to accomplish a need for you, then when he returns you say to him: "(What is behind you, O 'Iṣām)," with the kasra in address to a feminine even though he is a man. Why? Because the saying was first uttered to a feminine, so it remained in this feminine form even if the addressee is masculine.

The story of this mathal is that al-Ḥārith, king of Kinda, wanted to marry Umm Iyās, and he sent someone to propose to her on his behalf. Her name was 'Iṣām. When the envoy went to her, her mother said to her: "The woman has come to propose to you on behalf of so-and-so, so do not hide anything from her, let her smell you if she wishes, and answer her in what she asks you." When she entered upon the girl and wished to see her body, the girl took off her garment and uncovered her body. The woman said: "(Abandoning deception is from uncovering the veil)," and it became a proverb. Then she returned to al-Ḥārith, and he met her hastily, wanting to return her, and said: "(What is behind you, O 'Iṣām?)," meaning: what is the news? So the proverb remained in this form for the feminine, even when addressed to the masculine.

Allah, blessed and exalted, strikes this parable for you and says: take it into your minds, pay attention to it, open your ears well and understand it, for it will benefit you in your relationship with the Messenger of Allah and with the believers.

The address here is directed to people in general, not restricted to anyone in particular: ﴿O mankind, a parable has been presented to you, so listen to it...﴾ (22:73). He did not say "O believers," because this parable is directed at the disbelievers, and the believers have no need of it. ﴿So listen to it...﴾ (22:73): meaning: be attentive and understand its intent and its aim, so that you may move in your conduct in accordance with what it contains and according to what you have understood of its meaning.

So what is this parable?

﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for it...﴾ (22:73).

That is: those you worship and turn to besides Allah ﴿will never create a fly...﴾ (22:73): and it is the smallest of creatures ﴿...even if they gathered together for it...﴾ (22:73): meaning: their efforts combined and their affair unified altogether, not one by one. This is an escalation in the challenge, as it increases the strength of the opponent.

Just as the Qur'an escalated in challenging the Arabs: it first challenged them to produce the like of the Qur'an, and since the Qur'an is long, it challenged them to ten surahs and they could not; then it challenged them with a single surah and they could not.

Then it escalates the challenge, saying: gather all your eloquent and rhetorical ones, and even the jinn helping you, and you will not be able: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like...﴾ (17:88).

As for His saying: ﴿will never create a fly...﴾ (22:73): He used the negation of the future, and did not say "they did not create."
