So the negation here is for perpetuity: they were not able in the past, and they will not be able afterward either, lest anyone think that they might be able to do so in the days to come. Negating the verb in this manner, in the sense of perpetuity, is because you may leave the act while you are capable of it; but when you challenge with it, you act to answer that challenge. So Allah, exalted is He, made clear to them that they were not able before the challenge, and will not be able after the challenge.

Then He, exalted, says: ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them anything, they could not retrieve it from it...﴾ (22:73). You might say: this act of creation is a difficult act, one not used as a challenge, so He challenged them with something easier than creation: ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them anything, they could not retrieve it from it...﴾ (22:73). Can anyone restore what the fly has taken from its food on its wings, its feet, or its proboscis?

They used to slaughter sacrifices at the idols and place food before them to bless it, so blood would flow there and scatter upon them, and the flies would gather around them and take some of this blood on their slender feet, or on their wings, or on their proboscis. So He challenged them to restore what the fly had taken, and this matter is easier than the matter of creation.

You may try this yourself: if a fly lands on the honey in front of you, it must take some of it, though it is tiny, imperceptible, unweighable, and you can hardly see it. But can you catch the fly and return what it has taken from you?

Therefore He, exalted, says after it: ﴿Weak are the seeker and the sought.﴾ (22:73): meaning: both are weak. The fly in itself is weak, and they too are weak, as is evident from their inability in this matter. But there is a weak one who claims strength, and a weak one whose strength lies in his acknowledging his weakness. The fly, though weak, is mentioned by Allah, exalted, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to strike a parable of a gnat or what is above it...﴾ (2:26): meaning: what is above it in smallness, not what is above it in size, such as a sparrow, for example.

Then the Truthful, glorified and exalted be He, says:

﴿They have not measured God with His true measure. Surely God is Strong, Mighty.﴾ (74)

That is: these disbelievers who worship, besides God, gods that cannot create a fly, and cannot even retrieve from the fly what it has taken, have not known God's true measure (qadr). Had they known God's measure, they would not have worshipped other than Him.

Qadr means the measure of a thing. We have said that the measures of things differ according to what one wishes to know of their measure. Length, for example, has a unit by which its magnitude is measured, but this unit differs according to what is being measured. If you wish to measure the distance between Cairo and Alexandria, for example, you do not use the millimetre, the centimetre, or even the metre; rather you use the kilometre. If you wish to buy a piece of cloth you say metre; but if you want a passport photograph you say centimetre.

So everything has a measure by which it is assessed and a standard by which it is gauged. If you want distance, you measure length; if you want area, you measure length times breadth; if you want volume, you measure length times breadth times height. Length is measured in metres, area in square metres, and volume in cubic metres. Likewise in weight, you measure in kilos, pounds, or grams, and so on.

Qadr also comes with the meaning of constriction, as in the words of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿But when He tries him, and restricts his provision (qadara 'alayhi rizqahu)..﴾ (16) [al-Fajr].

And the Lord, Glorified is He, says: ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted (qudira 'alayhi rizquhu), let him spend from what God has given him..﴾ (7) [al-Talaq].

Measure, as it applies to material things, applies also to immaterial ones. For example, you express material increase by saying: "So-and-so has grown," meaning he has matured and increased. In immaterial matters, the Lord, Glorified is He, uses the same idea: ﴿It is a grave word that comes out of their mouths..﴾ (5) [al-Kahf], meaning: it is magnified.

Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is not matter, because He, Glorified is He, is above matter. So the meaning of measure with respect to Him, Exalted is He, is the greatness of His perfect attributes. ﴿They have not measured God with His true measure..﴾ (74) [al-Hajj]: they did not glorify Him with the glorification that is due to Him, and they did not know His measure. Had they known, they would not have worshipped other than Him, nor would they have worshipped anyone alongside Him from these gods which cannot create a fly, nor even retrieve what the fly has taken from them. How then do they equate these with God and compare them with Him, Mighty and Majestic? If they truly knew God's measure, they would have been ashamed of all of that.

Then the verse concludes with His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Surely God is Strong, Mighty.﴾ (74) [al-Hajj]. What is the connection between these two attributes and the context we are dealing with?

They said: because Allah, Glorified and Exalted, spoke in the previous parable about those who turned away from His worship to the worship of idols, and said: ﴿Weak are the seeker and the sought.﴾ (73) [al-Hajj]. In contrast to this weakness, He said: surely God is Strong. He is strong against the worshipper, because He has no need of his worship, and strong against the worshipped, because if He willed He could crush it. Since you have turned away from God and worshipped other than Him, this involves harm, as though there were a battle. In that case, God is Mighty and cannot be overcome.

The verse ﴿They have not measured God with His true measure..﴾ (74) [al-Hajj] occurs in several places in the Book of God, among them: ﴿And they did not measure God with His true measure when they said, "God has not sent down anything upon a human."..﴾ (91) [al-An'am]. They did not know God's measure, because they accused Him, while He, Glorified is He, possesses perfect justice. How would He charge His servants with worship and not convey to them through a messenger? He, Glorified is He, says: ﴿And We would not punish until We sent a messenger.﴾ (15) [al-Isra'].

So when they say: ﴿God has not sent down anything upon a human,﴾ (91) [al-An'am], it is as though they describe the Truthful, Glorified is He, as punishing people without conveying anything to them. He responds to them on this matter: ﴿Say, "Who sent down the Book which Moses brought..?"﴾ (91) [al-An'am].

In another place: ﴿They have not measured God with His true measure, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand..﴾ (67) [al-Zumar].

We say: "qaddarahu haqqa qadrihi" and "qaddarahu qadrahu", as if things differ in the assessment of things. For example, you look at a room and say: "This is roughly 4 by 5," which is a general, approximate estimate. But if you take the measure and assess it precisely, you may find it larger or smaller. For the former you say: "I estimated the room's size." For the latter you say: "I measured the room's true size."

Accordingly, if you wish to measure God the Exalted with His true measure, you measure Him according to the capacity of the human intellect; but His true measure is not something you can encompass, because His perfections are infinite and cannot be fully grasped.

Among this is what we have mentioned earlier about the knowledge of certainty ('ilm al-yaqin), the eye of certainty ('ayn al-yaqin), and the truth of certainty (haqq al-yaqin). When the words of Allah, Exalted is He, were revealed: ﴿O you who believe, fear God with His true fear..﴾ (102) [Al 'Imran], some of the Companions(1) said: "And who can do that? It is a difficult matter that we fear God with the complete fear He deserves, Mighty and Majestic." So God, Exalted is He, revealed: ﴿So fear God as much as you are able﴾ (16) [al-Taghabun], and it was revealed: ﴿God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾ (286) [al-Baqarah].

And the Prophet (ﷺ), when he praised God, Exalted is He, would say: "Glory be to You, we cannot count the praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself." (2)

Why? Because no one, however eloquent in expression, can praise God with the praise that befits Him, Glorified is He. Out of God's mercy to His servants, this matter has been lifted from them, and the Truthful, Glorified is He, praised Himself and taught us how to praise Him. So when the eloquent speaks and praises God with the varieties of speech and commendation, the inarticulate one who does not master speech is reassured, since he praises his Lord with what he has been taught of praise, and with formulas that the philosopher says and that the shepherd says too.

Had God not taught us the formula of praise in Surat al-Fatihah, saying: ﴿All praise is due to God, Lord of the worlds﴾ (2) [al-Fatihah], we would not have learned this formula. So God's teaching His servants the formula of praise is itself a blessing that deserves praise, and the praise deserves praise, and so on in an endless chain, so that the Truthful, Blessed and Exalted, remains ever praised, and the servant remains ever praising.

1 - On the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, one of the senior Successors, who said: When this verse was revealed, the people found the obligation burdensome; they stood in prayer until their ankles swelled and their foreheads became raw. So God revealed, as a lightening for the Muslims: ﴿So fear God as much as you are able﴾ (16) [al-Taghabun], and the first verse was abrogated. [Related by Ibn Abi Hatim]. And concerning Ibn 'Abbas's words on ﴿Fear God with His true fear﴾ (102) [Al 'Imran], he said: it was not abrogated, but "His true fear" means that they strive for God with the striving due to Him, do not fear the blame of any blamer in God's cause, and stand for justice for God even against themselves, their fathers, and their mothers. [Related by Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Nahhas in his book on abrogation]. Both are cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2/283.

2 - Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (6/58, 120), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (486), from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her, who said: I missed the Messenger of God (ﷺ) one night from the bed, and I searched for him, and my hand fell upon the soles of his feet while he was in the mosque, and they were upright, and he was saying: "O God, I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, and in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in You from You. I cannot count the praise of You; You are as You have praised Yourself."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 75:

After the Truth, glory be to Him, spoke about the matter of divinity (ulūhiyya) and what befits it of absolute perfection, and warned against attributing to it what is not of it and what does not befit it, which is the summit of beliefs, and after we believe in the divine matters with this purity and cleanse our faith of everything that taints it, there must be a conveying (balagh) of this divine power in which we have believed, and this conveying happens through the sending of messengers. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.﴾ (22:75)

So then: the second stage in faith, after believing in the divine summit, is belief in the messengers. ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind...﴾ (22:75). And al-iṣṭifā' (choosing): selecting an elite from among many. Choosing a few from the many is evidence that they are the essence and the elite. Just as choosing differs according to the one chosen, if the one doing the choosing is Allah, the Exalted, then He must choose the essence of the essence.

Choosing (al-iṣṭifā') pervades the whole of existence: He chooses from among the angels messengers, and from among mankind messengers; He chooses from time, and He chooses from place, just as He chose Ramadan from time and the Ka'bah from place. The Truth, glory be to Him, did not make choosing a means of privileging the chosen over others; rather, it is so that His choosing spreads over the creation of Allah. When He chose Ramadan over all of time, it was not to pamper Ramadan, but so that you take from it a charge that strengthens your spirit and purifies the rest of the days, so that you benefit from the good of your deeds in them.

Choosing may recur with a difference in what it is related to. Therefore the orientalists paused at the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds﴾ (3:42).

They say: What is the benefit of repeating the choosing here? If we reflect on the verse, we find a difference between the first choosing and the second. The first choosing is a choosing because you are a worshipful, pure, devoted one, secluded in your sanctuary for Allah; but the second choosing is a choosing above all the women of the worlds, by your being a mother to a child without a father. So the object of choosing is different.

In the matter of choosing, the angels are divided into angels who are chosen and angels from among whom [messengers] are chosen. In another verse He, exalted, says: ﴿Who made the angels messengers﴾ (35:1): meaning, all of them have a message, along with other worlds besides us.

As for the verse before us, the discussion concerns the angels who have a connection with humans, such as Jibril, Mikha'il, Israfil and 'Azra'il, and the recording guardians and those charged with protecting the human being. Allah, the Exalted, chooses these. As for the rest of them, Allah chooses them for His worship; they are absorbed (muhayyamūn), not knowing anything of this creation. They are the exalted angels (al-mala'ika al-'ālūn) about whom Allah spoke in the account of Iblis: ﴿Have you become arrogant, or have you been among the exalted?﴾ (38:75), meaning: those not included in the command to prostrate, because they have another task.

Then He, exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾ (22:75). Hearing relates to sounds, and seeing relates to actions, and these two, as we have said, are the foundation of all the senses. The Truth, glory be to Him, in His saying ﴿Hearing and Seeing﴾ (22:75) makes clear to us that His messengers will be confronted with words that hurt them and mockery, and they will meet with deeds that obstruct the course of their call. So let this be known, lest it weaken their resolve: and I am with them, Hearing what is said, Seeing what is done; they are under My hearing, My sight and My protection.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 76:

﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and to Allah all matters are returned.﴾ (22:76)

﴿What is before them﴾ (22:76): that is, what is in front of them. He also knows what is behind them. So let man do what he wishes; the knowledge of Allah encompasses him.

﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾ (22:76): the final return is to Him, glory be to Him. The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, did not create His creatures to leave them neglected. Rather, He created them for a wisdom, and appointed for them an end at which each will be recompensed for his deeds. Whoever has toiled and exerted himself in the cause of Allah's call and borne hardships in supporting the messengers of Allah, for him is his reward. And whoever confronted them and opposed them, whether with abusive, insulting, mocking words, or with deeds that obstruct their call, for him too is the punishment he deserves.

After our Lord, mighty and majestic, spoke to us about the divine matters and about the messengers who convey from Him, glory be to Him, He now speaks to us about the method (manhaj) which they will bring to organize the movement of our life. This method is summarized in "do such and such, and do not do such and such." Its commands and prohibitions do not encompass every movement of life. The commands and prohibitions are confined to a number of matters, and the rest is permissible, because Allah, exalted is He, placed the commands and prohibitions in the fundamentals that protect the movement of life from desires and whims, and left the rest to your choice, so that you may do it in whatever manner you wish.

Therefore we see the scholars striving (ijtihad) and differing over such matters that Allah has left to us. Had He wished, glory be to Him, He would have sent down in them a decisive ruling (hukm muhkam) upon which no one would differ. And you may say: why did the Truth, glory be to Him, leave these matters where opinions clash, views differ, and disputes arise among people?

They said: this is the will of Allah, because Allah, exalted is He, created man subjected (musakhkhar) in some things and free-choosing (mukhtar) in other things. So people should let the mujtahid strive as far as his effort reaches, and then they judge that what he has reached is true; another strives and they determine that it is false, because had Allah willed it to be of one single form, He would have said so. Rather, He left it open to various opinions.

Thus, Allah, glory be to Him, willed that these opinions exist, because man, just as he is governed by compulsion in many cosmic matters and has choice in some affairs, so too is the case with the obligation (taklif): he is compelled in the fundamentals, from which, if he deviates, the world would be corrupted, and free in other matters, where doing them is valid and leaving them is valid.

The Exalted says in this method:

﴿O you who believe, bow down, prostrate yourselves, worship your Lord, and do good, that you may succeed.﴾ (22:77)

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 77:

﴿O you who have believed, bow, prostrate, worship your Lord, and do good that you may succeed.﴾ (77):

The address in the preceding parable (1) was to people in general, because it wants to draw the worshippers of idols to this parable and make them hear it. Here, however, the discourse concerns a method and a constitution addressed specifically to those who have believed, because one is only charged with its rulings if one has believed in it. As for one who disbelieves, he is not fit to bear this trust, and therefore it has been left to him and it does not organize the movement of his life. As we said regarding the traffic policeman: he helps the one who seeks his help and trusts him, guiding and directing him, whereas one who doubts his words and belittles his authority is left to go astray at the crossroads.

So when your Lord addresses you with what He obligates you to, know that the directive is specific, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, believe...﴾ (136) [An-Nisa'].

Some who take the verses at face value have objected to the style of this verse. They say: how does He address them as "O you who have believed" and then say "believe"? How, when they already believe?

They said: the meaning is, "O you who have believed, before hearing the new ruling, remain upon your faith in the new ruling, and persist in your faith." Therefore, when you ask something of one who is described by it, know that what is meant is persistence in it.

Moreover, there is a difference between believing in a ruling and carrying out the ruling. You may believe that a ruling is from God, without doubting it or objecting to it, yet you do not carry it out and you disobey it. For example, regarding the Hajj, God, exalted is He, says: ﴿And due to God from the people is the pilgrimage to the House...﴾ (97) [Ali 'Imran]. What is due to God from His servants is that they make pilgrimage to the House. ﴿For whoever is able to it a way﴾ (97) [Ali 'Imran]; this is an essential condition, for there is no obligation without capability. Then He says: ﴿And whoever disbelieves﴾ (97) [Ali 'Imran]. Does this mean that whoever does not perform the Hajj is a disbeliever?

They said: No, because the meaning is: "It is a ruling due to God upon people which the believer holds as a belief, that the pilgrimage to the House is due to God from the people. Whoever holds this belief is a believer. As for whether he carries it out or does not carry it out, that is another matter."

Then He begins, first of all, in the obligations, with the matter of prayer: ﴿Bow, prostrate, and worship your Lord...﴾ (77) [Al-Hajj]. The messengers came from God with many obligations, but here prayer is singled out because it is the obligation that recurs five times every day, whereas the rest of the obligations are seasonal: fasting is one month in the whole year, Hajj is once in a lifetime for whoever is able, and zakat is due at the harvest for one who possesses the minimum threshold (nisab) or at the completion of the lunar year.

Thus the obligation of prayer differs from the other obligations, and therefore the Messenger of God (ﷺ) singled it out in his saying: "The covenant between us and them is the prayer; whoever abandons it has disbelieved." (2)

And he said: "Prayer is the pillar of the religion." (3)

The Truth, blessed and exalted is He, singled it out with a special legislative status: prayer was prescribed directly, whereas the other obligations were prescribed through revelation.

We have given an example for this, and to God belongs the highest likeness: we said that the head of a workplace may send you a note saying, "Do such-and-such." If the matter is important, he phones you and informs you of what he wants because of its importance. If the matter is more important than that and comes from a higher authority, he says to you, "Come to me, there is an important matter," and assigns it to you directly. Likewise, according to the degree of importance, there is the mode of legislation.

So prayer did not come through revelation like the other obligations; rather it came directly from the One who revealed, glory be to Him, because it is to be a connection between the servant and his Lord. He willed to purify it even of this intermediary. Then He distinguished it from other obligations, making it the obligation that never falls from the Muslim in any circumstance. You may be poor, so zakat does not bind you; unable, so Hajj does not bind you; sick or traveling, so fasting does not bind you.

But prayer is not dropped from you by any of this. If you are unable to stand, you may pray seated, lying on your side, or lying on your back, indicating your bowing and prostration with your eyes; even if the actions of prayer run only in your heart. The important thing is that you remain mindful of your Lord and connected to Him, such that no time passes over you without Him, glory be to Him, in your mind.

We have said that the remembrance of God in the call to prayer, the iqamah, and the prayer is a constant remembrance at every time that never ceases. When you pray the dawn prayer, for example, someone else prays the noon prayer; when you bow, someone else prostrates; when you say "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate," someone else says "Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds," and so on.

It is therefore a worship that interpenetrates and is permanent, never interrupted. Hence one of the people of knowledge, addressing time, says: "O time, in you is all time." That is, in every part of time is all of time, as if he said: "O noon, in you is the afternoon, in you is the sunset, in you is the night prayer," and so on. The whole world turns in worship of God that never ends.

Among the prayer's components He mentioned bowing and prostration, because they are the most evident actions of prayer. But bowing and prostration are movements performed by the sincere believer and also by the hypocrite, and the hypocrites were the first of people to the front rows. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, wished to distinguish this from that, and He said: ﴿and worship your Lord...﴾ (77) [Al-Hajj].

The value is not in the movements of bowing and prostration; the value lies in directing them toward God and making one's intention in them sincere for God. Otherwise prayer becomes mere movements, no more than athletic exercises, as some like to say: "Prayer contains athletic exercises that move every part of the body." Yes, it is, as you say, exercise, but it is not worship. Worship is that you perform it because God, exalted is He, has commanded you to do it.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿and do good that you may succeed﴾ (77) [Al-Hajj]. "Good" is a general word that includes all the commands of obligation, but it came alongside prayer in a summary manner, because what the obligation cannot be completed without is itself obligatory. So "good," then, is a comprehensive word for everything that the functions of the methods perform of the good of society, because the method came only to organize the movement of life in an organization that cooperates and supports, not one that conflicts. If the matter comes in this form, the whole of society is made happy.

Do not forget that when the method restricts you and constrains your movement, it does so for your own benefit, and you are the beneficiary of the restriction of movement, because your Lord has restricted your movement and constrained you so that you do not inflict evil upon others. At the same time, He has constrained all others from moving with evil toward you. You are one and they are many, so for the sake of restricting your movement He has restricted the movement of all people. Who, then, is the winner in this matter?

The Law said to you: "Do not steal," and you are one; and it said to all people: "Do not steal from him." It said to you: "Lower your gaze from the forbidden things of others," and you are one. And it said to every other person: "Lower your gazes from the forbidden things of so-and-so." Thus every obligation from God to creation returns to your benefit.

So the meaning of ﴿and do good﴾ (77) [Al-Hajj] is: that which never produces corruption at all. As long as movements proceed from one desire, they support and cooperate with one another. But if you have a desire and another has a desire, the desires collide and conflict. "Good" is everything that the legislated methodical obligations command from the Truth, blessed and exalted is He.

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿that you may succeed﴾ (77) [Al-Hajj]. But where will this success be: in this world or in the Hereafter?

Success occurs in this world for whoever establishes God's law, adheres to His method, and does good. Success is the natural fruit of God's method in any society whose members move in the direction of good for themselves and for others: a society that acts by the saying of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself." (4) In such a case you will not see in society competition, repulsion, injustice, or bribery, etc. This is success in the world. Then, in addition to the success of this world, comes the success of the Hereafter.

So do not suppose that the legal obligations are a burden upon you, for they are for your benefit in this world, and by them your worldly life succeeds. Then their reward in the Hereafter will be pure grace from God.

The Prophet (ﷺ) alerted us to this matter when he said: "None of you will enter Paradise by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Not even I, unless God covers me with His mercy." (5) This is because a person does good in this world for his own benefit and the benefit of the world he lives in, and then he receives the reward for it in the Hereafter from God's grace, as He, exalted is He, says: ﴿and He will increase them from His bounty﴾ (173) [An-Nisa'].

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿that you may succeed﴾ (77) [Al-Hajj], we know that "la'alla" (perhaps/that) is a particle of hope, and hope has degrees, some more hopeful than others. For example, when you say, "Perhaps so-and-so will give you," you hope from another and do not guarantee his giving. If you say, "Perhaps I will give you," then the hope is in your hand; this is more hopeful than the previous. Yet you and I are still equal, and perhaps I will give you first. But when you say, "Perhaps God will give you," you have placed your hope in God, which is more hopeful than the previous. If God, exalted, says of Himself, "Perhaps I will give you," this is the strongest and most firm degree of hope, because the promise is from God, and hope in Him, glory be to Him, never disappoints.

1 - He means His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O mankind, a parable is presented, so listen to it...﴾ (73) [Al-Hajj].
2 - Related by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan (2621), and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan (1/231), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Buraydah from his father. al-Tirmidhi said: a hasan sahih gharib hadith.
3 - al-Hafiz al-Iraqi said in his takhrij of the Ihya' (1/147): "al-Bayhaqi related it in al-Shu'ab with a chain he judged weak, from the hadith of Umar." Mulla Ali al-Qari said in al-Asrar al-Marfu'ah (hadith 578): Ibn al-Salah said in Mushkil al-Wasit: it is not known. al-Nawawi said in al-Tanqih: it is munkar and false; but al-Daylami related it from Ali, as mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durar al-Muntathirah (no. 279).
4 - Agreed upon. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (13) and Muslim in his Sahih (45), Kitab al-Iman, from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him).
5 - A hadith agreed upon. Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (6463), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (2816), from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 22, verse 78:

Then Allah, glorified is He, says:

﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. The religion of your father Abraham. He named you "Muslims" before [this] and in this [revelation], that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish prayer, give zakah, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protector; how excellent the Protector and how excellent the Helper!﴾ (78)

The meaning of ﴿with the striving due to Him (78)﴾ [al-Hajj] is like what we said regarding ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure (74)﴾ [al-Hajj], because striving also requires sincerity, and that you keep Allah in mind. A person may go out merely to rid himself of blame, take up arms in deed, and enter the battle, yet in his heart it is not for Allah, and in his heart there is not the raising of the Word of Allah. Such is one who fights for fame and so that people will see his standing, or who fights out of greed for spoils, or because he is enraged at the enemy and has a blood feud with him and wants to take revenge on him. These and other such matters take fighting away from its aim and empty it of its substance.

Therefore, when the Master of the Messengers, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, a man fights for booty, a man fights to be remembered, and a man fights to be seen in his station. Which of them is in the way of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever fights so that the Word of Allah is the highest, he is in the way of Allah" (1). This is the striving due to Him, and you are the judge of yourself in it, for the scale of that is in your hand.

And you may ask: why striving? They said: because when you benefit from the method by applying it after the verification brought by the Messengers, you benefit yourself, but your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, wants the benefit to spread to those with you as well. This cannot be achieved except by striving with the self, or wealth, or anything beloved. Otherwise, how would you gain the transaction of which Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their property in exchange for that they will have Paradise.. (111)﴾ [al-Tawbah].

Just as the soldiers have a task on the battlefield, so too those who sit and do not go out have a task. The soldier who plunges into terrors and dangers and exposes himself to death—this means that he did not enter the battle nor expose himself to killing except while fully certain that what he goes to by being killed is better than what he would obtain by cowardice. This encourages others and urges them to fight.

Therefore, at the Battle of Badr, when a Companion heard the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the reward of the martyr, and there was a date in his mouth that he was sucking, he said: "O Messenger of Allah, is there between me and Paradise only that I be killed in the way of Allah?" He said: "Yes." So he threw the date from his mouth and went out immediately to jihad (2), because he was fully certain that what he would go to by martyrdom was better than what he left behind.

As for those who remained and did not go out, their task is to carry the method and to realize it; for if everyone went out to fight and all were martyred, who would then carry the method of Allah and spread it?

The word jihad came in general terms to include all kinds of jihad. So when jihad bears its fruit and we overcome disbelief, and there are no disbelievers left, or they clear the way of our call and leave us alone and love to live in our lands as dhimmis, then there is no need for fighting, and jihad turns to another field, which is the jihad of the self.

Therefore, after this Allah said: ﴿He has chosen you (78)﴾ [al-Hajj], meaning: He selected you and chose you so that you would be the best nation brought forth for mankind. The price of this choosing is that we should be worthy of it, at the level of its responsibility, and that we fulfil what Allah wanted from us.

We also advise a group of the people of the call who have carried its banner: we say to them, Allah has chosen you, so be worthy of this choice, and place His words in their proper place.

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty (78)﴾ [al-Hajj], meaning: He did not choose you to burden you, or to constrain you, or to make matters difficult for you. Rather, He made the whole matter ease, legislated it according to capacity, and granted you concessions that lighten for you and remove from you hardship and constraint. Whoever cannot stand prays sitting; whoever is ill breaks his fast; and the poor person has no zakah obligation upon him, nor hajj... etc.

As He, glorified is He, said elsewhere: ﴿And if Allah had willed, He could have put you in difficulty (220)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. But He, glorified is He, did not put you in difficulty nor constrain you, and He did not obligate you except with what you are able to carry out.

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿The religion of your father Abraham (78)﴾ [al-Hajj]. The word "millah" came thus in the accusative, because it is the object of a verb whose implied form is "adhere to" (ilzamu): the religion of your father Abraham, because you are the answer to his supplication when he said: ﴿Our Lord, and make us Muslims [in submission] to You and from our descendants a Muslim nation to You. And show us our rites and accept our repentance...(128)﴾ [al-Baqarah].

And from the supplication of Abraham, peace be upon him: ﴿Our Lord, and send among them a messenger from themselves...(129)﴾ [al-Baqarah]. Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "I am the answer to the supplication of my father Abraham, and the glad tidings of Jesus" (3).

That is: from his offspring and the offspring of his son Isma'il. ﴿And show us our rites (128)﴾ [al-Baqarah]: give us the obligations, as though he were eager for the obligations of Allah. Does a person long for an obligation if it involves constraint or hardship?

Likewise the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) were in love with the obligations of Islam and would ask the Messenger of Allah about them, despite his saying to them: "Leave me as I have left you" (4). Nevertheless, they would ask about matters of religion in order to build their new lives, not on what the Jahiliyyah used to do, but on what Islam commanded.

We have a note on His saying: ﴿The religion of your father Abraham (78)﴾ [al-Hajj]. The address here is to the nation of the call and the nation of response. Is the entire Muslim nation from the descendants of Abraham, so that it says: ﴿The religion of your father Abraham (78)﴾?

We say: Islam is a doctrinal submission for all, and within the Muslim nation there are those who are not from the descendants of Abraham. But Abraham, peace be upon him, is the father of the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ), and the Messenger is a father to everyone who believes in him, because the fatherhood of the Messenger is a fatherhood of action and following, as came in the saying of Allah, the Exalted, in the story of Noah about his son: ﴿Indeed, he is not of your family (46)﴾ [Hud].

Since the Prophet (ﷺ) was a father to everyone who believed in him, Allah named his wives "mothers of the believers," and He, glorified is He, said: ﴿The Prophet is more worthy of the believers than themselves, and his wives are their mothers (6)﴾ [al-Ahzab].

And since the wives are mothers, the husband is a father; and on the basis of this relation, Abraham, peace be upon him, is a father to the Muslim nation, even if among them are some who are not of his lineage.

Some who like to object to the words of Allah say, regarding the fatherhood of the Messenger to his nation: "But the Qur'an said otherwise. It said in the story of Zayd ibn Harithah: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men (40)﴾ [al-Ahzab]," so He negated that Muhammad is the father of anyone, and this contradicts your statement.

We say: If you understood from Allah what you would not object to His words. Allah says: Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men, but he is a father to all. What is negated is that the Messenger of Allah be a father to a single individual, not that he be a father to his entire nation. Then He said after it: ﴿But he is the Messenger of Allah (40)﴾ [al-Ahzab], and since he is the Messenger of Allah, he is a father to all.

Then He, the Exalted, says about Abraham, peace be upon him: ﴿He named you "Muslims" before (78)﴾ [al-Hajj], meaning: Abraham, peace be upon him, named you Muslims, as though this were a clear matter and a known affair, that you have been Muslims since Abraham, peace be upon him: ﴿And in this [revelation], that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people (78)﴾ [al-Hajj].

In another place the order is reversed, and He, glorified is He, says: ﴿That you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger may be a witness over you (143)﴾ [al-Baqarah].

Why? They said: because the Messenger of Allah conveyed the message of Allah, and he called Allah to witness that when he said: "O Allah, I have conveyed; O Allah, bear witness." Bear witness that I have conveyed. He (ﷺ) wants from his nation that each person in it be a bearer of this message and a conveyer of it, until whoever did not attend and did not see him hears the words of the Messenger. Thus the Messenger is a witness over whoever believed in him, and whoever believed is a witness over whoever has reached him.

Therefore, among the honors of the nation of Muhammad is, first, that no messenger comes after him, because they are entrusted with the method of Allah, and it is as though goodness never dies out among them. We have said that messengers come only after corruption has spread, and people lose the natural immunity that restrains them from evil, and society as a whole loses it so that no one forbids anyone from evil. Then Allah, glorified is He, intervenes with a messenger and a new miracle to set right what has been corrupted.

Thus the sealing of the messages with Muhammad (ﷺ) is a testimony that goodness will never cease from his nation, and however much people deviate, there will remain a group upon the right path, carrying the method, holding fast to it, and serving as an example for others. Therefore the Messenger of Allah defined this matter when he said: "The good is in my elite, and scattered among my nation." So all goodness and all perfection are in the person of the Messenger of Allah, and scattered throughout his nation.

Then the context returns to the command of prayer: ﴿So establish prayer and give zakah (78)﴾ [al-Hajj], because it is the obligation that accompanies the believer, and in it is the raising of devotion repeated five times a day, and through it the remembrance of Allah continues across all time, never ceasing for a moment of time, when you look at the whole world and join some of it to others.

Whoever reflects on time with respect to the Real, blessed and exalted is He, finds it never ceasing. Today, for example, for us is twenty-four hours, while a day with Allah is a thousand years of what you count (Q. 22:47), and a day on the Day of Resurrection is fifty thousand years (Q. 70:4). There is also a day called "the day of now," that is, the moment we are in, and it is the Day of Allah about which He said: ﴿Every day He is in a matter (29)﴾ [al-Rahman]. Therefore it is said: "What has your Lord been occupied with now, when it is established that the pen has dried?" He said: "Matters which He brings into being and does not initiate; He raises peoples and lowers others" (6).

So the day of "now" is the day of 'Ad: it is neither the day of Egypt, nor the day of Syria, nor the day of Japan. In every moment a day begins for Allah and a day ends, so His day is continuous and never ceases.

And we read in the noble Prophetic hadith: "Indeed, Allah stretches out His hand by night so that the one who sinned by day may repent, and He stretches out His hand by day so that the one who sinned by night may repent" (7).

Whose day? And whose night? Day and night in time are constant and never cease, and at every moment of time a day ends and a day begins, and a night ends and a night begins. Thus Allah's hand is always outstretched and He never withdraws it, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Rather, both His hands are outspread; He spends however He wills (64)﴾ [al-Ma'idah].

Then He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And hold fast to Allah (78)﴾ [al-Hajj]: take refuge in Him in hardships. This means that you will be confronted and persecuted, for no bearer of the method of Allah is spared persecution. Let this not affect you or weaken your resolve, and make Allah your refuge and stronghold in every calamity that overtakes you, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿There is no protector today from the decree of Allah, except for whom He has mercy (43)﴾ [Hud].

Your holding fast to Allah is not something you bring about by yourselves; rather ﴿He is your Protector (78)﴾ [al-Hajj], meaning: the one who takes charge of your affairs. And since He, glorified is He, is your Protector, ﴿how excellent the Protector and how excellent the Helper! (78)﴾ [al-Hajj].

1 - Agreed upon (Muttafaq 'alayh). Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (123), and Muslim in his Sahih (1904), from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.
2 - From Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: a man said, "Where am I if I am killed?" He said: "In Paradise." So he threw away some dates that were in his hand, then fought until he was killed. In the hadith of Suwayd: a man said to the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud. Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (4046), and likewise Muslim in his Sahih (1899), Kitab al-Imarah. Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (7/354): "I have not found the name of the man. Ibn Bashkuwal claimed that he was 'Umayr ibn al-Hammam, and al-Khatib preceded him in this, citing what Muslim recorded from the hadith of Anas. I say: but it is explicitly stated in the hadith of Anas that this was on the day of Badr."
3 - Abu Umamah said: I said, "O Prophet of Allah, what was the beginning of your affair?" He said: "The supplication of my father Abraham, and the glad tidings of Jesus, and my mother saw that a light came forth from them by which the palaces of Syria were illuminated." Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/262).
4 - Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/247) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "Leave me as I have left you, for those before you were destroyed by their excessive questioning and their disputing with their prophets. What I forbid you, abstain from; and what I command you, do of it as much as you are able."
5 - Recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (1739) in the Farewell Sermon, from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he (ﷺ) said: "Indeed your blood, your property, and your honor are sacred to you, like the sanctity of this day of yours, in this land of yours, in this month of yours."
6 - From Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying: ﴿Every day He is in a matter (29)﴾ [al-Rahman], he said: "Among His matters is that He forgives a sin, relieves a distress, raises a people, and lowers others." Recorded by Ibn Abi 'Asim in al-Sunnah (1/129), Ibn Majah in his Sunan (202), Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah (5/252), and Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azamah (no. 150).
7 - Recorded by Ahmad in his Musnad (4/395, 404) and Muslim in his Sahih (2759) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.
